title: Listo Pairing Ledger
lede: Every subclass in the modlist swept, every split it can express searched, and 298 bodies scored on ten axes across three acts, then paired with every other. v6 rebuilds the two damage axes: single-target and AoE are no longer judged against a checklist of features but computed as a ratio to a per-act par that carries the run's enemy-HP inflation, with every resource amortised over three hard fights of four rounds. That change alone re-ranks the field — a flat rider now visibly decays, Improved Extra Attack turns out to only just outpace the HP curve, and a body that stops one level short of its die step pays for it.
footer: Built 21 August 2026 against the installed Listonomicon 10.2 paks. 157 subclasses swept by four agents, 149 promoted, 1,073,626 raw splits enumerated and culled to 88,987 on the frontier, 298 variants scored by eleven agents, 44,253 pairings computed. Saves and Skills derived from evidence rather than judged; single-target and AoE computed as ratios to par. Chassis ids resolved centrally by naming.py after scoring.

Nullify.note: A Cleric that holds Counterspell natively and spends its reactions on the enemy caster instead of on itself; it gives up armour, martial weapons and any real weapon routine to do it.
Nullify.strength: In a duo there is no wizard to hold the counter-reaction, and Lone Wolf's second reaction means Nullify can counter and still Warding-Flare-equivalent or opportunity-attack in the same round; Arcane Abjuration also banishes off a short-rest Channel Divinity charge rather than a slot.
Nullify.wants: A body that carries the pair's crowd damage, because this one has no area engine at all and sits at 1 on AoE in every act.
uncertain: Swapped the search's College of Stormcalling for College of Lore — Stormcalling is outside my read set and I cannot price it; Lore is named in the Bard dip section and its Expertise is what carries the skills row.
Arcane Abjuration's banishment is scored low because it only reaches celestial/elemental/fey/fiend targets; the level threshold at Cleric 14 is CR 3, below boss grade.

Cipher.split: Barbarian 1 (none) / Cleric 14 (Arcana) / Monk 5 (Way of the Friar)
Cipher.note: The same Counterspell chassis rebuilt unarmoured — Barbarian 1 for Str/Con saves and a d12 hit die, Monk 5 for Extra Attack, Stunning Strike and a ki pool; Rage is dead weight because a raging body cannot cast.
Cipher.strength: Friar's bond puts a d4 on both bodies' saves and a per-turn temp-HP tap on the partner, and the short-rest ki pool is the resource shape a 120-supply long rest actually rewards.
Cipher.wants: A body that can talk — this one is at zero Persuasion in every act and cannot clear routine town dialogue.
uncertain: friars-blessing assumed live at Monk 5; the Monk dip section names Way of the Friar's bond but not the level it lands, which is outside my read range.
Level order assumed Barbarian 1 → Cleric 2–9 through Act I → Monk in Act II, so the Monk block scores from Act II on.

Reaper.note: A martial-weapon Cleric whose cantrips hit two creatures apiece and whose Channel Divinity converts a corpse into a third body; it has no heavy armour and its whole damage output is necrotic.
Reaper.strength: Control Undead buys the one thing a two-person party is structurally short of — a third initiative slot — and Reaper's cantrip doubling means the Lone Wolf second Action is two extra targets, not one.
Reaper.wants: A second damage type: necrotic is resisted across Act III's undead, and this body caps out on a single school.
uncertain: Swapped College of Stormcalling for College of Swords — the Duelling style is what keeps this body's single-target row at par, and Stormcalling is outside my read set.
AoE scored on Spirit Guardians holding the concentration slot, with a halving applied from Act II for necrotic resistance.

Cortege.note: The Death domain opened on Fighter for Str/Con saves, heavy armour and a Fighting Style, then run as a weapon-and-cantrip body; it trades the Cleric's Wis/Cha save pair for armour it otherwise could not wear.
Cortege.strength: Fighter 1 is the cheapest heavy armour in the run and it returns two armour feats, so the whole feat budget goes to Wisdom and durability while Control Undead still buys a third body.
Cortege.wants: A body with a real area engine and a second damage type; this one is necrotic-locked and its crowd answer is one concentration spell.
uncertain: Fighter 1's heavy armour is credited per the Fighter dip section (level-1 node only); the Death domain grants none.

Torpor.split: Barbarian 1 (none) / Cleric 14 (Dream) / Monk 5 (Way of the Friar)
Torpor.note: A lockdown Cleric: Deep Slumber leaves Torpor behind, which strips a creature to one of attack/action/bonus action with no reactions, and Mind Sliver taxes the next save on top. It gives up armour and almost all damage.
Torpor.strength: Torpor is the mirror image of Lone Wolf — it takes an enemy's action suite down to one while the duo keeps six — and Deep Slumber costs no concentration, so the pair's two slots stay free.
Torpor.wants: A body that removes enemy hit points; Torpor buys rounds and cashes none of them in itself.
uncertain: Inception is scored as a rung-3 rider rather than rung-4 no-concentration control: it consumes the Channel Divinity charge and only taxes the first save.
friars-blessing assumed live at Monk 5; the level is not stated in the dip section I read.

Somnus.note: The Dream domain in armour — Fighter 1 for Str/Con saves, heavy armour and a Fighting Style, Bard 5 for Song of Rest, Expertise and a short-rest Inspiration clock; the trade is the Cleric's own Wis/Cha save pair.
Somnus.strength: It is the rare controller that survives being reached: heavy armour plus four disjoint saves under Listo's inflated boss DCs, holding Hypnotic Pattern while Deep Slumber and Mind Sliver run off the non-concentration side.
Somnus.wants: A body that converts held enemies into corpses; this one is at par on single-target and has no crowd damage.
uncertain: Expertise placed on Perception and Persuasion; Investigation stays at bare proficiency because this body dumps Intelligence.

Prophecy.split: Fighter 1 (none) / Cleric 14 (Eldritch) / Warlock 5 (The Great Old One)
Prophecy.note: A crowd-lockdown Cleric: Prophecy of Doom drops a random Eldritch Effect on everything in a 5m sphere off a short-rest charge, and Eldritch Contagion re-applies one as a bonus action forever. It buys none of that with concentration, and almost none of it is reliable for a specific plan.
Prophecy.strength: Two Channel Divinity charges refunded by every short rest is exactly the resource shape a 120-supply long rest rewards, and 'can move or act, not both, and no reactions' is an action-economy tax that mirrors what Lone Wolf hands the duo.
Prophecy.wants: A body that can hold the pair's one concentration spell and finish the enemies this one merely disables.
uncertain: Warlock patron is outside my read set; The Great Old One is chosen for fit, and only the boon (Pact of the Chain, named as the duo pick) and Beguiling Influence's Persuasion are actually scored.
Eldritch Contagion and Prophecy of Doom deliver from a random effect table, so the control rows are the expected value of that table rather than a chosen effect.

Contagion.split: Barbarian 1 (none) / Cleric 14 (Eldritch) / Monk 5 (Way of the Friar)
Contagion.note: The same Eldritch control engine on an unarmoured monk frame — Extra Attack, Stunning Strike and a ki pool bolted to a domain whose whole output is bonus-action and Channel-Divinity driven. It has no armour and no crowd damage.
Contagion.strength: Everything this body does runs off bonus actions and reactions, and Lone Wolf doubles both — Contagion re-applies an Eldritch Effect and Stuns in the same turn without touching its Action.
Contagion.wants: A body that removes enemy hit points and one that can carry the party's dialogue, since this one rolls flat zero on Persuasion.
uncertain: friars-blessing assumed live at Monk 5.
Eldritch's free re-selectable skill proficiency is not credited to Perception/Investigation/Persuasion because it competes with the domain's own utility picks each long rest.

Forge.note: The most durable Cleric on the list — heavy armour, a permanent +1 AC blessing, another +1 from Soul of the Forge and fire resistance on top — built as a Spirit Guardians platform. At Cleric 14 it never reaches Saint of Forge and Fire, so the physical resistance capstone is out of reach.
Forge.strength: With no taunt in the game, the pair is only as tough as its softer half, and Anvil is the half that never is; the Artisan's Blessing reaction also lets the partner punch through the physical resistances Absolute Wrath layers on.
Forge.wants: A body that answers bosses — this one has no single-target control above par and its damage decays across the acts.
uncertain: Swapped College of Stormcalling for College of Swords; Stormcalling is outside my read set.
Act III durability drops a rung because Forge's mitigation below the level-17 capstone is flat and narrow, and the act is boss-weighted.

Bellows.split: Cleric 11 (Forge) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Great Old One)
Bellows.note: Forge shortened to eleven levels to buy Lore's Expertise and a Pact of the Chain familiar; it keeps the armour and the +1 AC layers but loses Divine Strike's 2d8 upgrade and the 7th-tier domain pair.
Bellows.strength: The familiar is a permanent third initiative slot in a two-body party, and the pact slots come back on every short rest — both are things the duo's long-rest economy cannot otherwise buy.
Bellows.wants: A body that carries boss damage; Bellows is a durable platform with a decaying weapon routine and no single-target answer.
uncertain: Warlock patron outside my read set; only Pact of the Chain and the short-rest pact slots are scored.
Act III Actions falls to 1 because a single familiar is par at best by then per the rubric's act table.

Sentinel.note: A Cleric built around Sentinel at Death's Door — a reaction that turns a critical hit on either body into a normal hit — plus Path to the Grave's vulnerability window and the domain's own Revivify and Death Ward. It has no heavy armour and no weapon routine worth the name.
Sentinel.strength: Enemy Critical Hits are on and the pair's failure mode is one body eating a crit and dropping; this deletes that outcome several times per long rest using the reaction Lone Wolf gives away spare, and Path to the Grave doubles the partner's biggest single swing.
Sentinel.wants: A body with a large single hit to spend on Path to the Grave, and one that can wear armour, because this one cannot.
uncertain: Swapped College of Stormcalling for College of Lore; Stormcalling is outside my read set.
Sentinel at Death's Door is scored as outward prevention on the Rescue axis and as one mitigation layer on Durability, never both at full value.

Cairn.note: Grave opened on Fighter so it can wear the heavy armour the domain refuses to grant, at the cost of the Cleric's Wis/Cha save pair; Bard 5 adds Song of Rest and a short-rest Inspiration clock.
Cairn.strength: The crit-cancelling reaction plus armour means the softer half of the duo is genuinely hard to spike down, which matters more here than anywhere because the pair value on Durability is a minimum, not an average.
Cairn.wants: A crowd-clear engine; Cairn's only area answer is the one concentration spell it already holds.

Witchhunter.note: A heavy-armour, martial-weapon Cleric whose rider is force damage and whose Channel Divinity hands the partner temp HP plus resistance to spell damage and advantage on saves against spells. Witch Hunter's Strike does not stack with the Divine Strike interrupt, so one swing carries one rider.
Witchhunter.strength: Force is the least-resisted type in the list against Absolute Wrath's layers, and one Spell Shield charge covers fifty percent of this party rather than twenty-five; Rebuke Invoker gives Lone Wolf's spare reaction something to do every enemy cast.
Witchhunter.wants: An area engine — the domain's whole kit is single-target and reactive, and its crowd row rests entirely on the one concentration spell.
uncertain: Swapped College of Stormcalling for College of Swords; Stormcalling is outside my read set.
Spell Shield is scored as rung-4 outward prevention; it is a bonus action rather than no-action, which is why Act III sits at 3.

Tribunal.split: Cleric 11 (Inquisition) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Great Old One)
Tribunal.note: Inquisition cut to eleven levels for Lore Expertise and a Pact of the Chain familiar; it keeps the armour, Spell Shield and Rebuke Invoker but loses Witch Hunter's Strike's 2d8/3d8 upgrade and the 7th-tier domain pair.
Tribunal.strength: It is the pair's anti-caster body and its skills body at once — Spell Shield covers half the party on one short-rest charge while Lore's Expertise carries the untelegraphed Perception and Persuasion load neither Cleric nor Fighter can.
Tribunal.wants: A body that clears crowds; Tribunal's every lever points at one enemy caster at a time.
uncertain: Warlock patron outside my read set; only the Chain boon and short-rest pact slots are scored.

Archive.note: The skills body of the batch — Lore's three proficiencies and Expertise stacked on a Wisdom primary, with Magical Secrets at Cleric 6 and 10 filling the domain's damage hole with Counterspell and Hypnotic Pattern. It has light armour, no weapon routine and no area damage.
Archive.strength: Two characters have to clear every check in the campaign, and this is the only body in the batch that puts a real Perception number in front of Listo's unannounced DC 15–25 traps while still holding the pair's crowd-control spell.
Archive.wants: Damage of any kind — Archive is at 1 on AoE and 2 on single-target in every act, so the partner has to be the entire kill clock.
uncertain: Swapped College of Stormcalling for College of Lore; Stormcalling is outside my read set and Lore is the whole point of this chassis.
Knowledge's own double proficiency lands on Arcana/History/Nature/Religion, none of which the Skills axis reads any more, so it contributes nothing here.
Magical Secrets pick count at Cleric 6 and 10 is flagged unverified in the class file; I assumed two useful spells total, not a full Bard-grade selection.

Palimpsest.split: Barbarian 1 (none) / Cleric 14 (Knowledge) / Monk 5 (Way of the Friar)
Palimpsest.note: Knowledge without the Bard, so without the Expertise that made it a skills body — what is left is Magical Secrets, a monk frame with Extra Attack and Stunning Strike, and Barbarian 1's Str/Con saves.
Palimpsest.strength: Friar's bond puts a d4 on every save both bodies make and a per-turn temp-HP tap on the partner, and Stunning Strike off a short-rest ki pool is control that costs neither a slot nor the pair's concentration.
Palimpsest.wants: A face — this body rolls zero Persuasion in every act and its Investigation is untrained, so the partner has to carry both.
uncertain: friars-blessing assumed live at Monk 5.
Stunning Strike is credited on Control (single) as a no-slot rider rather than as hard control, since Listo's enemies get a Con save that scales.

Mercy.note: Heavy armour and the strongest sustain in the domain list — Disciple of Life on every heal from any source, Preserve Life, Revivify, Death Ward and Heal — stopping one level short of Supreme Healing, which lives at Cleric 17.
Mercy.strength: Healing potions are nerfed and Short Rest Full Heal is off, so out-of-combat healing is the only cheap route between fights, and Lone Wolf's halved damage doubles the value of every point restored; keeping the softer body up is also the only way to move the pair's Durability minimum.
Mercy.wants: A body that removes enemy action points — Mercy restores its own side's and does almost nothing to the other's.
uncertain: Swapped College of Stormcalling for College of Lore; Stormcalling is outside my read set.
Blessed Healer is not scored outward — Goon's fix makes it heal only the caster, which is Durability, and it is too small to move that rung.

Vigil.split: Cleric 11 (Life) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Great Old One)
Vigil.note: Life shortened to eleven levels — it keeps heavy armour, Disciple of Life, Preserve Life and Death Ward but loses 6th-tier Heal and Divine Strike's upgrade, buying Lore Expertise and a Chain familiar instead.
Vigil.strength: A permanent third body on the initiative order plus pact slots that refresh every short rest is the cheapest way this pair escapes the two-actions-and-a-long-rest economy, and the healing still doubles under Lone Wolf's halving.
Vigil.wants: A kill clock; Vigil's damage rows fall across the acts and it has no answer to a boss beyond Hold Person.
uncertain: Warlock patron outside my read set; only the Chain boon and short-rest pact slots are scored.

Flare.split: Cleric 11 (Light) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Great Old One)
Flare.note: The area-damage Cleric — Radiance of the Dawn twice per short rest on top of an upcast Fireball, with Warding Flare imposing disadvantage on attackers as a reaction. Cut to Cleric 11 it never reaches Corona of Light and keeps only 6th-tier slots.
Flare.strength: Lone Wolf's spare reaction means Flare can impose disadvantage twice a round without giving up an opportunity attack, and its two damage types — fire and radiant — sidestep the single-school trap Absolute Wrath sets for every other burst caster.
Flare.wants: A body that can take a hit and hold a line; Flare is in medium armour and its whole defence is a reaction it can be baited out of.
uncertain: Warlock patron outside my read set.
Durability rung 3 credits double Warding Flare as roughly equivalent to heavy armour plus shield; the rubric's table only names armour categories, so this is a judgement call.
Act III AoE falls to 3 because Cleric 11 caps the Fireball upcast at 6th tier.

Corona.note: Light run to fourteen for the full Radiance and a 7th-tier upcast Fireball, opened on Barbarian for Str/Con saves and a d12 hit die; Rage is unusable on a casting body and is not scored.
Corona.strength: Two Channel Divinity charges refunded by every short rest plus one slot is a repeatable crowd answer that never touches the pair's two concentration slots, which is what lets the partner hold Hold Monster all fight.
Corona.wants: A front line — Corona's Durability is the pair's likely minimum and it has nothing to stop a melee body reaching it.
uncertain: Barbarian 1's Rage is scored at zero: a raging body cannot cast, so this chassis buys only the d12 die, Str/Con saves and shields from that level.

Bramble.note: A Wisdom melee cleric that swings Shillelagh off its own domain list and holds Spirit Guardians all fight; the Bard block buys Song of Rest, short-rest Inspiration and late Expertise. It gives up any real single-target engine — two attacks a round and one Divine Strike is well under par at every act.
Bramble.strength: Nature is the only domain that hands a Wisdom body a weapon without a feat tax, so the whole 22 goes into one stat that drives attacks, spell DC and the AC of heavy armour it already has — and Spirit Guardians is at-will area damage that costs nothing per round against Listo's inflated crowd counts.
Bramble.wants: A partner that can actually kill a boss, because this body's single-target row never clears par and its concentration is already spent.
uncertain: College of Stormcalling's own features were outside the read set; the Bard 6 block is scored on the shared class features only (Jack of All Trades, Song of Rest, Font of Inspiration, Expertise ×2).
Assumes the Bard block is taken last, so its Expertise only lands in Act III.

Verdance.split: Cleric 11 (Nature) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend)
Verdance.note: The Nature chassis rebuilt as a back-line body: eleven Cleric levels for Spirit Guardians, Death Ward and Greater Restoration, Lore for skill coverage, and a Warlock 3 tail for Eldritch Blast, Repelling Blast and a Chain familiar. It gives up Divine Strike 2d8 and the domain capstone entirely.
Verdance.strength: Three of its four best pieces — Repelling Blast, the familiar and the pact slots — cost no concentration and no long-rest slot, which is exactly what a duo that already spends both its concentration slots needs; and the familiar is a third initiative entry in a two-body party.
Verdance.wants: A body that can hold a hard single-target lock, because this one's boss answer never rises above Hold Person off a long-rest slot.
uncertain: Feat count read off Listo's class-level cadence (6); the character-level 3/6/9/12/13/15/18 reading gives 7.
Warlock patron picked as The Fiend for Dark One's Blessing; the patron list was outside the read set.
Eldritch Blast rides Charisma, which this body dumps, so the beams are scored at a +1 modifier.

Gloaming.note: Night domain wearing the heavy armour and shield its own domain does not grant, bought with a single opening Fighter level that also pays for Str + Con saves and a Fighting Style. It gives up Action Surge — the Fighter level stops at one.
Gloaming.strength: Ward of Shadows is a reaction that imposes disadvantage on an attack, and Lone Wolf hands every body two reactions, so this chassis can blank two attacks a round for free — proportional mitigation that does not decay against +126% HP the way a flat rider does.
Gloaming.wants: A body that removes bosses permanently, since everything this one does to a single target is temporary and its damage row sits at 1 in every act.
uncertain: Feat count read off Listo's class-level cadence (6); the character-level reading gives 7.
Ward of Shadows is scored as unlimited and reaction-gated; the class text names no per-rest cap but does not state one is absent.
No Persuasion proficiency is reachable before the Bard block, so Acts I and II record a bare Charisma modifier.

Eclipse.split: Cleric 11 (Night) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend)
Eclipse.note: The pure controller reading of Night: Invocation of Night off a short-rest Channel Divinity charge, blinding everything in 9m for Cleric-level rounds, with Repelling Blast layered under it. It gives up armour, Divine Strike and the domain capstone.
Eclipse.strength: Its two best area answers — Invocation of Night and Repelling Blast — both cost zero concentration, so they stack on top of whatever spell the partner is holding rather than competing for the duo's two slots.
Eclipse.wants: A durable front body, because this one is in medium armour with no redirection and dies first to anything that reaches it.
uncertain: Feat count read off Listo's class-level cadence (6); the character-level reading gives 7.
Warlock patron picked as The Fiend; the patron list was outside the read set.
Invocation of Night's blind is scored as area control on a short-rest clock; whether Listo's enemies commonly resist Blinded is not established in the read set.

Decree.note: Order built as the duo's action-economy engine: every levelled spell aimed at the partner buys them a free weapon attack, and Embodiment of the Law casts an enchantment as a bonus action. It gives up damage entirely — two attacks and a Divine Strike is a rung-1 single-target row.
Decree.strength: Voice of Authority pays out once per ally-targeting cast and the party has exactly one ally, so it never misfires; in a two-body party every heal and every buff is also a free attack, which is the structural repair for the one problem a duo actually has.
Decree.wants: A partner with a weapon routine worth triggering — the free reaction attack is worth what the other body's attack is worth, and nothing beside a caster.
uncertain: College of Stormcalling's own features were outside the read set; the Bard 6 block is scored on shared class features only.
Voice of Authority costs a slot every time it fires, so the Actions rung assumes the ~7 slots a fight can spend, not one per round indefinitely.

Precept.split: Barbarian 1 (none) / Cleric 14 (Order) / Monk 5 (Way of the Friar)
Precept.note: Order's free-attack engine on an unarmoured monk frame — Barbarian 1 for Str + Con saves and a d12 die, Monk 5 for the Extra Attack the domain does not have. It gives up the heavy armour Order grants, because Martial Arts and Flurry both require going without it.
Precept.strength: Lone Wolf's second bonus action doubles Flurry of Blows while Voice of Authority hands the partner a reaction attack every time this body casts, so a single round can put four attacks on the board from two characters without either spending an Action on damage.
Precept.wants: A body that can soak, since this one trades armour for unarmoured AC and has no redirection to move the damage anywhere.
uncertain: Feat count read off Listo's class-level cadence (6); the character-level reading gives 7.
The level at which Way of the Friar's +1d4 blessing lands is not stated in the read set; it is authored as Act III only, on the assumption the Monk block is taken last.
Order's heavy armour proficiency is unused on this build and is not scored.

Concord.note: The rescue chassis: Emboldening Bond, Protective Bond, Balm of Peace, Revivify and Death Ward, with a Friar monk tail for per-turn temporary HP on both bodies. It gives up armour, damage and area control — its single-target and area rows are both at the floor.
Concord.strength: Both of its blanket save effects are pair-scope and the party is two people, so Emboldening Bond and the Friar blessing cover the whole party with no bodies left out — and Protective Bond lets the tougher half eat the hit that would otherwise drop the softer one, which is the only thing that argues with a Personal-kind minimum.
Concord.wants: A body that carries the pair's entire kill rate, because this one contributes almost none of it.
uncertain: Expansive Bond is Cleric 17 and is out of reach at Cleric 14, so the Act III redirect stays at tier 1.
The level at which Way of the Friar's +1d4 blessing lands is not stated in the read set; authored as Act III only.

Armistice.note: Peace as a full caster rather than a monk frame — Emboldening Bond and the bond chain kept, with the Bard block buying Song of Rest, short-rest Inspiration and late Expertise instead of temporary HP. It gives up heavy armour, which Peace never grants, and every point of damage above the floor.
Armistice.strength: Emboldening Bond is a permanent d4 on every attack, check and save for both characters at once, which in a two-body party is the whole party — and Lone Wolf's halved damage doubles the value of every point of outward healing this body puts back.
Armistice.wants: A body that holds the pair's kill rate and its area control, because this one holds neither and is spending its own concentration on Spirit Guardians.
uncertain: College of Stormcalling's own features were outside the read set; the Bard 6 block is scored on shared class features only.
Expansive Bond is Cleric 17 and out of reach at Cleric 14, so the Act III redirect stays at tier 1.

Colossus.note: A heavy-armour Strength-domain body whose plan is Haste on the partner and Heavy Armour Master on itself, with Avatar of Battle for a damage rider and physical resistance. It gives up Spirit Guardians — the concentration slot is spent on Haste — so its area row sits at the floor.
Colossus.strength: Strength is the only Cleric domain with Haste on its own list, and handing a second Action to the other half of a two-body party is worth more than anything this chassis could do with the slot itself; Heavy Armour Master's flat reduction lands on top of Lone Wolf's halving against Listo's added small enemies.
Colossus.wants: A partner whose turn is worth doubling — Haste on a low-output body wastes the whole plan — and a body that can cover crowds, because this one has no area answer.
uncertain: Feat count read off Listo's class-level cadence (6); the character-level reading gives 7.
Durability falls to 3 in Act III because Heavy Armour Master is flat-only mitigation in a boss-weighted act, per the rubric's flat-versus-proportional rule.
Whether Rhonas' level-1 druid cantrip can still pick Shillelagh is flagged unverified in the class text; the build does not rely on it.

Sinew.split: Barbarian 1 (none) / Cleric 14 (Strength (Rhonas)) / Monk 5 (Way of the Friar)
Sinew.note: Strength domain rebuilt unarmoured: Barbarian 1 for Str + Con saves and Rage's physical resistance, Monk 5 for the Extra Attack and Flurry the domain lacks, Haste held on the partner. It gives up the domain's heavy armour, which Martial Arts forbids, and all area coverage.
Sinew.strength: It is the only chassis in this batch that both hands the partner a second Action and swings a real attack routine of its own — four unarmed strikes plus Flurry off Lone Wolf's two bonus actions — so the pair gets two upgraded turns from one concentration slot.
Sinew.wants: Crowd clear, because both its damage and its control are aimed at one target at a time.
uncertain: Feat count read off Listo's class-level cadence (6); the character-level reading gives 7.
The level at which Way of the Friar's +1d4 blessing lands is not stated in the read set; authored as Act III only.
Nothing on this chassis is proficient in Persuasion in any act; the recorded modifier is a bare Charisma score.

TempestCleric.note: Destructive Wrath used as an area engine — maximised Shatter twice a fight off a short-rest Channel Divinity pool, under a Spirit Guardians aura — in heavy armour with Heavy Armour Master. It gives up single-target output; two attacks and one Divine Strike is well under par.
TempestCleric.strength: Channel Divinity refills on a short rest, so the maximised burst is available in every one of the three hard fights a long-rest cycle contains, which is the resource shape a 120-supply long rest actually rewards; and the aura and the burst stack because only one of them holds concentration.
TempestCleric.wants: A boss answer — hard single-target control or real single-target damage — since everything this body does well is spread across four targets.
uncertain: Feat count read off Listo's class-level cadence (6); the character-level reading gives 7.

The AoE ratio uses maximised Shatter at four targets twice a fight plus Spirit Guardians, following the rubric's Consuming Fervor worked anchor; Tempest has no Fireball on its list, so the burst is roughly half Zeal's per slot.

Heavy armour comes from the Tempest domain at Cleric 1, not from the level-1 Barbarian, so Heavy Armour Master is affordable but sits outside the rubric's literal 'level-1 class grants heavy armour' clause.

Thunderhead.split: Cleric 11 (Tempest) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend)
Thunderhead.note: The same maximised-thunder engine at Cleric 11, traded down for Lore skill coverage, a Chain familiar and Repelling Blast. It gives up Divine Strike 2d8 and the deeper slot table, so the burst is smaller and the single-target row is a flat zero for two acts.
Thunderhead.strength: Its whole kit sits off the long-rest clock — Channel Divinity, pact slots and Repelling Blast all refill on a short rest or cost nothing at all — which is the difference between three hard fights and two when a long rest costs 120 supplies.
Thunderhead.wants: A durable body to stand in front, because this one has no redirection, no self-healing and dies to anything that closes.
uncertain: Feat count read off Listo's class-level cadence (6); the character-level reading gives 7.
Warlock patron picked as The Fiend; the patron list was outside the read set.
Thunder and lightning are commonly resisted under Absolute Wrath; the AoE ratio does not apply the 0.5 resistance multiplier because Spirit Guardians supplies a second damage type.

Mirage.note: The weakest of the vanilla domains carried by the base Cleric kit — Invoke Duplicity as a decoy, Spirit Guardians as the damage, and the full rescue list underneath. It gives up armour, damage and the Improved Duplicity capstone, which is Cleric 17 and out of reach at 14.
Mirage.strength: The duplicate is a third body on a two-body board, and Listo's enemy AI selects by softness rather than by taunt, so a decoy that draws attacks off the pair's weaker half is doing work the model's Personal-kind minimum would otherwise punish.
Mirage.wants: Almost everything offensive — this body's job is Death Ward, Revivify and Spirit Guardians, and its partner has to be the fight.
uncertain: College of Stormcalling's own features were outside the read set; the Bard 6 block is scored on shared class features only.

Invoke Duplicity is scored as one extra body on a short-rest clock, falling to rung 1 in Act III where a single extra body is below par; the class text notes the Trickery buff mod the docs recommend is not installed.

Feint.note: Trickery given the armour it never had: an opening Fighter level buys heavy armour, shields, a Defence style and Str + Con saves, and the Lore block buys the skill coverage the Cleric multiclass node refuses to grant. It gives up Action Surge and the domain capstone.
Feint.strength: One level repairs the domain's worst structural gap, and it repairs it at level 1 where the save proficiencies are still purchasable — in a duo the Str + Con pair stops the grapples and shoves that separate two bodies and protects the concentration this chassis rides all fight.
Feint.wants: A partner that supplies both damage rows, because this body's contribution to killing anything is Spirit Guardians and nothing else.
uncertain: Feat count read off Listo's class-level cadence (6); the character-level reading gives 7.
No Persuasion proficiency exists before the Bard block; Acts I and II record a bare Charisma modifier.

Evenfall.note: Twilight Sanctuary as a standing outward tap — temporary HP or a charm cleanse on every body that ends its turn inside — with Steps of Night for flight, heavy armour, martial weapons and Spirit Guardians for the damage. It gives up single-target output and the Twilight Shroud capstone at 17.
Evenfall.strength: The sanctuary costs one Channel Divinity charge that a short rest refunds and then runs with no action for a minute, which in a two-body party means both characters get temporary HP every round for free — and Lone Wolf's halved damage makes each of those points count double.
Evenfall.wants: A body that ends fights, since this one's whole contribution is keeping both halves standing while the clock runs.
uncertain: College of Stormcalling's own features were outside the read set; the Bard 6 block is scored on shared class features only.
Rescue falls to 4 in Act III because the act's rung-5 row wants 9th-tier restoration and Mass Heal, which Cleric 14 cannot prepare even on a caster-20 slot table.

Penumbra.split: Cleric 11 (Twilight) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend)
Penumbra.note: Twilight taken only as deep as its Channel Divinity and Greater Restoration, then spent on Lore skills, a Chain familiar and Repelling Blast. It gives up Divine Strike, Steps of Night's later uptime and the deeper slot table.
Penumbra.strength: Everything it leans on refills without a long rest — the sanctuary on a Channel Divinity charge, the pact slots on a short rest, Repelling Blast on nothing — so the pair can take a third hard fight in a cycle instead of paying 120 supplies for it.
Penumbra.wants: A front body with real mitigation, because this one's only defensive layer is the temporary HP it is already handing out.
uncertain: Feat count read off Listo's class-level cadence (6); the character-level reading gives 7.
Warlock patron picked as The Fiend; the patron list was outside the read set.

Vanguard.note: The only Cleric with true Extra Attack, played as a pure weapon body: four swings a round off Lone Wolf's two Actions, a War Priest bonus attack on top, Divine Strike 2d8, and no concentration spell at all. It gives up Spirit Guardians and with it any area damage worth the name.
Vanguard.strength: Holding no concentration is the point — the pair's two slots both stay with the partner, and this body's damage is at-will weapon output with no clock, so it keeps swinging through a third hard fight when the slot-funded chassis have run dry.
Vanguard.wants: Crowd clear and area control, both of which sit at the floor here; the partner has to own the whole crowd side of the square.
uncertain: Feat count read off Listo's class-level cadence (6); the character-level reading gives 7.
The single-target row follows the rubric's 'Extra Attack plus a flat rider' anchor at 3/2/2 — Divine Strike 2d8 is flat and is outrun by the enemy-HP multiplier, which the ratio already prices.
Durability falls to 3 in Act III because Heavy Armour Master is flat-only mitigation in a boss-weighted act.

War.note: The same War engine with the concentration slot spent: Extra Attack and War Priest under a Spirit Guardians aura, which turns a pure single-target body into one that also clears. It gives up the freedom of holding nothing — every hit taken is now a concentration check on a body standing in melee.
War.strength: It is the only chassis here that reaches par on single-target and rung 3 on area at once, and Lone Wolf's two Actions are what make that true: four weapon swings plus a bonus attack while the aura ticks on everything adjacent, which is what Listo's larger enemy counts actually punish a duo for lacking.
War.wants: Save support or a body that can pull attention, because a melee concentration holder in Listo's encounters loses the aura early without one.
uncertain: College of Stormcalling's own features were outside the read set; the Bard 6 block is scored on shared class features only.
Durability falls to 3 in Act III because Heavy Armour Master is flat-only mitigation in a boss-weighted act.

Pyre.note: Consuming Fervor turning Fireball into a maximised 48-per-target burst twice a short rest, from a heavy-armour body that also holds Haste on its partner. It gives up single-target damage — Zeal has a bonus-action attack but no Extra Attack, so two swings a round is all it gets.
Pyre.strength: Two maximised Fireballs land in every fight because Channel Divinity is a short-rest pool, and the concentration slot goes to Haste on the other body rather than to a spell of its own — so one character funds the pair's crowd clear and the other character's extra Action out of two different clocks.
Pyre.wants: A partner whose turn is worth hasting and who can finish a boss, since this body's single-target row never clears 0.6 of par.
uncertain: Feat count read off Listo's class-level cadence (6); the character-level reading gives 7.

The AoE row uses the rubric's own Consuming Fervor anchor (74 raw per round, 5/4/4); fire is commonly resisted from Act II but Consuming Fervor also fires on thunder, so no 0.5 resistance multiplier is applied.
Durability falls to 3 in Act III because Heavy Armour Master is flat-only mitigation in a boss-weighted act.

Fervor.note: The same maximised-Fireball engine with the concentration slot deliberately left empty, opened on Barbarian for Str + Con saves, a d12 die and Rage's physical resistance. It gives up Haste and therefore most of its action-economy value, buying resilience with it.
Fervor.strength: Consuming Fervor needs no concentration at all, so this body delivers the batch's best area burst while holding nothing the enemy can break — which in a duo means both of the pair's concentration slots are free for the partner to spend.
Fervor.wants: A body that owns both concentration slots and can lock a boss down, because this one deliberately holds neither and has no single-target answer.
uncertain: Feat count read off Listo's class-level cadence (6); the character-level reading gives 7.

Heavy armour comes from the Zeal domain at Cleric 1, not from the level-1 Barbarian, so Heavy Armour Master is affordable but sits outside the rubric's literal 'level-1 class grants heavy armour' clause.
Durability falls to 3 in Act III because Heavy Armour Master is flat-only mitigation in a boss-weighted act.

Fletch.split: Wizard 6 (Bladesinging) / Fighter 11 (Arcane Archer) / Druid 3 (Circle of the Moon)
Fletch.note: A bow Fighter that opens Wizard for Bladesong AC and Con saves, then spends its last levels on a Druid familiar. Gives up heavy armour entirely — the Fighter node taken after level 1 grants no Heavy proficiency — and its Wizard list freezes at 3rd-tier spells.
Fletch.strength: Arcane Arrows recharge on a short rest, so the rider that removes a threat costs nothing against a 120-supply long rest, and Banishing/Enfeebling Arrow is how a two-body party subtracts an enemy it cannot out-damage.
Fletch.wants: A body that carries Perception and town dialogue, because this one rolls +0 and −1 on them in every act.
uncertain: Level order assumed Wizard 1-2, Fighter 1-11, Druid 1-3, Wizard 3-6; a different order moves Act II by a rung on aoe and ctrl_a.
Circle of the Moon chosen for the 3-level Druid dip; the dip text says circle features keyed to Druid level are poor dip targets, so the circle contributes almost nothing.

StormcallingBard.note: Arcane Archer taken to 14 for ten Arcane Arrows and five shots, with a Bard opener for Dex+Cha saves, three skills and late Expertise. It trades heavy armour and any Act I skill depth for the deepest short-rest rider pool in the Fighter list.
StormcallingBard.strength: Ten arrows come back on every short rest and each is a no-concentration rider, so this body spends nothing the pair's two concentration slots or its long rest need.
StormcallingBard.wants: A body that holds area control, because this one puts every arrow into one target and has no answer to a crowd.
uncertain: College of Stormcalling's own features were not in my read set; its AoE contribution is scored as generic 3rd-tier Bard slots.

Standard.split: Fighter 11 (Banneret) / Bloodhunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Standard.note: Heavy-armour Banneret built for Inspiring Surge, with a late Bard block for Expertise and a three-level Blood Hunter tail for Crimson Rite. It gives up every form of concentration control to keep its reactions and its Action Surge free.
Standard.strength: Inspiring Surge turns one Action Surge into the partner's off-turn weapon attack, and in a party of exactly two that is half the party's action economy bought with a short-rest resource.
Standard.wants: A body that supplies area control and area damage; this one is zero on both in every act.
uncertain: Rallying Cry scored as rung-3 repeatable outward healing on a short-rest clock; it heals for Fighter level per ally, which is flat and therefore decaying, but the clock is what earns the rung.

Pennant.split: Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling) / Fighter 11 (Banneret) / Paladin 3 (Oath of the Ancients)
Pennant.note: The same Banneret action-economy engine opened on Bard for Dex+Cha saves and a full three-skill level-1 package, with a Paladin tail for Divine Smite off Bard slots. The cost is heavy armour, which the Fighter multiclass node does not grant.
Pennant.strength: Rallying Cry heals the other body off Second Wind's short-rest clock and Inspiring Surge hands it an attack off Action Surge — two features that normally scale with party size and here land entirely on one partner.
Pennant.wants: A body that holds the pair's concentration slot and covers crowds; this one has no area answer at all.
uncertain: Oath of the Ancients picked for the 3-level Paladin dip; its aura is a level-7 feature, so only the oath spells and Channel Oath land here.

Cadence.note: Battle Master to 14 for five d10 superiority dice, opened on Bard for Dex+Cha saves and Expertise. Medium armour only — the Fighter node taken after level 1 carries no Heavy proficiency — so it buys manoeuvres with defence.
Cadence.strength: Every superiority die comes back on a short rest, which is the only clock that matters when a long rest costs 120+ supplies, and Commander's Strike hands the other body an attack on your turn.
Cadence.wants: A body that answers crowds — area damage or area control — because this one puts every die into one target.

Drillmaster.note: The same Battle Master body opened on Fighter, which buys Str+Con saves and heavy armour at the cost of the Bard's level-1 skill package. It has no spell above 3rd tier and no rescue until Act II.
Drillmaster.strength: Heavy armour plus shield is a floor Lone Wolf's halving multiplies, and the whole manoeuvre kit refills twice per long rest, so three hard fights cost nothing but supplies for the rest.
Drillmaster.wants: A body that covers area damage and dialogue; this one is a single-target engine with a thin Charisma.

Anvil.split: Fighter 11 (Brute) / Bloodhunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Anvil.note: Brute Force on every hit stacked onto Improved Extra Attack and a Crimson Rite, in heavy armour. It has no control, no area damage and no rescue — the whole build is one number going up.
Anvil.strength: Brutish Durability is +1d6 on every saving throw with no resource and no action, which directly answers the run's failure mode: one of two bodies losing a save and the fight ending.
Anvil.wants: A body that holds both control axes; this one is 0-1 on area everything and cannot remove an enemy turn.
uncertain: Brute Force stays at d6 because the split stops at Fighter 11; the d8 at 16 and d10 at 20 are never reached, which is why the Act III ratio does not climb.

Ancients.split: Cleric 6 (Tempest Domain) / Fighter 11 (Brute) / Paladin 3 (Oath of the Ancients)
Ancients.note: A Tempest opener for Wis+Cha saves, heavy armour and Spirit Guardians, then eleven Fighter levels of Brute Force. It is very slow: no Extra Attack until Act II and no third attack until Act III.
Ancients.strength: Spirit Guardians is at-will area damage for as long as concentration holds, which on a heavy-armour body with Brutish Durability is a concentration slot the pair can actually keep.
Ancients.wants: A body that carries every skill check — this one rolls +0 on Investigation and Persuasion in all three acts.
uncertain: Spirit Guardians is booked to aoe and therefore not also claimed on ctrl_a, per the one-pool-one-axis rule.
Level order assumed Cleric 1-6 first; deferring the Cleric block would raise Act I st and drop Act I aoe by two rungs.

Bridle.note: Cavalier to 14 for Unwavering Mark, Warding Maneuver and Hold the Line, opened on Bard for Dex+Cha saves and Expertise. No heavy armour, and Vigilant Defender at 18 is never reached.
Bridle.strength: Warding Maneuver spends a reaction to add 1d8 AC and resistance to an attack aimed at the other body, and Lone Wolf's second reaction means it can be spent twice a round in a party where there is only one other body to protect.
Bridle.wants: A body that removes enemy turns outright; this one redirects attention but never takes an action away.
uncertain: Unwavering Mark and Warding Maneuver are both long-rest pools sized by an ability modifier, so their per-fight allowance is roughly two each; the ctrl_s rung rests on the mark's disadvantage clause, which costs no concentration.

Pikeman.note: The same Cavalier opened on Fighter, which buys Str+Con saves and heavy armour and makes Warding Maneuver's resistance the second mitigation layer on an already-hard body.
Pikeman.strength: Heavy armour plus shield plus a reaction that halves one incoming attack is the closest thing in the Fighter list to a taunt, and BG3 has none — enemy AI picks the softer half of a duo, so relocating hits is worth more here than in a four-body party.
Pikeman.wants: A body that answers crowds and carries dialogue; this one has almost no area game and a thin Charisma.

Edge.split: Fighter 11 (Champion) / Bloodhunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Edge.note: A crit-fishing Champion in heavy armour with a Crimson Rite and a late Bard block. It buys nothing but attack quality — no control, no area, no rescue.
Edge.strength: Heroic Warrior is a free reroll on a failed save every turn with no resource, which in a two-body party is a second Indomitable on the axis that actually loses fights.
Edge.wants: A body that covers both control axes and area damage; this one is 0-1 on all three.
uncertain: Superior Critical is a Champion 15 feature and the split stops at 11, so Act III keeps a 19-20 range; the small st rise comes from Crimson Rite, not the crit band.

Vantage.note: Rogue opener for four proficiencies and two Expertise, Thief's extra bonus action, then a Champion core. It gives up heavy armour and every spell above 3rd tier to be the pair's skill body and its highest-throughput attacker.
Vantage.strength: Thief's bonus action lands on top of Lone Wolf's second one, so this body throws three off-hand strikes a round on a clock that never runs out, and its Rogue-plus-Bard Expertise is the only thing in the pair that reads a trap.
Vantage.wants: A body that holds concentration and answers crowds; this one is 0-1 on both control axes in every act.
uncertain: Scored dual-wielding, which drops damage per hit to 1d8+Dex against par's 2d6; a two-handed configuration would trade the three off-hand strikes for a bigger die and land in the same band.

Interval.note: A Chronoknight built to hand its Action away, opened on Bard for Dex+Cha saves. The subclass is the least battle-tested in the file and its signature feature cannot be used on the same turn as Action Surge, so the two action-economy engines alternate rather than stack.
Interval.strength: Borrowed Time grants an entire Action to any entity you choose, and in a party of exactly two there is one obvious recipient; Alacrity's extra Reaction stacks on top of Lone Wolf's for four reactions across the pair.
Interval.wants: A body that can spend a spare Action well — a caster with more good turns than turn slots — and one that answers crowds.
uncertain: Borrowed Time runs on sorcery points equal to 1 + Int modifier per long rest, so at a martial's Intelligence it is roughly one use per fight; act is scored at 4 rather than 5 for that and for the Action Surge exclusion.
Subclass mechanics come from the DTO reference site rather than the pak; the class file flags it as added for testing.

Reprise.note: The same Chronoknight opened on Fighter for Str+Con saves and heavy armour, which is the version that can stand in the front rank while it lends its turns out.
Reprise.strength: Rewind is a short-rest reaction that turns one of the pair's failed saves into a success, and with only two bodies a single failed save is half the action economy.
Reprise.wants: A body with more good things to do per round than it has rounds, and an answer to crowds.
uncertain: Same DTO-site provenance caveat as the Bard-opened variant.

Doppel.split: Wizard 6 (Bladesinging) / Fighter 11 (Echo Knight) / Monk 3 (Way of the Friar)
Doppel.note: Echo Knight with a Bladesinging opener for Int+Wis saves and Con-save AC, and a Friar tail for the bonded temp HP. Legion of One is not implemented in this modlist, so the subclass stops giving at Fighter 15.
Doppel.strength: The echo is a second threatened zone that generates opportunity attacks 9m away and Shadow Martyr eats an attack aimed at the other body on a short-rest clock — a duo has no spare body to interpose, and this one manufactures a disposable third position.
Doppel.wants: A body that carries Perception and dialogue; this one rolls 0 and -1 on those and cannot be repaired by levels.
uncertain: Unleash Incarnation is uses = Con modifier on a long rest, so it amortises to roughly one extra attack per fight and moves st by well under a rung.
friars-blessing is a pair-scope blanket booster and only lands in Act III on this level order.

Afterimage.split: Wizard 6 (Bladesinging) / Fighter 11 (Echo Knight) / Druid 3 (Circle of the Moon)
Afterimage.note: The same Echo Knight with a Druid tail instead of a Monk one, trading the Friar's shared save die and temp HP for a permanent familiar and Wild Shape. It still ends with no Perception and no Charisma.
Afterimage.strength: Echo plus familiar plus Action Surge puts three separate positions on the initiative order for a party that only has two, and the echo costs nothing per round to maintain.
Afterimage.wants: A body that carries every out-of-combat check and holds outward healing; this one is 0 on rescue until Act II.
uncertain: Druid 3 arrives at character 18-20 on this order, so Find Familiar and Wild Shape are Act III only and buy no rung.

Grimoire.split: Fighter 11 (Eldritch Knight) / Bloodhunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Grimoire.note: Eldritch Knight in heavy armour with the school restrictions removed, a Bard block for slots and Expertise, and a Crimson Rite tail. It splits its stat budget across Strength and Intelligence and is behind on both.
Grimoire.strength: Action Surge resets the PHB2024 War Magic counter, so a surge turn is two attacks plus a cantrip and then a levelled spell plus an attack — and Lone Wolf's second Action is a third pass on top of that.
Grimoire.wants: A body that carries dialogue and outward rescue; this one is 0 on rescue in Act I and never above 2.
uncertain: Booming Blade is 1d8 per tier at character 5/10/17 here, so the Act III st rise is the cantrip scaling plus Crimson Rite, not the subclass.
Improved War Magic is an Eldritch Knight 12 feature and the split stops at 11, so the two-attacks-for-a-levelled-spell trade never lands.

Sigil.split: Sorcerer 6 (Draconic Bloodline) / Fighter 11 (Eldritch Knight) / Paladin 3 (Oath of the Ancients)
Sigil.note: A Sorcerer opener for Metamagic and Con+Cha saves under an Eldritch Knight core, with a Paladin tail so unspent slots become Divine Smite. Three casting-adjacent stats and no armour proficiency from the level-1 class.
Sigil.strength: Quickened Spell converts an Action cast to a bonus action, and beside Lone Wolf's second Action that is the only reliable route in the list to three casts plus a weapon routine in one turn.
Sigil.wants: A body that carries Perception and holds the pair's durability floor; this one is medium armour at best and thin on every trap check.
uncertain: Sorcery points equal Sorcerer level, so six points across three fights is roughly two per fight — enough for one Twinned buff or one Quickened cast, not both.
Twinned Death Ward needs 4th-level spells known, which a Sorcerer 6 does not have; rescue is scored on Twinned Healing Word and Lay on Hands instead.

Bastion.note: Psi Warrior to 14 for twelve psionic dice, opened on Bard for Dex+Cha saves and Expertise. It forgoes heavy armour and spends its Intelligence on a die size rather than a spell list.
Bastion.strength: Protective Field spends a reaction to cut damage to the other body from 9m away on their turn, and Lone Wolf gives two reactions a round — with only one partner to cover, every die goes where it is needed.
Bastion.wants: A body that answers crowds with damage or control; this one is 0-1 on both area axes.
uncertain: Psionic dice restore on a long rest with one bonus-action refresh per short rest, which is why end sits at 3-4 rather than in the short-rest band.

Fulcrum.note: The same Psi Warrior opened on Fighter, buying Str+Con saves, heavy armour and Guarded Mind's psychic resistance on top of the shield. It gives up the Bard's level-1 skill package.
Fulcrum.strength: It is the durable half of a pair that can still spend its reactions outward — heavy armour and shield for itself, Protective Field for the other body, both every round.
Fulcrum.wants: A body that removes several enemy turns at once, and one that carries town dialogue.

Wyrmwatch.split: Wizard 6 (Bladesinging) / Fighter 11 (Purple Dragon Knight (2024 UA)) / Monk 3 (Way of the Friar)
Wyrmwatch.note: The 2024 Purple Dragon Knight's amethyst dragon carried on a Bladesinging opener, with a Friar tail. The author warns the dragon needs a fresh playthrough and breaks pathfinding indoors, and this body has no Perception at all.
Wyrmwatch.strength: The dragon is a third combatant sharing your initiative that needs no bonus action to command, and Rallying Surge turns Action Surge into reaction attacks for the partner and the dragon both — a duo's action economy roughly doubled off a short-rest charge.
Wyrmwatch.wants: A body that reads traps and talks; this one is 0 Perception and -1 Persuasion in every act.
uncertain: The dragon's own attacks and Gravity Breath are excluded from st and aoe per the rule that summons and extra bodies are scored on Actions, not on the damage axes.
Camp-supply cost scales with camp population, which the dragon adds to; not priced into end.

Hatchling.split: Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling) / Fighter 14 (Purple Dragon Knight (2024 UA))
Hatchling.note: Purple Dragon Knight to 14 for Amethyst Pinnacle, opened on Bard for Dex+Cha saves, Expertise and a real dialogue score. Medium armour only, and the dragon carries the stability caveats the mod author flags.
Hatchling.strength: Rallying Surge lets up to three allies react off one Action Surge; with two bodies and a dragon the pair fields three attackers on a single short-rest charge, which is what Listo's inflated enemy counts are tuned against.
Hatchling.wants: A body that holds the concentration slot and controls a crowd; this one adds bodies but takes no enemy turns away.
uncertain: Dragon damage excluded from st and aoe, as above.

Glyph.split: Cleric 6 (Tempest Domain) / Fighter 11 (Rune Knight) / Bloodhunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer)
Glyph.note: Tempest opener for Wis+Cha saves and heavy armour, then eleven Rune Knight levels and a Crimson Rite tail. Very slow off the line — one attack per Action until Act II — and it never reaches Master of Runes at 15.
Glyph.strength: Almost the whole rune toolbox is on the short-rest clock: Hill Rune's physical resistance, Cloud Rune's redirect and Runic Shield's forced reroll all refill twice per long rest, which is the cadence a 120-supply rest actually allows.
Glyph.wants: A body that carries every out-of-combat check; this one rolls +0 on Investigation and Persuasion in all three acts.
uncertain: Rune save DCs key off Constitution, not Intelligence; the level-up UI display is wrong. Scored against a Con of 16-18, not the primary.
Rune inscription persistence across rests is only partly verified in the class file.
Spirit Guardians is booked to aoe and not double-claimed on ctrl_a.

Thief.split: Rogue 3 (Thief) / Fighter 11 (Rune Knight) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Thief.note: Rogue opener for four proficiencies and two Expertise plus Thief's bonus action, a Rune Knight core, and a Bard block for slots and two more Expertise. It trades heavy armour and saves depth for being the pair's only competent skill body.
Thief.strength: Three bonus actions a round — Thief's on top of Lone Wolf's two — turned into off-hand strikes, and a rune toolbox that all refills on the short rest the pair takes anyway.
Thief.wants: A body that holds the pair's concentration slot for real area control; this one has surfaces and shoves, nothing that lands on four enemies at once.
uncertain: Scored dual-wielding to use all three bonus actions, which costs damage per hit against par's 2d6.
Giant's Might uses = proficiency bonus on a long rest, roughly one per fight; it moves st by well under a rung.

Bushido.split: Fighter 11 (Samurai) / Bloodhunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Bushido.note: Samurai in heavy armour for the third save proficiency, with a Crimson Rite tail and a late Bard block. Fighting Spirit is a long-rest pool of three and Rapid Strike at 15 is never reached.
Bushido.strength: Elegant Courtier is a fifth save proficiency on a chassis that already holds four, and save proficiencies are otherwise obtainable only from the level-1 class, Lone Wolf and Resilient — in a pair where one failed save is half the action economy that is a structural buy, not a bonus.
Bushido.wants: A body that answers crowds and holds concentration; this one has no area damage and no area control worth the name.
uncertain: Elegant Courtier's saving-throw pick is Wisdom, or Int/Cha if Wisdom is already held; Charisma taken here because Lone Wolf already covers Wisdom.

Kagemusha.note: Swashbuckler opener so Sneak Attack needs no advantage and no adjacent ally, under a Samurai core that hands out advantage anyway. It gives up heavy armour to be the pair's skill and dialogue body.
Kagemusha.strength: Swashbuckler's Sneak Attack works when there is no second melee body, which in a two-person party is most of the time, and Fighting Spirit's advantage feeds it on the turns it does not.
Kagemusha.wants: A body that holds concentration and controls crowds; this one is 0-1 on both control axes throughout.
uncertain: Elegant Courtier lands at Fighter 7, character 11, so the fifth save proficiency is Act II onward.

Enfilade.split: Fighter 11 (Sharpshooter (UA)) / Bloodhunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Enfilade.note: The Sharpshooter subclass — not the feat — in heavy armour, with a Crimson Rite and a late Bard block. Steady Aim is three uses on a short rest and Rapid Strike at 15 is out of reach at Fighter 11.
Enfilade.strength: Steady Aim's +2 plus half Fighter level on every hit for a turn refills on the short rest, so the biggest per-round number in this batch costs nothing against a 120-supply long rest, and Careful Eyes makes Search a bonus action.
Enfilade.wants: A body that holds both control axes and answers a crowd; this one converts everything into single-target damage.
uncertain: Steady Aim assumed active on three of four rounds; the bonus action it costs competes with nothing else on this chassis.
The Sharpshooter feat is a separate, differently rebalanced thing and is assumed taken alongside.

Ballista.split: Cleric 6 (Tempest Domain) / Fighter 11 (Sharpshooter (UA)) / Paladin 3 (Oath of the Ancients)
Ballista.note: A Tempest opener for Wis+Cha saves, heavy armour and maximised lightning, then the Sharpshooter subclass. Its Act I is genuinely poor — one attack per Action and a 3rd-tier spell list — and everything it has arrives late.
Ballista.strength: Destructive Wrath maximises Call Lightning off a Channel Divinity charge that returns on a short rest, and the spell keeps firing every round on one concentration slot while the bow routine runs underneath it.
Ballista.wants: A body that carries dialogue and secret doors; this one rolls +0 on Investigation and Persuasion in every act.
uncertain: Call Lightning rather than Spirit Guardians chosen as the concentration spell, since a ranged body cannot stand in the aura; that is the rule-3 configuration call.
Cleric grants no skill proficiencies in this modlist, which is why the skills row is so narrow.

Flourish.split: Mesmerist 14 (Aspect of the Daredevil) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Flourish.note: A rapier skirmisher running on Panache, Feints and Riposte stances, with a late Bard block for Expertise and 3rd-tier slots. The Daredevil carries no damage rider at all and never gets a second Extra Attack, so four attacks a round is the whole engine and the run outgrows it.
Flourish.strength: Feint and Hypnotic Stare cost no resource at all and the Tier-3 Feints — Blinded/Slowed/Silenced, or Disarmed/Prone/Maimed for two rounds — refresh on a short rest, so this body imposes hard control without ever touching the pair's two concentration slots.
Flourish.wants: A body that supplies area damage and area control; this one is 0-1 on both, and its single-target damage is only par.
uncertain: st reads 2/1/1 — the frozen-chassis signature. Four attacks with no rider is 0.96x par in Act I and 0.66x by Act III; nothing in the Daredevil table fixes that.
Panache only refills on a crit or a kill with a one-handed piercing weapon, otherwise on a long rest; end is scored at 4 on the strength of the at-will core rather than the stance clock.
Superior Defense taken as the level-4 boon (Charisma to AC unarmoured), which is the configuration the durability rung assumes.
The Mesmerist multiclass node is undocumented; skills assume the level-1 three-skill package, which this build gets.

Duellist.split: Mesmerist 11 (Aspect of the Daredevil) / Barbarian 3 (Zealot) / Monk 6 (Way of the Friar)
Duellist.note: A Daredevil with a Monk Flurry engine bolted on and a Barbarian tail for Rage and Reckless Attack. Three different unarmoured-defence formulas compete on one sheet and Rage rewards Strength this body does not have.
Duellist.strength: Lone Wolf's second bonus action doubles Flurry of Blows, and Way of the Friar hands per-turn temp HP and a +1d4 save die to both bodies at once — in a pair, a bonded blessing covers the entire party.
Duellist.wants: A body that carries area damage and holds concentration; this one is 0 on aoe in every act.
uncertain: Rage's +2 damage and physical resistance want Strength and no armour; on a Cha/Dex finesse body the Barbarian tail is close to dead weight and is scored that way.
Monk Extra Attack does not stack with Daredevil's Deeds, so Monk 5 buys nothing here.

Basilisk.split: Sorcerer 6 (Favored Soul) / Mesmerist 14 (Aspect of the Eyebiter)
Basilisk.note: An Eyebiter that turns one enemy into a permanent debuff platform, opened on Favored Soul Sorcerer for Con+Cha saves, medium armour, shields and Metamagic. It has one attack per Action all run — its action economy is the worst in this batch.
Basilisk.strength: Every Bold Stare rides the Hypnotic Stare, which is a bonus action with no resource and no concentration, so the pair's two concentration slots stay free while one enemy eats a standing penalty to saves, AC and attack rolls.
Basilisk.wants: A body that generates actions and covers crowds; this one is 1 on Actions in every act and has no area control at all.
uncertain: Boons taken as Resistance at 4 and Manifold Stare at 8; Manifold is what carries st, Resistance is what carries dur, and a different pair of boons would move both.
Painful Stare triggers once per hit and this body only lands two hits a round, so it uses two of Manifold Stare's three allowed triggers.
Mesmerist's maximum spell level is unverified in the class file; scored as a half-caster topping out at 5th.

Glare.split: Sorcerer 6 (Favored Soul) / Mesmerist 11 (Aspect of the Eyebiter) / Barbarian 3 (Zealot)
Glare.note: The same Eyebiter lockdown three levels shallower, with a Barbarian tail for Rage and Danger Sense. Painful Stare stops at 2d10 because the level-12 die increase is never reached.
Glare.strength: The Stare's penalty is permanent, free and stacks with whatever the partner casts, so a single concentration spell held by the other body lands against a target already down three on its saves.
Glare.wants: A body that supplies actions and area coverage — this one is 1 on Actions and 0-1 on both area axes.
uncertain: Rage wants Strength and no armour; on a Cha body wearing Favored Soul medium armour the Barbarian tail contributes Danger Sense and little else.
Sorcerer 4-6 arrive in Act III on this order, so Fireball is Act III only.

Marionette.split: Mesmerist 11 (Aspect of the Trickster) / Barbarian 3 (Zealot) / Druid 6 (Circle of the Moon)
Marionette.note: A Trickster that implants tricks on the other body and fires them as free actions, with a Druid block for area control and summons. It is not a damage chassis at all — under half par on single-target from Act II onward.
Marionette.strength: Gift of Will adds Charisma plus half level to the partner's Wisdom saves, Mesmeric Mirror makes an attack on them automatically miss, and both fire as free actions off Hypnotic Bonds that refill on a short rest — the two structural problems of a duo, answered on the cheap clock.
Marionette.wants: A body that carries the pair's damage entirely; this one is 0 on single-target from Act II and will never contribute a kill.
uncertain: Boons taken as Healing Bond at 4 and Mocking Machinations at 8; Mocking Machinations is what carries the whole aoe row and a different boon pick zeroes it.
Gift of Will is a pair-scope partial that lands on the partner, so it cannot raise this body's own rung — recorded as a booster so the combiner sees it.
Act III drops from rung 5 to 4 on rescue because the ladder's Act III row wants 9th-tier restoration or Mass Heal, which the Trickster never reaches.

Ventriloquist.split: Barbarian 3 (Zealot) / Mesmerist 11 (Aspect of the Trickster) / Druid 6 (Circle of the Moon)
Ventriloquist.note: The same Trickster support kit opened on Barbarian for Str+Con saves, a d12 hit die, Rage and Unarmoured Defence. The cost is three character levels before the Mesmerist starts, so Gift of Will and the Tier-3 tricks land a whole act later.
Ventriloquist.strength: Towering Ego and Danger Sense between them cover Wisdom and Dexterity saves from Act I, and the Barbarian opener gives the pair's softest support body a Constitution save and a d12 — in a duo the enemy AI picks the softer half and this one is not it.
Ventriloquist.wants: A body that carries all of the pair's damage; this one is 0 on single-target from Act II.
uncertain: Rage is off-synergy with a Charisma caster's routine; scored for its physical resistance and hit die only.
Whether a Mesmerist taken at level 2+ still grants its three skills is undocumented in the class file; the skills row assumes it does.

Lockstep.note: A Wisdom half-caster martial whose whole subclass is written in the second person: Shared Judgment copies every active Judgment onto the partner, and Tempered Champion upgrades apply only to them. It gives up personal damage ceiling and any real area answer to do it.
Lockstep.strength: Every 'per ally' clause in Tactics is priced for a four-body party and paid out to a two-body one — Shared Judgment covers 100% of the party that is not you, and Resiliency's per-turn temp HP plus physical resistance is a no-action outward source on a short-rest clock, which is exactly the clock a 120-supply long rest rewards.
Lockstep.wants: A body that clears crowds, because this one is 0-1 on AoE and 1-2 on area control in every act and will simply be outnumbered.
uncertain: The shipped Inquisitor 2.2.0 pak still carries the dangling level-3 subclass GUID and cannot level past 2; scored under the standing decision that the run swaps to 2.2.1, so nothing here has been seen in a level-up screen.
College of Stormcalling is outside my read set — its Act III contribution is scored as a generic 3rd-tier Bard lightning package.
Battle Acumen's 'per ally within 9m' caps at +1 with one partner unless summons count (unverified in the class text).

Phalanx.note: The Tactics package rebuilt on a d12 opener and finished with a Twilight domain, so the ally-facing kit arrives twice — Shared Judgment's Resiliency temp HP early, Twilight Sanctuary late. It pays three levels of Barbarian it can never rage in, since raging blocks the spellcasting the whole chassis runs on.
Phalanx.strength: Spirit Guardians on a Wisdom martial in heavy armour is a damage floor that needs no Action after the first, and with only two bodies the pair's second concentration slot stays free; Twilight Sanctuary is a no-action aura that covers exactly one other person, which is the entire rest of the party.
Phalanx.wants: A body that holds hard single-target control, because this one never reaches 5th-tier slots and its ctrl-single sits at 1 for two of the three acts.
uncertain: Inquisitor 2.2.0's dangling level-3 subclass GUID is still in the class text; scored under the standing decision to patch to 2.2.1.

Barbarian 3 is scored for Str+Con saves, the d12 hit die and Danger Sense only — Rage and every Rage-gated Zealot feature (Fanatical Focus, Divine Fury) are unusable on a body whose plan is Spirit Guardians, so no Rage-conditional booster is claimed.
Spirit Guardians is claimed on AoE, so it is deliberately not also scored on control-area.
Persuasion is 0 in all three acts — no class in the split grants it and Charisma is a dump stat.

Vengeance.note: The selfish Inquisition: Divine Scourge lifts Monster Lore's once-per-target limit and refunds the bonus action, so a resistance-ignoring scaling die lands every round, and Studied Combat rolls all damage against the marked target with advantage. It carries almost no area game and no summons.
Vengeance.strength: Monster Tactician's Expertise plus double Wisdom on one Intelligence skill is the strongest Investigation total in the roster, which matters when two bodies have to find every secret door in the run; and Inquisitor's Edge is reaction-priced, so Lone Wolf's second Reaction buys two contests a round.
Vengeance.wants: Area damage or area control — this body is 0-1 on AoE in every act and will stall the moment an encounter fields five bodies instead of one.
uncertain: Inquisitor 2.2.0's dangling level-3 subclass GUID is still in the class text; scored under the standing decision to patch to 2.2.1.
Monster Tactician's 'double your WIS mod' is read as additive on top of Expertise; whether it replaces the ability modifier instead is not stated.
College of Stormcalling is outside my read set and is scored as a generic 3rd-tier Bard package.

Scourge.note: Vengeance's repeatable resistance-ignoring damage engine opened on a Sorcerer so the level-1 saves are Con+Cha rather than Str, and closed with Metamagic. The six Sorcerer levels arrive last, so Quickened and Twinned exist only in Act III.
Scourge.strength: Twinned Spell in a two-person party is a party-wide buff for one point per slot level — Twinned Death Ward covers everyone there is — and Exploit Weakness plus Monster Lore both ignore resistance, which is the specific thing Absolute Wrath punishes.
Scourge.wants: A body that answers crowds; this one is 0 on AoE for two acts and its area control never clears rung 2.
uncertain: Inquisitor 2.2.0's dangling level-3 subclass GUID is still in the class text; scored under the standing decision to patch to 2.2.1.
Warding Bond is claimed off Favored Soul (Peace) at Sorcerer 3, which lands at character 18 — Act III only.
Whether Inquisitor and Sorcerer stack cleanly on the multiclass slot table is unverified per the class file's own note.

Vigil2.split: Sorcerer 6 (Favored Soul) / Inquisitor 11 (Zeal Inquisition) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend)
Vigil2.note: The bodyguard build: Crusader's Conviction's fast healing, Unyielding Resolve's delayed-damage pool and Wrathful Taunt make it hard to kill and hard to ignore, and Ardent Protector eats damage aimed at the partner outright. It stops at Inquisitor 11, so Guardian's Counterstrike and 5th-tier spells never arrive.
Vigil2.strength: BG3 has no taunt, which is why the pair's durability is its weaker half — Wrathful Taunt is one of the few real taunts in the list, and Ardent Protector plus fast healing turns the softer body's damage into damage this one regenerates for free against a long rest that costs 120+ supplies.
Vigil2.wants: A body that removes enemy action points fast, because this one converts almost nothing into tempo — 0-3 on AoE and 1-2 on both control axes.
uncertain: Inquisitor 2.2.0's dangling level-3 subclass GUID is still in the class text; scored under the standing decision to patch to 2.2.1.

Ardent Protector (absorb 100% of damage dealt to a linked ally) is a redirection effect with no id in the closed registry; it is priced inside the rsc rung-1 redirection cap and NOT authored as a redirect, so the pair's durability floor does not see it. It probably deserves an id.
Unyielding Resolve's '+1 to saves per 5 points in the pool' is a conditional save bonus with no booster id; not claimed.

Keeper.note: Zeal taken deep enough for 4th-tier slots, so Death Ward joins the fast healing and the delayed-damage pool, with six Sorcerer levels bolted on last for Metamagic and Fireball. It never reaches Zeal 15, so the pool discharge and Guardian's Counterstrike are out of the build.
Keeper.strength: Fast healing at full Inquisitor level every turn is long-rest-free sustain, which is the resource Listo actually taxes, and Death Ward plus Ardent Protector means the fight-ending event in a duo — one body going down — has two independent answers on this chassis alone.
Keeper.wants: Area control or lockdown; this body is 1-2 on both control axes and its Act III area game is a single Fireball line.
uncertain: Inquisitor 2.2.0's dangling level-3 subclass GUID is still in the class text; scored under the standing decision to patch to 2.2.1.
Ardent Protector has no redirect id; priced only through the rsc redirection cap.
Blood Rage (+10 STR / −5 AC) is available from Act I but is deliberately not in the scored configuration, since the −5 AC contradicts the durability the chassis exists for.

Abjuration.note: A Wizard that opens Fighter for heavy armour, shields and Str+Con saves, then spends most of its slot budget charging the Arcane Ward instead of throwing it. Five Warlock levels at the end buy short-rest slots the Wizard table cannot.
Abjuration.strength: Projected Ward is one of the only ways in the list to spend Lone Wolf's second Reaction on keeping the *other* body alive, and Improved Abjuration recharges the ward on every short rest — a defensive resource priced in the rest this run can afford rather than the one it cannot.
Abjuration.wants: Damage. This body clears rung 1 on single-target in every act and spends its slots on defence, so the partner has to be the one removing enemy action points.
uncertain: Fighter 1 grants heavy armour only as the level-1 class, which the split honours; Resilient (Wisdom) is assumed taken by Act II to reach four disjoint saves covering all of Wis/Con/Dex.
Warlock 5's Agonizing Blast is scored near-worthless here because Charisma is a tertiary stat on an Int chassis — the invocation is taken for Armour of Shadows and Devil's Sight instead.

Aegis.note: The same heavy-armoured Abjurer taken three levels deeper, which buys 9th-tier slots and the 8th/9th-tier control the Wizard 14 version never learns; the Warlock dip shrinks to two levels and costs a feat by breaking the three-level block.
Aegis.strength: Spell Resistance plus a short-rest-recharging ward on a body already in heavy armour and a shield means the softer half of the duo is not this one — which matters because with no taunt in BG3 the pair's durability is its minimum, and 9th-tier area control that resolves on cast never touches the pair's two concentration slots.
Aegis.wants: A body that actually deals damage; this chassis is rung 1 single-target in all three acts and exists to not die and to lock the room.
uncertain: Act III control-area is scored 4 on the strength of a 9th-tier area effect that resolves on cast (Psychic Scream) rather than holding concentration — reachable only because Wizard 17 learns 9th-level spells, which the Wizard 14 splits do not.
Resilient (Wisdom) assumed by Act II.

Cadenza.note: A Bladesinger that finishes into six Monk levels for ki, a bonus-action strike engine and Hands of Healing — accepting that Monk's Extra Attack and Bladesinging's do not stack and that Unarmoured Defence is dead weight on a low-Wisdom body.
Cadenza.strength: +4 AC and +4 to Constitution saves from a class feature is the largest concentration-protection package a full caster can buy in this list, and in a duo the pair only has two concentration slots — so the body that can actually hold one through Listo's inflated damage is worth more than its damage suggests.
Cadenza.wants: Endurance and an area answer: Bladesong is a long-rest resource in a run that taxes long rests hardest, and this body sits at 1 on Endurance for two acts.
