uncertain: Perception and Persuasion are 0 in all three acts: neither Wizard nor Monk offers either on its skill list and no dip in the split supplies one. This is an honest hole, not a missing value.
Song of Victory (+Int to weapon damage, Wizard 14) is in the scored configuration from Act II; Monk levels arrive at character 15-20 so the bonus-action strike engine is Act III only.

Refrain.split: Wizard 11 (Bladesinging) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Archfey)
Refrain.note: A shallower Bladesinger — no Song of Victory, no Song of Defence scaling past 6th-level slots — traded for Lore's Expertise and Cutting Words and a Pact of the Chain familiar. Two casting stats it cannot both afford.
Refrain.strength: Bladesong's +AC and Constitution saves keep the pair's one held spell alive while Lore's Expertise gives the duo a second body that can actually roll a skill check, which a two-character party has to solve with two sheets and no third.
Refrain.wants: Single-target damage and a durability floor; the Wizard side is rung 1-2 all run and the body is still in light armour.
uncertain: A Bard taken as a later multiclass is credited with one skill proficiency, not three; the class file states the three-skill package for Bard as the level-1 class and does not document the multiclass node.
Single-target falls back to 1 in Act III because Wizard 11 never reaches Song of Victory and the weapon routine stops scaling.

Kennel.note: A summoner in heavy armour: the level-6 school feature reaches off-list for Conjure Animals, Focused Conjuration at 10 makes damage unable to break concentration on it, and the item conjurer supplies a bonus-action consumable every turn. Its own damage is an afterthought.
Kennel.strength: Two players against encounters tuned for five is an action-economy problem, and this is the chassis that answers it directly — a summon set whose concentration cannot be broken by damage, on a body wearing heavy armour and a shield, in a run where the thing that loses fights is a concentration break dropping your third and fourth combatants.
Kennel.wants: A body that removes bosses; this one is rung 1-2 single-target in every act and its summons do not count toward the damage axes.
uncertain: The mod places its level-2/3 features ambiguously (the class file records the mod page at 3 and 6 against vanilla's 2 and 6, unverified) — scored as though the summon reach at 6 is intact.

concentration is authored false on the strength of Focused Conjuration plus 13458's non-concentration Conjure Animals; if that combination does not hold in the install, this body's saves should cap at 3.

Aviary.note: The same summoner opened on Barbarian instead — d12 hit die, Str+Con saves and Unarmoured Defence off Constitution rather than heavy armour, which means the robe stays but the hit points do not. The three Rage charges are unusable on a caster.
Aviary.strength: Unarmoured Defence on a Constitution-heavy Wizard is free AC in a run where the class file says better caster armour is never going to arrive, and a summon set that cannot be concentration-broken doubles the party's body count against Listo's More Enemies pass.
Aviary.wants: Boss damage and a durability partner — it is rung 1-2 single-target throughout and sits in the low band on Durability despite the hit die.
uncertain: Barbarian 1's Rage is scored as contributing nothing — it blocks spellcasting, which is this chassis's entire plan; only the saves, hit die, Unarmoured Defence and Perception proficiency are credited.
Conjuration's level-2-versus-3 feature placement is unverified in the class file.

Augur.split: Wizard 11 (Divination) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Archfey)
Augur.note: Portent as a resource rather than a novelty: three dice by Wizard 6, refunded on short rests by Expert Divination, spent through Lone Wolf's two Reactions. Stopping at Wizard 11 costs 7th-tier and up entirely.
Augur.strength: Portent is a reaction and Lone Wolf gives a second one, so the dice are a pool of guaranteed enemy-save failures or guaranteed enemy misses — and with only two characters, converting one boss save into a failure is often the whole fight; the short-rest refunds fit a 120-supply long rest better than any other Wizard school.
Augur.wants: A body that carries damage, and one that can take a hit — this chassis is rung 1-2 single-target and rung 1-2 Durability in a robe.
uncertain: Portent is scored on control-single as a no-concentration rider (rung 3-4) and again on Rescue as prevention aimed at the partner's failed save; these are different dice from the same pool, so the pool is being read twice at reduced value rather than in full on either axis.
Expansion's Greater Portent at 14 is flagged unverified in the class file and is not scored — Wizard 11 would not reach it anyway.

Oracle.note: Portent on a heavy-armoured chassis taken all the way to 9th-tier slots, so the dice sit behind Time Stop and Psychic Scream rather than behind Hypnotic Pattern. The two Warlock levels break the three-level feat block and cost a feat.
Oracle.strength: Heavy armour and a shield on the body holding the pair's Portent dice means the reaction is actually available — with no taunt, enemy AI picks the softer half, and a Diviner in a robe spends its Reactions on Shield instead. Nine-tier area control that resolves on cast leaves both concentration slots free.
Oracle.wants: Single-target damage; this body never clears rung 2 on st and its whole tempo contribution is control.
uncertain: Resilient (Wisdom) assumed by Act II to reach the four-disjoint set covering Wis/Con/Dex.
Act III control-area 4 rests on a 9th-tier effect resolving on cast rather than holding concentration.

Lure.split: Wizard 11 (Enchantment) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Archfey)
Lure.note: Hypnotic Gaze as the primary weapon — charm plus incapacitate on one creature, maintainable every turn, and under mod 22655 it strips the target's concentration without touching yours. Split Enchantment at Wizard 10 doubles it up. It spends every slot on control and deals almost no damage.
Lure.strength: It is single-target hard control that costs no concentration, which in a duo holding exactly two slots between them is worth a full rung more than anything that spends one — and stripping an enemy caster's concentration is a two-for-one against the encounters Listo's overhaul adds.
Lure.wants: Damage on both axes: this body is rung 1 single-target and rung 2 AoE in every act, so the partner has to be the entire kill clock.
uncertain: The class file warns that Listo enemies are far more save-capable than vanilla and bosses carry magic resistance; Hypnotic Gaze is still scored at rung 4 because the rung-4 clause is about concentration cost, not landing rate, but a save-based reading would drop it to 3.

Beguiler.note: The same no-concentration lockdown taken three levels deeper for 7th-tier slots, closed with six Monk levels that buy ki, a bonus-action strike and Hands of Healing. The Monk half is a resource clock, not a damage plan — Unarmoured Defence does nothing on a low-Wisdom Wizard.
Beguiler.strength: Split Enchantment doubling Hold Monster or Dominate lands at exactly the level Listo's encounters start fielding pairs of dangerous bodies, and Instinctive Charm gives Lone Wolf's spare Reaction something to do every round rather than only when a Shield is worth a slot.
Beguiler.wants: Crowd clear and a durability floor; it is rung 1-2 AoE throughout and has no armour worth the name.
uncertain: Perception and Persuasion are 0 in all three acts — neither Wizard nor Monk lists either skill and no dip supplies one.
Enemy magic resistance and Listo's raised enemy saves are a live threat to the whole chassis; scored on the concentration-cost clause rather than on landing rate.

Evocation.note: The safe default: Sculpt Spells so the partner never eats your own fireball, Potent Cantrip, and Empowered Evocation adding Intelligence to every Evocation damage roll. Six Friar levels at the end buy shields, per-turn temp HP for both bodies and a teleport to the partner.
Evocation.strength: In a two-body party the partner is *always* inside your own area spell, so Sculpt Spells is worth far more here than in a four-body one; and Empowered Evocation adds Intelligence to each of four targets, which is the multiplier the crowd term rewards against Listo's added bodies.
Evocation.wants: Boss removal and control — this body never clears rung 2 on single-target and its area control is background from Act II on.
uncertain: friars-blessing is a pair-scope blanket booster and is authored on Act III only, since Monk 3 lands at character 17.
Perception and Persuasion are 0 in every act; Wizard/Monk offers neither.
Evocation is scored as a generalist (Fireball, Cone of Cold, Lightning Bolt) so Absolute Wrath's resistance multiplier is not applied; a build locked to Fire would drop a rung on AoE from Act II.

EvocationWizard.note: Evocation carried by a Bard tail rather than a Monk one, which trades the ki clock for Expertise, Jack of All Trades and six more caster levels — so the slot table reaches 9th tier even though the Wizard's known spells stop at 7th.
EvocationWizard.strength: Two full-caster halves stack slot progression 1-for-1, so the damage half of the pool is upcast two tiers higher than a Wizard 14 with a martial dip; and Sculpt Spells means the partner can stand inside every one of them, which is the only reason a duo can throw area damage at its own melee.
EvocationWizard.wants: Something that survives being hit — this is a robe with no mitigation layer at all, and Durability sits at 1-2 all run.
uncertain: College of Stormcalling is outside my read set; it is scored as a generic Bard college contributing caster levels, Expertise and Jack of All Trades, with no subclass-specific damage credited.
Bard taken as a later multiclass is credited with one skill proficiency, not three.

Hexcraft.note: The slot-economy school: Warlock spells copied into an Intelligence spellbook, five Eldritch Invocations by Wizard 14, ritual casting feeding temporary hit points, and Heart of Darkness refunding a slot on every kill. Six Friar levels add shields and a pair-wide save die.
Hexcraft.strength: Slots are the binding constraint in a game where a long rest costs 120+ camp supplies, and this is the only Wizard that makes its own — Intelligence-modifier refunds per long rest on top of Ritual Caster teaching every ritual on the list, which feeds the level-6 temp-HP engine constantly.
Hexcraft.wants: A body that removes bosses; this chassis converts its extra slots into more of the same mid-tier output rather than into a kill.
uncertain: Hexcraft's level-10 immunity to all emotion-altering conditions is a genuine blanket defence against the charm/fear line with no booster id in the closed registry; it is not claimed on saves and probably deserves one.
Invocations are scored for Armour of Shadows, Devil's Sight and Repelling Blast rather than Agonizing Blast, which is near-worthless on an Intelligence chassis.
Perception and Persuasion are 0 in every act.

Marginalia.split: Fighter 1 (none) / Wizard 14 (Hexcraft) / Monk 5 (Way of the Friar)
Marginalia.note: The same slot-refunding Hexcrafter opened on Fighter for heavy armour, shields and Second Wind, with the Monk tail cut to five levels so it still reaches the Friar's tier-1 package and Deflect Missiles. The five-level Monk block breaks the feat cadence.
Marginalia.strength: Heavy armour on a full caster removes the reason a Wizard is the body the enemy AI picks, and Heart of Darkness plus short-rest ritual temp HP means the pair can take the short rests this run wants instead of the long rests it cannot afford.
Marginalia.wants: Crowd control that does not spend a concentration slot, and a face — Persuasion is 0 in every act.
uncertain: Resilient (Wisdom) assumed by Act II.
Hexcraft's charm/fear immunity has no booster id and is not claimed.
friars-blessing authored on Act III only — Monk 3 lands at character 18 on this level order.

Reliquary.note: The Wizard that heals: Erudite Remedy as a bonus-action outward heal that also hands the target a chosen damage resistance, Divine Scribe's always-prepared Cleric line, Raise Dead as a ritual at 10, and Warding Rejuvenation raising a downed partner at 14. Heavy armour comes from the Fighter opener.
Reliquary.strength: In a two-person run the fight-ending event is one character going down, and this is the only Wizard that both raises the downed body and pre-applies elemental resistance to it as a bonus action before a known damage type lands — a rescue kit that costs no concentration and therefore never competes with the pair's two slots.
Reliquary.wants: Tempo. It is rung 1-2 single-target and its area damage is one Spirit Guardians; the partner has to be the kill clock.
uncertain: Spirit Guardians is claimed on AoE, so it is deliberately not also scored on control-area.

Rescue 5 in Act II rests on Greater Restoration (Hierophant 9) plus Warding Rejuvenation (14) on a short-rest recharge, which the Act II rung-5 row asks for in Flurry-of-Healing terms; the Act III row asks for 9th-tier restoration this Wizard 14 never learns, hence the fall to 4.
Resilient (Wisdom) assumed by Act II.

Viaticum.note: The healer-Wizard taken to 9th-tier slots, which buys the top of the area-control ladder alongside the rescue kit; the Warlock tail shrinks to two levels for at-will beams and costs a feat by breaking the three-level block.
Viaticum.strength: It holds the pair's rescue and the pair's crowd answer on the same body, so the partner is free to be a pure damage chassis — and Erudite Remedy is a bonus action, which means Lone Wolf's second Action is never the thing being spent to keep the other half alive.
Viaticum.wants: A partner that kills things; this body is rung 1-2 on single-target in all three acts by design.
uncertain: Act III rescue 5 assumes the 9th-level slot is spent on the upcast restoration line rather than on the area control also credited at rung 4; if only one 9th slot exists per long rest these two claims compete, and rescue would fall to 4.
Resilient (Wisdom) assumed by Act II.

Ossuary.split: Wizard 11 (Necromancy) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend)
Ossuary.note: A necromancer stopped at Wizard 11 for 6th-tier slots and finished with Lore and a Pact of the Chain familiar. Animate Dead++ removes the undead cap and moves the free casting to Wizard 5, so the body count is the build; its own damage is ordinary.
Ossuary.strength: Two players against encounters tuned for five is solved most directly by fielding four to eight extra bodies, and this is the only chassis in the list built to do that — undead that benefit from short rests, carry proficiency bonus to damage, and scale with the upcast slots the Bard tail keeps handing out.
Ossuary.wants: Concentration-free control or a real boss answer; the undead are long-rest-bound, so a partner that carries the fights where the bodies are already spent.
uncertain: Undead are excluded from the two damage axes per the ratio rules (summons and extra bodies are §4), so Necromancy's whole payload sits on Actions and nothing on st/aoe.
Actions is held at 4 rather than 5 in Act III because Wizard 11 never reaches the 9th-tier summons the rung-5 row names, even though the multiclass slot table does.
Endurance is 1 in every act: the undead are a long-rest pool and the class file names heavy turn-time as the other cost.

Charnel.note: The same undead engine taken to Wizard 14 for 7th-tier upcasting, with a Bard tail stacking caster levels so Animate Dead can be thrown from a 9th-level slot. Inured to Undeath at 10 blanks the max-HP reduction Act II leans on.
Charnel.strength: Upcast Animate Dead adds two undead per slot with the cap removed, so the pair's body count scales with exactly the resource two full-caster halves stack fastest — and Inured to Undeath means the body running the summons is immune to the one effect Listo's undead-heavy Act II uses to grind a two-person party down.
Charnel.wants: A partner who deals the damage; the undead do not count on either damage axis and this chassis is rung 2 there at best.
uncertain: Actions 5 in Act III is claimed on the uncapped-undead clause the rung-5 row names explicitly, reached through the combined 19-caster-level slot table rather than through Wizard level.
College of Stormcalling is outside my read set and is scored only for caster levels, Expertise and Jack of All Trades.
Expansion's Command Undead at 14 is flagged unverified in the class file and is not scored.

Colophon.split: Fighter 1 (none) / Wizard 14 (Order of Scribes) / Bard 5 (College of Lore)
Colophon.note: Formulaic Attunement makes one damage type ignore resistance and hit slightly harder, and the Spectral Mind is both a remote casting position and an extra body. Attunement cannot be changed mid-combat, so the pick is made before the fight and lived with.
Colophon.strength: Absolute Wrath is on and Listo's Combat Extender hands bosses resistance liberally — this is the cleanest answer in the list to it, and a caster that keeps working in fights where a mono-element Evoker stalls is worth more to a duo than to a party that can bring a second element.
Colophon.wants: A body that holds concentration control, and a face — Persuasion only exists here from Act III.
uncertain: The class file marks the levels for Wizardly Quill / Awakened Spellbook and the exact Formulaic Attunement bonus as unverified (the mod page tables are images); the resistance bypass is scored, the extra damage is not.
No Absolute Wrath resistance multiplier is applied to this chassis on either damage axis, which is the whole point of the subclass.
Resilient (Wisdom) assumed by Act II.

Quillmark.split: Wizard 14 (Order of Scribes) / Monk 6 (Way of the Friar)
Quillmark.note: The resistance-ignoring scribe with a Friar tail instead of a Fighter opener — shields, a pair-wide save die, a teleport to the partner and a ki clock, at the cost of heavy armour and the Str+Con save pair.
Quillmark.strength: One With The Word prevents damage outright once per long rest while the Spectral Mind is up, and the Mind itself is a remote casting position — which is a real survivability tool when there is no third body to block for you, and the pair has no taunt to make one.
Quillmark.wants: Boss damage and a Perception body; this chassis rolls nothing on traps in any act.
uncertain: Order of Scribes' feature levels and Formulaic Attunement magnitude are unverified in the class file.
Perception and Persuasion are 0 in every act.
friars-blessing is authored on Act III only (Monk 3 lands at character 17).

Bombardment.split: Fighter 1 (none) / Wizard 14 (School of Bombardment) / Bard 5 (College of Lore)
Bombardment.note: Arcane Ordnance is a slot-free area attack every single turn — a 3m explosion for cantrip-scaling dice plus Intelligence, refilled by casting any spell — and Saturating Fire at 14 rides it along on a bonus action. The Salvo and Barrage toggles are unreachable on the shipped pak, so it is one projectile at a time.
Bombardment.strength: At-will area damage delivered every round outruns a once-per-fight burst by far more than any single-target engine outruns another, and here it costs no slot at all — so the Wizard's Actions stay free for the levelled spell while the bomb handles chip damage and leaves a surface behind for the partner to fight on.
Bombardment.wants: Hard control and a defensive layer for the pair; this chassis has no mitigation of its own beyond the Fighter opener's armour and never clears rung 2 on either control axis.
uncertain: The bomb's 3m radius is modelled at 3 targets against the AoE par's 4; at 2 targets the Act I ratio still clears rung 5, so the rung is not sensitive to that choice, but the headline number is.
Salvo and Barrage are scored as unreachable per the DEFECT note in the class file (EnabledConditions want 2 and 3 Bombs, the pak grants 1).
Whether a bomb itself counts as a spell for the refill is unverified; scored as one bomb per turn alongside one spell, not one bomb per Action.

Shrapnel.split: Barbarian 1 (none) / Wizard 14 (School of Bombardment) / Bard 5 (College of Lore)
Shrapnel.note: The same bomb engine opened on Barbarian for a d12 hit die, Str+Con saves and Unarmoured Defence off Constitution rather than armour. The Rage charges are dead weight on a caster and the body stays in a robe.
Shrapnel.strength: A slot-free area attack every turn is the one damage source in the list that does not decay against +126% enemy HP, because it scales on character level and fires twice per round from Act III — and it needs no concentration, so the pair's two slots stay with the partner.
Shrapnel.wants: Anything defensive: no armour, no mitigation layer, and rung 1-2 on both control axes throughout.
uncertain: Barbarian 1 credited only for saves, hit die, Unarmoured Defence and Perception — Rage blocks spellcasting and is unusable here.
Salvo and Barrage scored as unreachable per the class file's DEFECT note; bomb target count modelled at 3.

Cerement.split: Wizard 14 (School of Death) / Monk 6 (Way of the Friar)
Cerement.note: Reaper doubles every single-target necromancy cantrip, Inescapable Destruction makes the damage ignore necrotic resistance, and Touch of Death converts Arcane Recovery charges straight into damage. It has no defensive layer of its own, which is what the six Friar levels are for.
Cerement.strength: Its damage is at-will and its damage type is the one Listo resists most, which Inescapable Destruction cancels outright — so this is the rare chassis that neither decays against +126% HP nor gets halved by Absolute Wrath, and Touch of Death spends charges that only ever bought back long-rest slots anyway.
Cerement.wants: Control and rescue; it removes enemy action points permanently and does nothing else, sitting at rung 2 or below on both control axes.
uncertain: Reaper doubles necromancy cantrips to two targets against the AoE par's four; the rung still clears because at-will two-target damage twice a round beats a once-per-fight Fireball on the ratio, but the margin in Act I is not large.

Single-target rises 1 to 3 between Acts I and II because Inescapable Destruction, Touch of Death and Negative Energy Infusion all land at Wizard 6-10 — this is a genuine back-loading body, not a scoring drift.
Perception and Persuasion are 0 in every act.

Death.split: Wizard 14 (School of Death) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Death.note: The same necrotic engine with a full-caster tail instead of a Monk one, so the slot table reaches 9th tier and Improved Reaper doubles 1st-to-5th necromancy spells rather than only cantrips. It buys skills and slots and gives up shields and the ki clock.
Death.strength: Doubling every single-target necromancy spell and cantrip is a crowd answer that costs no concentration and no short-rest charge, and the necrotic resistance bypass means it keeps working in the fights where the pair's other damage type has already been halved.
Death.wants: A durability floor — this is a robe with no mitigation at all, and with no taunt in BG3 it is the half the enemy AI will pick.
uncertain: Improved Reaper explicitly requires Expansion, which Listo has; scored as working.
College of Stormcalling is outside my read set and is credited only with caster levels, Expertise and Jack of All Trades.
Reaper's doubled cantrip is modelled at two targets against a four-target par.

Crucible.split: Wizard 11 (Transmutation) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Archfey)
Crucible.note: The thinnest of the base schools taken shallow: Transmuter's Stone at Wizard 6, remade after any Transmutation cast, and nothing else the ladder rewards. The Lore and Warlock tails are carrying most of the sheet.
Crucible.strength: The stone is one of very few cross-character buffs a Wizard can simply leave equipped on the other player — the Constitution-save variant is the cheapest concentration insurance in the class and it protects the half of the duo that is holding the pair's one spell.
Crucible.wants: Almost everything sharper than it is: a real damage engine, hard control, or a rescue kit. It is a competent generalist with no rung above 3.
uncertain: Transmuter's Stone can grant the OTHER body Constitution save proficiency, which is a real pair-scope effect with no representation in either the saves grant list or the boosters registry; it is scored only as a rung-1 outward buff on Rescue, which understates it.
Experimental Alchemy does not stack with any other source per the class file and buys nothing on these axes.

Lodestone.note: Transmutation carried to Wizard 14 with a full-caster tail, so the slot table reaches 9th tier even though the school itself contributes a stone and a blue jay. Two full-caster halves is the actual argument for this body.
Lodestone.strength: Stacking Wizard and Bard caster levels 1-for-1 means the damage half of the slot pool is upcast two tiers above a Wizard 14 with a martial dip, and the stone hands the pair's other body Constitution-save proficiency for free — which in a duo with exactly two concentration slots is worth more than the school's own features.
Lodestone.wants: A defensive layer and a lockdown tool; this chassis is a robe with no mitigation and rung 2 on both control axes from Act II.
uncertain: Transmuter's Stone's outward Constitution-save proficiency has no representation in the schema and is scored only as a rung-1 outward buff.
College of Stormcalling is outside my read set and is credited only with caster levels, Expertise and Jack of All Trades.

Parry.split: Wizard 11 (War Magic) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Archfey)
Parry.note: The gish-flavoured school that is not Bladesinging — a reaction-priced AC and save spike plus initiative, stopped at Wizard 11 so Deflecting Shroud never arrives. Its numbers are the least verified of any subclass in this batch.
Parry.strength: Its defence is a reaction, and Lone Wolf hands every body a second one, so the AC and save spike is available twice a round — which is the specific way a two-character party gets more out of reaction-priced features than a four-character one does.
Parry.wants: A body that can take a hit for it and one that deals real damage; this chassis is rung 1-2 single-target and has no armour beyond a robe.
uncertain: The class file states outright that the per-level feature table on the mod page is images-only and the numbers for Arcane Deflection, Tactical Wit, Power Surge and Durable Magic are unverified; every War Magic value here is scored on the shape of the features, not on their magnitudes.
Arcane Deflection's save bonus is not authored as a booster because no id covers a reaction-priced conditional spike.

Magic.note: War Magic taken deep enough for Deflecting Shroud, whose range was shrunk to affect everything in the radius rather than three chosen targets, with six Mercy levels adding a ki clock and Hands of Healing folded into Flurry. Unarmoured Defence is wasted on a low-Wisdom body.
Magic.strength: Two reaction-priced defensive layers on one Wizard, both usable twice a round under Lone Wolf, plus Mercy's free healing riding a bonus-action attack — outward healing that costs the pair no Action at all, in a run where Short Rest Full Heal is off and Camp Cost is 3.
Magic.wants: Crowd removal and a durability floor; it never clears rung 3 on AoE and has no armour worth the name.
uncertain: War Magic's feature magnitudes are unverified in the class file (mod page tables are images); scored on feature shape only.
Perception and Persuasion are 0 in every act — neither Wizard nor Monk lists either skill.
Way of Mercy's Flurry-borne healing lands only in Act III on this level order (Monk 3 at character 17); Flurry of Healing and Harm at Monk 11 is out of reach.

Frenzy.split: Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Barbarian 11 (Berserker) / Paladin 3 (Oath of Devotion)
Frenzy.note: A Berserker whose Frenzied Strike turns Lone Wolf's spare bonus action into a fifth swing, opened on Bard 1 for Dex+Cha saves and closed with Lore Expertise and three Paladin levels of smite fuel. It gives up Retaliation and Primal Champion — Barbarian 11 stops three levels short of the capstone the subclass is famous for.
Frenzy.strength: Frenzied Strike is the cheapest way to spend the second bonus action Lone Wolf hands out, and the Lore half makes this the rare Barbarian body that can also carry the pair's Perception and town dialogue rather than dumping both on the partner.
Frenzy.wants: A body that will hold the pair's one concentration slot and cover area control, because this one cannot cast at all while raging and sits at 0–1 on both control axes for most of the run.
uncertain: Rage disables spellcasting and concentration, so the Bard 6 and Paladin 3 slots are scored as out-of-rage and out-of-combat utility only.
Frenzied Strike credited as one extra attack per round, not two; whether Listo lets both Lone Wolf bonus actions fire it is unconfirmed.

Grimshout.split: Warlock 3 (The Fiend) / Barbarian 11 (Berserker) / Bard 6 (College of Lore)
Grimshout.note: The same Frenzy engine opened on Warlock 3 instead — Wis+Cha saves at level 1, Pact of the Chain for a third body, and two short-rest pact slots — with Lore arriving only in Act III. It pays for that opening by reaching Extra Attack at character 8 rather than 6.
Grimshout.strength: Wis+Cha from the level-1 class plus Lone Wolf's Con+Dex is the full disjoint four on the body that will be standing in front, and the Chain familiar is a third initiative slot in a party that only has two.
Grimshout.wants: Area control and a real crowd answer — this body is 0–1 on control-area in every act and its damage is single-file.
uncertain: Rage disables spellcasting, so Eldritch Blast and the pact slots are a non-raging fallback, not a routine.
Skill coverage is near-zero until Bard 1 lands at character 15; the Act I/II rungs assume the partner carries every check.

Surge.split: Barbarian 11 (Path of Wild Magic) / Warlock 3 (The Great Old One) / Wizard 6 (School of Divination)
Surge.note: A Wild Magic Barbarian that spends its late levels buying a familiar and a small arcane list it can only use out of rage. Bolstering Magic is the real payload — a free spell slot or a d3 handed to the partner every rest cycle.
Surge.strength: Magic Awareness with Goon's fix puts the proficiency bonus on *both* bodies' saves against spells, which in a two-body party is a genuine pair-wide anti-caster aura against a modlist that turned half the bestiary into wild magic sorcerers.
Surge.wants: A partner that converts resources into damage, because Bolstering Magic's donated slot is worth whatever the other body does with it.
uncertain: Bolstering Magic gifts the partner a spell slot; no axis represents a transferred resource, so it is scored as rsc 1.
Rage disables spellcasting, so the Wizard 6 list is an out-of-rage option, not the plan.

Bolster.split: Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Barbarian 11 (Path of Wild Magic) / Paladin 3 (Oath of the Ancients)
Bolster.note: Wild Magic opened on Bard for Dex+Cha saves and Lore Expertise, so the same Bolstering Magic donation arrives on a body that can also clear the run's skill checks. Damage is bare Extra Attack — the subclass buys nothing offensive.
Bolster.strength: Magic Awareness covers both bodies and Lore Expertise covers both bodies' checks, so a duo that would otherwise have no answer to either caster-heavy encounters or Perception traps gets both from one half.
Bolster.wants: A damage engine — this body is par or below on single-target in every act after the first and has no area damage at all.
uncertain: Rage disables spellcasting and concentration; the Bard and Paladin lists are out-of-rage only.

FiendWarlock.split: Barbarian 11 (Path of the Giant) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend) / Wizard 6 (School of Evocation)
FiendWarlock.note: The throwing Giant, with Elemental Cleaver's 1d6 rider on every hit and Goon's throw fixes carrying Reckless Attack and Brutal Critical onto thrown attacks. Stopping at Barbarian 11 forfeits Demiurgic Colossus, so the reach and the 2d6 Cleaver never arrive.
FiendWarlock.strength: Thrown attacks give a melee-statted body a ranged line, which is what keeps a two-character party from having to walk to every target on maps built for five.
FiendWarlock.wants: Concentration control and sustained area damage — Mighty Impel is the only multi-target thing here and it is incidental.
uncertain: Elemental Cleaver's rider is a single chosen element and takes the Absolute Wrath resistance multiplier on the rider only; the weapon dice are physical.
Rage disables spellcasting, so the Wizard 6 block is out-of-rage utility.

Hurl.split: Bard 6 (College of Swords) / Barbarian 11 (Path of the Giant) / Paladin 3 (Oath of Vengeance)
Hurl.note: The same throwing Giant opened on Bard for saves, Expertise and Jack of All Trades, then finished with three Paladin levels for smite conversion. It never reaches the level-14 capstone that makes the subclass Huge.
Hurl.strength: One body covering the thrown-damage line *and* the party's Perception and Persuasion is worth more here than in a four-person party, because there is no third character to hide a dump stat behind.
Hurl.wants: A concentration holder — this body has neither the slots nor the ability to hold a spell while raging.
uncertain: Rage disables spellcasting; Bard and Paladin casting is out-of-rage only.

Ursine.split: Paladin 3 (Oath of Devotion) / Barbarian 11 (Wildheart) / Cleric 6 (Life Domain)
Ursine.note: Bear Heart Wildheart — resistance to every damage type but psychic while raging — opened on Paladin for Wis+Cha saves and closed with six Life Cleric levels for post-fight recovery. Bestial Attunement at 14 is out of reach, so there is no taunt.
Ursine.strength: Bear Heart is proportional mitigation and therefore scale-invariant against the +126%/+170% HP inflation, and it stacks under Lone Wolf's own halving on the body enemy AI will be picking on.
Ursine.wants: Damage and crowd clear — this chassis is par on single-target and zero on area, and its whole contribution is not dying.
uncertain: Bear Heart resistance is disabled in heavy armour under Goon's, so this body stays in medium armour and forfeits the rung-3 armour line.
Rage blocks Cleric concentration; Spirit Guardians is unavailable in the configuration scored.

Ghostslayer.split: Barbarian 11 (Wildheart) / Bloodhunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer) / Bard 6 (College of Lore)
Ghostslayer.note: Bear Heart Wildheart that buys a Crimson Rite off three Blood Hunter levels — an at-will 1d4 rider with no clock — and finishes on Lore for Expertise. It gives up the Wildheart capstone and any real caster tier.
Ghostslayer.strength: Crimson Rite never amortises down and Bear Heart's resistance never decays, so this body's two signature features are both scale-invariant against the run's HP inflation while everything flat around them rots.
Ghostslayer.wants: Area control and concentration — this body has neither and cannot acquire either while raging.
uncertain: Blood Curses from a 3-level dip are scored as slot-free short-rest single-target control at rung 2; most of them carry no saving throw so low Intelligence does not sink them.
Hemocraft self-damage is a real HP cost with Short Rest Full Heal off; not represented on any axis.

Ginnung.split: Warlock 3 (The Great Old One) / Barbarian 11 (Path of Ginnungagap) / Bard 6 (College of Lore)
Ginnung.note: The dedicated anti-caster: Null Warrior's advantage on spell saves and once-per-Rage crit denial, Magic Syphoning's Constitution-check counterspell, and Spell Eater turning every made save into 2d6 back. Warlock first buys Wis+Cha and a Chain familiar; Herald of Ginnungagap at 14 is never reached.
Ginnung.strength: Listo's own balance notes say goblins, fae and Kuo-toa are now effectively wild magic sorcerers — a reaction counterspell that costs no slot and refreshes every Rage is a direct answer, and Lone Wolf's second reaction lets it fire alongside something else.
Ginnung.wants: Area damage and a crowd answer, because everything this body does is aimed at one caster at a time.
uncertain: Magic Syphoning scored as repeatable no-concentration single-target control; its Constitution check versus DC 10 + spell level is not a save-DC effect and does not decay.
rage-of-ginnungagap only applies while raging, which is also when this body cannot cast — the booster is scored at full blanket tier as the registry defines it.

Voidmaw.split: Barbarian 11 (Path of Ginnungagap) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Great Old One)
Voidmaw.note: The same Ginnungagap counter-caster taken from level 1, so Magic Syphoning and Spell Eater are both online inside Act I and Lore Expertise lands in Act II rather than Act III. It trades Wis+Cha saves for Str+Con.
Voidmaw.strength: Getting the counterspell reaction at character 6 instead of character 9 matters in a run where Act I encounters already field wild magic casters, and Lone Wolf's spare reaction means interrupting a spell costs nothing this body was using.
Voidmaw.wants: A crowd answer — area damage or area control — since this chassis is 0–1 there in every act.
uncertain: Spell Eater's 2d6-on-a-made-save is scored as self-healing under durability, not rescue.

Ancestor.split: Barbarian 11 (Path of the Ancestral Guardian) / Bloodhunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer) / Druid 6 (Circle of the Land)
Ancestor.note: Spirit Shield as the pair's standing damage-prevention layer, with Ancestral Protectors pulling fire onto the durable half, a Crimson Rite for at-will damage, and six Druid levels of out-of-rage utility. Vengeful Ancestors at 14 never arrives.
Ancestor.strength: Spirit Shield is outward damage prevention that costs a reaction — and Lone Wolf hands out a second reaction nobody else was using — so in a party of exactly two it protects the only other body, every round, off no rest resource at all.
Ancestor.wants: Damage output and crowd clear; this body's tempo is par at best and its whole value is keeping the partner alive.
uncertain: Spirit Shield is scored as rescue rung 3–4 (repeatable outward prevention, reaction cost) rather than redirection, which the rubric caps at 1.
Ancestral Protectors is a taunt-shaped effect with no booster or redirect id; it is folded into control-single 1–2.

Spiritward.split: Paladin 3 (Oath of the Ancients) / Barbarian 11 (Path of the Ancestral Guardian) / Sorcerer 6 (Divine Soul)
Spiritward.note: The Ancestral Guardian opened on Paladin for Wis+Cha and closed on Divine Soul for Twinned support that reaches the whole party because the party is two. Damage is bare Extra Attack throughout.
Spiritward.strength: A Wis+Cha+Con+Dex disjoint four on the body that eats the crits, plus Spirit Shield aimed outward every round — this is a chassis built entirely around the fact that losing either half ends the fight.
Spiritward.wants: Tempo: something that removes enemy action points permanently, because this body barely clears par on one target and does nothing to a crowd.
uncertain: Sorcerer 6 reaches only 3rd-level slots, so Twinned Death Ward and Twinned Greater Restoration are out of range; rescue is scored on Twinned Cure Wounds and Spirit Shield.

Talon.split: Warlock 3 (The Fiend) / Barbarian 11 (Path of the Beast) / Bard 6 (College of Valour)
Talon.note: Claws Form of the Beast: an extra claw attack on every Attack action, so six swings a round with Lone Wolf's two Actions, plus Infectious Fury turning an enemy's reaction against its own side. It forfeits shields and dual-wield entirely, and Call the Hunt at 14 is out of reach.
Talon.strength: Six attacks a round off two Actions is the cleanest use of Lone Wolf's doubled economy in this file, and Infectious Fury's reaction-steal is one of the few things a two-body party can do to enemy action economy without spending a slot.
Talon.wants: Area damage and a concentration holder; this chassis is 0 on area damage in Act I and Act II and cannot concentrate while raging.
uncertain: Claws require an empty hand in both weapon sets, so no shield: durability is scored on Unarmoured Defence plus Rage resistance, not medium armour and shield.
The class file warns a Hasted extra Action starts a new Attack action and forfeits the bonus claw; Haste is assumed off.

Maul.split: Barbarian 11 (Path of the Beast) / Bard 6 (College of Valour) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend)
Maul.note: The same six-attack claw engine started at level 1, so Str+Con saves and Infectious Fury both land earlier and Valour Expertise arrives in Act II. It still stops three levels short of Call the Hunt.
Maul.strength: The claw attack rides the Attack action rather than a bonus action, so it is the one melee engine here that does not compete with Rage for Lone Wolf's spare bonus action — the whole economy converts to swings.
Maul.wants: A crowd answer: this body deletes one target at a time and has nothing for the extra bodies Listo's encounter mods add.
uncertain: No shield with Claws; durability rests on Unarmoured Defence and Rage resistance.

Immovable.split: Warlock 3 (The Undead) / Barbarian 11 (Path of the Juggernaut) / Bard 6 (College of Lore)
Immovable.note: A Juggernaut run as an actual tank — Resolute Stance held on, imposing disadvantage on every attack against it and paying for that with disadvantage on its own. The damage row is scored with the stance on, which is why it reads below par from Act II.
Immovable.strength: Imposing disadvantage on every incoming attack, on demand, with no resource, is how one of two characters absorbs an encounter tuned for five — and the cost lands on the axis the *other* player was covering anyway.
Immovable.wants: Damage, plainly: this body sits at 1–2 on single-target and 0–1 on area, and it is the partner's job to convert the safety into kills.
uncertain: Resolute Stance is scored as on for roughly four of five rounds, giving a 0.82 multiplier on damage; the rubric's one-configuration rule forced a choice and this is the tanking configuration.
Hurricane Strike granting the partner a reaction attack is scored on actions, not on this body's tempo.

Bulwark.split: Barbarian 11 (Path of the Juggernaut) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Undead)
Bulwark.note: The same Resolute Stance tank taken from level 1 for Str+Con and Barbarian Perception, with Lore Expertise arriving in Act II instead of Act III. Same trade: near-immunity to being hit, bought with its own accuracy.
Bulwark.strength: It is the only body here that can both tank an encounter with a no-resource toggle and carry the pair's Perception, which in a two-character party is the difference between eating every trap and seeing them.
Bulwark.wants: A partner that converts the bought time into damage — this chassis is the lowest single-target row in the batch.
uncertain: Same Resolute Stance multiplier as Immovable; if the stance is only used situationally the single-target row rises to 3/2/2.

Fulgurant.split: Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling) / Barbarian 14 (Path of the Lightning Vessel)
Fulgurant.note: The only Barbarian in this batch with a real area engine: Fulgurant Strike splashing 2×Con lightning off every melee hit and Roaring Crash opening the fight with a (Con)d8 leap, rising to 3×Con at the level-14 capstone. Bard 1 buys Dex+Cha and the College lands only in Act III.
Fulgurant.strength: At-will splash damage that costs an interrupt rather than a slot is the crowd answer a Barbarian normally cannot have, and Roaring Crash is a 30–60 ft gap-closer on a battlefield two characters have to cover alone.
Fulgurant.wants: A body that holds concentration and answers bosses, because the lightning is spread thin and Absolute Wrath resists it on roughly half the encounter list.
uncertain: Listo applies an unpublished CD nerf patch to this subclass that is not in the manifest; every damage figure here is the unmodified mod's and is therefore an upper bound.
Lightning is commonly resisted; the area row already carries a 0.75 multiplier from Act II for that.
All three Galvanic Heart powers and Rage itself compete for bonus actions until Lightning Reflexes at Barbarian 10.

Tempest.split: Barbarian 14 (Path of the Lightning Vessel) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Tempest.note: The same lightning chassis opened on Barbarian for Str+Con and a Perception proficiency, so Electric Beast lands at character 14 and the Stormcalling College is a pure Act III addition. Concentration is never on the table.
Tempest.strength: Two Actions each carrying a Fulgurant interrupt means the splash fires twice a round, which turns Listo's inflated enemy counts from a liability into the thing this body is best against.
Tempest.wants: Boss-shaped tempo and a concentration slot — the single-target row falls to par by Act III and the lightning does not care how big one target is.
uncertain: Same unverified CD nerf patch as Fulgurant — treat the area rung as an upper bound.
Lightning Reflexes' +Con to Dexterity checks helps lockpicking and trap disarm, which the three scored skills do not capture.

Wraith.split: Warlock 3 (The Undead) / Barbarian 11 (Path of the Revenant) / Bard 6 (College of Lore)
Wraith.note: Heavy armour from Ghost Armor, physical resistance and a flat −2 on every incoming hit, plus Haunt frightening a target and mirroring damage back onto it. The price is absolute: while the rage is up it cannot be healed by any means and cannot be ended.
Wraith.strength: Flat −2 under Rage's physical resistance under Lone Wolf's halving is the deepest stack of mitigation in this file, and Haunt is repeatable no-concentration control that costs only the bonus action Lone Wolf duplicated.
Wraith.wants: A partner whose contribution is not healing — this body invalidates outward healing entirely, so the other half must pay its way in tempo or control.
uncertain: "Cannot be healed by any means" is a hard anti-synergy with any rescue-carrying partner and has no representation on any axis; it should be read as a pairing constraint.
Charm/Fear/Poison/Disease immunity while raging has no booster id and is not scored.

Barrow.split: Barbarian 11 (Path of the Revenant) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Undead)
Barrow.note: The Revenant taken from level 1, so heavy armour and DR 2 arrive at character 3 and Haunt at character 6 — the whole defensive and control package is live inside Act I. It trades Wis+Cha saves for Str+Con and the same no-healing clause applies.
Barrow.strength: A body that is functionally unkillable by weapon damage from Act I, in a run where a single death ends the fight, and it pays for itself offensively by mirroring everything it absorbs back onto the Haunted target.
Barrow.wants: Everything aimed at a crowd, and a partner who will not waste levels on healing this body cannot receive.
uncertain: Same no-healing constraint as Wraith.
Gravemarch's stacking max HP on Haunted kills is scored inside the durability rung rather than as a separate effect.

Tundra.split: Wizard 5 (School of Divination) / Barbarian 14 (Path of the Storm Herald) / Monk 1 (none)
Tundra.note: Tundra Storm Aura re-triggered as a bonus action every turn, feeding the partner temp HP and sharing cold resistance from level 10, with Raging Storm's speed-zero rider at 14. Wizard 5 buys Int+Wis saves and a small list; the single Monk level is a stat filler and grants no subclass.
Tundra.strength: A temp-HP stream and a shared resistance that cost no rest resource at all, in a party that cannot afford 120-supply long rests — and with only two bodies both are always inside the 10 ft aura.
Tundra.wants: Tempo of any kind; this chassis is par on single-target, near-zero on area, and its output is entirely defensive.
uncertain: Tundra's temp HP is 4–5 per turn at these levels, far below Twilight Sanctuary; rescue is scored at 3 on the clock, not the size.
The Monk 1 level is below subclass level and contributes only Unarmoured Defence, which Barbarian already supplies.
Rage disables spellcasting, so the Wizard list is out-of-rage only.

Rimesong.split: Wizard 6 (Bladesinging) / Barbarian 14 (Path of the Storm Herald)
Rimesong.note: The same Tundra aura with six Bladesinging levels instead of five Divination ones, adding Bladesong's +2 AC and +2 Constitution saves in Act III. Bladesong and Rage are alternatives rather than a stack, so this body picks a mode per fight.
Rimesong.strength: Int+Wis from Wizard 1 plus Lone Wolf's Con+Dex is a disjoint four covering every save that ends a two-person fight, and the aura keeps both bodies topped up between them for free.
Rimesong.wants: Damage and crowd clear — the whole chassis is a mitigation aura with a par attack routine attached.
uncertain: Bladesinging wants Intelligence and light armour while Storm Herald wants Constitution and Rage; the two halves are scored as alternating configurations, which the one-configuration rule strictly disallows — this is the doubt.
Perception is 0 in every act; this body cannot see a trap.

Fury.split: Paladin 3 (Oath of Vengeance) / Barbarian 11 (Path of the Zealot) / Cleric 6 (War Domain)
Fury.note: Divine Fury adding 1d6 plus half Barbarian level to the first hit each turn, Fanatical Focus rerolling a failed save every Rage, and Warrior of the Gods letting the partner pick this body up without a scroll. Rage Beyond Death at 14 is out of reach.
Fury.strength: A save reroll per Rage rather than per rest is enormous on a duo with two save sets and no third body to cover a failure, and Warrior of the Gods removes the scroll tax on the run's actual failure mode.
Fury.wants: A crowd answer and a concentration holder; Divine Fury is once per turn and this body has nothing that touches more than one enemy.
uncertain: Divine Fury scales with Barbarian level only, so stopping at 11 caps it at +1d6+5 once per turn.
Warrior of the Gods is inward rescue (the partner revives this body) and is deliberately not scored on rsc.

Deathless.split: Barbarian 11 (Path of the Zealot) / Bloodhunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer) / Bard 6 (College of Lore)
Deathless.note: Zealot from level 1, so Divine Fury scales as deep as the split allows, with a Crimson Rite bolted on for an at-will rider and Lore for the pair's skill coverage. Rage Beyond Death is three levels away.
Deathless.strength: Two riders that both ignore the rest clock — Divine Fury every turn and Crimson Rite until long rest — on a body whose saves reroll once per Rage, which is exactly the shape a duo needs against three hard fights per 120-supply cycle.
Deathless.wants: Area control or area damage; this chassis is 0–1 on both in every act.
uncertain: Crimson Rite at Blood Hunter 3 is a 1d4 hemocraft die; it never grows because the dip never deepens.

Dawn.split: Bloodhunter 11 (Order of the Ghostslayer) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend)
Dawn.note: Rite of the Dawn's Radiant rite doubled by Brand of Sundering at 11, four Blood Maledicts from level 3, and Aether Walk for intangibility. It stops seven levels short of Rite Revival and never reaches a real spell tier.
Dawn.strength: Crimson Rite is at-will with no clock, so this body's damage rider is the one thing in the file that does not amortise down against three fights per long rest — and Radiant is among the least resisted types once Absolute Wrath layers the rest.
Dawn.wants: Area damage; this chassis is 0–1 on aoe in every act and its control is all single-target curses.
uncertain: Blood Maledict is scored at rung 3–4 on control-single as slot-free short-rest hard control; most curses carry no save, so the low spell DC does not sink them.
Brand of Sundering requires the Brand to be placed first, costing a charge and an action on the opening turn.

Sunward.split: Sorcerer 6 (Divine Soul) / Bloodhunter 11 (Order of the Ghostslayer) / Paladin 3 (Oath of Devotion)
Sunward.note: The Ghostslayer opened on Divine Soul for Con+Cha saves and a Twinned support suite, closed with three Paladin levels for smite conversion off the sorcerer slots. The caster half arrives late — Sorcerer 2–6 lands in Act II and III.
Sunward.strength: Twinned Spell covers the entire party when the party is two, so one Sorcerer 3's worth of Metamagic buys the pair-wide buffs a four-body group would need a dedicated caster for, on a body that also carries an at-will Radiant rite.
Sunward.wants: A crowd answer and a body willing to hold the pair's concentration if this one is smiting instead.
uncertain: Sorcerer 6 reaches 3rd-level slots only, so Twinned Death Ward is out of range and rescue tops out at Twinned Cure Wounds plus Lay on Hands.
Sorcery points scale on Sorcerer class level only — six points is thin fuel for Twinning every fight.

Moonblood.split: Sorcerer 6 (Draconic Bloodline) / Bloodhunter 11 (Order of the Lycan) / Warlock 3 (The Hexblade)
Moonblood.note: Hybrid Transformation's Dex-scaling unarmed strikes with an unarmed Crimson Rite, six swings a round off Lone Wolf's doubled bonus actions, Resilient Hide's resistance and Lycan Regeneration from 11. Bloodlust is live and unmitigated until level 15, which this split never reaches.
Moonblood.strength: The highest raw single-target row in this batch, and the rite that drives it is at-will — against +170% boss HP the pair needs a body whose damage does not thin out over three fights.
Moonblood.wants: Crowd clear, and a partner who can pull this body out of a Bloodlust turn rather than one standing next to it.
uncertain: Bloodlust — a failed Wisdom save below half HP turns this body on its partner — is a structural risk in a two-body party with no representation on any axis.
Heightened Senses grants advantage on Perception, which the flat modifier does not capture.

Feral.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Zealot) / Bloodhunter 11 (Order of the Lycan) / Wizard 6 (School of Evocation)
Feral.note: The Lycan unarmed engine opened on Barbarian for Str+Con, Reckless Attack and Danger Sense, with Divine Fury adding a rider and Wizard 6 arriving as Act III utility. Rage and pact-free casting are mutually exclusive, so the arcane half only runs out of Rage.
Feral.strength: Six unarmed strikes a round with an at-will rite, under Rage's physical resistance and Resilient Hide's, on a body whose saves reroll once per Rage — it is the batch's rare chassis that is top-tier on tempo and still hard to remove.
Feral.wants: Area control; this body has none of its own and its Wizard levels land too late to be a plan.
uncertain: Barbarian 2–3 lands at characters 13–14, so danger-sense and fanatical-focus are unavailable in Act I.
Rage's damage bonus applies to Strength melee attacks; the Dex-scaled Predatory Strikes are scored without it.
Bloodlust risk as on Moonblood.

Mutagen.split: Bloodhunter 11 (Order of the Mutant) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Great Old One)
Mutagen.note: Celerity and Cruelty held together from Blood Hunter 7 — a raw ability-score boost plus an extra attack after any attack — with Lore Expertise for the pair's checks. Cruelty's price is disadvantage on Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma saves, which is the worst save band to give up here.
Mutagen.strength: Mutagens run on a short-rest clock against a run where long rests cost 120+ supplies, and Listo removed the ability-score cap, so Celerity is a permanent stat rather than a temporary one.
Mutagen.wants: A partner who covers Wisdom and Charisma saves for the pair, because Cruelty deliberately throws this body's away.
uncertain: Cruelty's disadvantage on Int/Wis/Cha saves has no negative booster id; the saves block therefore overstates this body and the penalty is recorded only here.
Cruelty read as one extra attack per turn, not per attack; the mutagen text is ambiguous.

Alembic.split: Sorcerer 6 (Wild Magic) / Bloodhunter 11 (Order of the Mutant) / Paladin 3 (Oath of the Ancients)
Alembic.note: The cautious Mutant: Celerity for the stat and Reconstruction for the self-healing, no Cruelty and no vulnerability trades, with Sorcerer 6 and Paladin 3 layered on for Twinned support and smites. It gives up the highest-damage mutagen line for a body that does not hand out liabilities.
Alembic.strength: Strange Metabolism's poison immunity and a short-rest self-heal on a body that also Twins its buffs across a two-person party — every mutagen and every pact-shaped resource here refreshes faster than the long rest this run cannot afford.
Alembic.wants: Crowd clear and a real area engine; its damage is par-shaped and it has nothing for the extra bodies Listo's encounter mods add.
uncertain: Strange Metabolism's poison immunity is a large defensive swing with no axis representation; it sits inside the durability rung.
Celerity is credited as +1 Dex modifier in Act I and +2 from Act II under Improved Mutagencraft.

Sapping.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of Ginnungagap) / Bloodhunter 11 (Order of the Profane Soul) / Cleric 6 (War Domain)
Sapping.note: Brand of the Sapping Scar at Blood Hunter 11 — blanket Disadvantage on the branded creature's saves, delivered by a free interrupt with no concentration — over Int-based pact magic on a short-rest clock, with a Ginnungagap dip for spell-save advantage and six War Cleric levels late. It is a support body first and a damage body second.
Sapping.strength: The pair holds exactly two concentration slots; Sapping Scar makes the partner's one spell land without spending either, which is the single best boss-fight lever available to a two-character party.
Sapping.wants: A body with a real control list to point at the branded target, because this chassis manufactures the opening and cannot exploit it alone.
uncertain: Rage and pact casting are mutually exclusive; the body is scored as a caster that rages only in weapon-only fights, so rage-of-ginnungagap is credited at its registry tier but is not always on.
Spirit Guardians would raise the Act III area row to 3 but would consume this body's concentration; the scored configuration keeps the slot for control.

Scarbrand.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Zealot) / Bloodhunter 11 (Order of the Profane Soul) / Wizard 6 (Bladesinging)
Scarbrand.note: The same Sapping Scar interrupt, opened on Zealot for Divine Fury and a save reroll per Rage and closed with six Bladesinging levels for AC, Constitution saves and a genuine 3rd-tier control list in Act III. It never becomes a primary caster — pact slots cap at spell level 2 here.
Scarbrand.strength: Blanket Disadvantage on a boss's saves with no concentration cost, on the same body that then casts the control spell — in a duo that owns two slots total, holding the debuff and the payload on one character frees the partner entirely.
Scarbrand.wants: Sustained damage and a crowd answer; this chassis buys openings and does not close them, and its rescue row is 0 in every act.
uncertain: Bladesong requires no shield and no medium armour, which conflicts with the Blood Hunter frame; Act III durability assumes Bladesong is used in caster-facing fights only.
Profane Soul spell DCs key off Intelligence, so this build carries Int 18 at the cost of Constitution.

Solstice.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Revenant) / Druid 11 (Circle of Dreams) / Cleric 6 (Life Domain)
Solstice.note: A heavy-armoured Dreams healer that spends its bonus actions on Balm of the Summer Court and its concentration on Sleet Storm; it gives up almost all damage to do so. Barbarian 1 buys Str+Con saves and a d12 die, Revenant buys the armour and a flat DR 2, Life buys Death Ward and Disciple of Life late.
Solstice.strength: Balm is a long-rest pool equal to Druid level spent in one bonus action on the other body, and Lone Wolf hands this chassis two bonus actions a round to spend it with; Hearth of Moonlight maximises every die, so a duo that loses half its action economy the moment one body drops gets the cheapest possible insurance against that.
Solstice.wants: A body that removes enemies, because this one's single-target and area damage sit at 0-2 and it can only keep the other half alive while that half kills things.
uncertain: Path of the Revenant taken from the barbarian dip list (heavy armour + DR 2 at 3); its Listo level table was not in my read range.
Level order assumed Barbarian 1-3 at characters 1-3, Druid to 14, Cleric 6 last, so the Life domain lands only in Act III.
Act III rsc 5 leans on Death Ward (Life) plus a 17-die Balm pool plus Greater Restoration; drop it to 4 if Hearth's max-healing clause does not apply to Balm's temp HP half.

Lullaby.split: Fighter 1 (none) / Druid 14 (Circle of Dreams) / Warlock 5 (The Fiend)
Lullaby.note: A Dreams druid wearing Fighter 1's heavy armour, with Warlock 5 bolted on for Eldritch Blast, two short-rest pact slots and Pact of the Chain. Its concentration goes to area control, so its own damage never rises above a chip.
Lullaby.strength: Walker in Dreams at Druid 14 is a free short rest once per long rest and Hidden Paths is a bonus-action extraction for the partner — both priced against a 120-supply camp and a party that cannot spare a body, and neither costs an Action.
Lullaby.wants: A body that carries the pair's damage on both fight types; this one is 1 on single-target and 2 on area in every act.
uncertain: Eldritch Blast scored at Cha 12 (+1) — this is a Wisdom body, so Agonizing Blast returns far less than the rubric's Cha-22 worked example (44 raw at four beams, 0.58x par).
Patron chosen as The Fiend; no warlock subclass text was in my read range, only the dip section.

Stormcalling.split: Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling) / Druid 14 (Circle of Stormchasers)
Stormcalling.note: A lightning engine: Storm Shift adds Wisdom to every Lightning roll and hands back 3x Druid level in temp HP for one Wild Shape charge, and Call Lightning is retriggered every round off one slot. The Bard levels arrive last and buy Song of Rest, short-rest Inspiration and two Expertises rather than casting.
Stormcalling.strength: Circle level 10 makes its Lightning ignore Resistance and treat Immunity as Resistance, which is the only clean answer in this batch to Absolute Wrath's layered resistances on a two-body party that cannot carry a second damage type; Chain Lightning at 14 adds a per-long-rest crowd finisher.
Stormcalling.wants: A body that can lock down a single boss, because this one's control-single sits at 1 in every act and its concentration is already spent on damage.
uncertain: Call Lightning scored at 2 targets, not the rubric's 4 — its radius is 3m against Fireball's 6m. At 4 targets every Call Lightning row in this batch rises a full rung.
College of Stormcalling's own features were not in my read range; the Bard 6 block is scored as generic Bard (Song of Rest, Font of Inspiration, Expertise x2, Countercharm).
Level order assumed Bard 1 at character 1 then Bard 2-6 at 16-20, so Expertise lands only in Act III.

AoE re-banded to the rubric's fixed 4-target convention (axis-rubrics.md, Constants). Authored at 2 targets on Call Lightning's 3m radius; the radius point is real but is a rubric-wide change, not a per-batch one.

Stormchasers.note: The same Storm Shift lightning engine in heavy armour and a shield from War domain at level 1, with War Priest bonus-action swings between casts. It pays for the armour with the Charisma trap — Cleric 1's Wis+Cha grant forces Lone Wolf's +4 onto Con and Dex instead of the primary.
Stormchasers.strength: Heavy armour plus a 42-point Storm Shift pool plus level-14 resistance to Lightning, Thunder and Cold means the pair's Personal durability minimum is not set here, which is what a no-taunt duo with Enemy Critical Hits on actually needs from a caster.
Stormchasers.wants: Skill coverage — no Perception or Investigation proficiency anywhere on this body, and its Persuasion is a Charisma 12 dump.
uncertain: Call Lightning scored at 2 targets (see Squall).
Level order assumed Cleric 1 at character 1 and Cleric 2-6 at 16-20, so the second short-rest Channel Divinity charge and War's tier-2 feature land only in Act III.
Wisdom 22 by character 18 assumed reachable without Lone Wolf's +4 (point buy 17 plus two ASI half-feats plus a gate); tight against a 7-feat budget.

AoE re-banded to the rubric's fixed 4-target convention (axis-rubrics.md, Constants). Authored at 2 targets on Call Lightning's 3m radius; the radius point is real but is a rubric-wide change, not a per-batch one.

Ember.split: Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling) / Druid 14 (Circle of Wildfire)
Ember.note: An action-economy chassis: the Wildfire Spirit is a permanent extra body that also casts this druid's spells from its own position, stacked on Conjure Animals made non-concentration until long rest by 13458. Its personal damage is deliberately thin.
Ember.strength: A second point of origin for area spells is something a two-character party otherwise cannot generate at all, and Blazing Revival is an automatic second life in a run where losing either body ends the fight; both are worth more here than the fire damage attached to them.
Ember.wants: Single-target burst against bosses — this body is 1 on that axis in every act and its summons add crowd pressure, not boss pressure.
uncertain: Cauterizing Flames and Blazing Revival levels are flagged (unverified) in the class file; I placed Blazing Revival in Act II, which is what carries dur from 2 to 3.
Call Lightning scored at 2 targets (see Squall).
College of Stormcalling's features were not in my read range.

AoE re-banded to the rubric's fixed 4-target convention (axis-rubrics.md, Constants). Authored at 2 targets on Call Lightning's 3m radius; the radius point is real but is a rubric-wide change, not a per-batch one.

Fiend.split: Warlock 5 (The Fiend) / Druid 14 (Circle of Wildfire) / Monk 1 (none)
Fiend.note: The Wildfire body count assembled out of three short-rest pools — Warlock's two 3rd-level pact slots, Wild Shape charges, and a Chain familiar — with Monk 1 for Unarmoured Defence off Wisdom and a bonus-action strike. It never reaches a real damage rung on either axis.
Fiend.strength: Everything on this chassis refills on a short rest, which is the clock that matters when a long rest costs 120+ supplies, and the Wildfire Spirit plus the pact familiar plus Conjure Animals put four initiative slots on the field for a party of two.
Fiend.wants: A body that holds a real concentration control spell and a boss-killing routine; this one is 1 on control-single and 1 on single-target throughout.
uncertain: Monk 1 taken after level 1 grants no saves; Unarmoured Defence assumed to work, but this body wants medium armour from the Druid side, so the Monk level is scored as a bonus-action strike only.
Patron chosen as The Fiend; no warlock subclass text was in my read range.

Rime2.split: Warlock 5 (The Fiend) / Druid 14 (Circle of Winter) / Fighter 1 (none)
Rime2.note: Winter Spirit adds Wisdom as bonus Cold damage to every damage-dealing Druid spell and cantrip and hands back 5x Druid level in temp HP, so one Wild Shape charge buys both the damage rider and the HP bar; Fighter 1 supplies heavy armour and Druidic Warrior, Warlock 5 supplies short-rest slots and a Chain familiar.
Rime2.strength: From Druid 10 anything that fails a save against one of its Cold spells falls Prone — area control generated by damage it was casting anyway, so it costs neither of the pair's two concentration slots, which is exactly the rung-4 clause the duo cap makes expensive for everyone else.
Rime2.wants: Out-of-combat coverage and a face: this body rolls a flat +1 Persuasion and has no Perception proficiency at all, so the partner has to carry every untelegraphed check.
uncertain: Winter Spirit's +Wis assumed to apply per damage instance (i.e. per target), not once per cast; per-cast would cost the aoe row a rung.
Call Lightning scored at 2 targets (see Squall).
Circle of Winter's damage is Cold-plus-Lightning, so no Absolute Wrath resistance multiplier applied; a Cold-only configuration would take the 0.5 share penalty from Act II.

AoE re-banded to the rubric's fixed 4-target convention (axis-rubrics.md, Constants). Authored at 2 targets on Call Lightning's 3m radius; the radius point is real but is a rubric-wide change, not a per-batch one.

Hoarfrost.split: Bard 6 (College of Swords) / Druid 14 (Circle of Winter)
Hoarfrost.note: A Winter druid that actually swings: Shillelagh off Wisdom, Winter Spirit's +1d6 Cold on every melee hit, and College of Swords supplying medium armour and an Extra Attack in the last five levels. It gives up the Bard's casting entirely — those levels are armour, blade flourishes and Expertise.
Hoarfrost.strength: Two Actions means the Extra Attack is four swings a round each carrying the Cold rider, and Winter's 70-point temp HP pool plus level-14 Cold immunity keeps the melee half of a two-body party from being the Personal minimum that decides the pair's durability.
Hoarfrost.wants: A partner who can answer a single hard boss, because everything this body brings to control is crowd-shaped Prone and its control-single never exceeds 3.
uncertain: College of Swords assumed to grant Extra Attack at Bard 6 as in vanilla BG3; the bard subclass text was not in my read range.
Level order puts Bard 2-6 at characters 16-20, so Extra Attack and Expertise are Act III only; a front-loaded Bard block would raise Act I st and skl and lower Act II ctrl_a.
Winter Spirit's +Wis assumed per damage instance (see Rime).

Cataclysm.split: Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling) / Druid 14 (Circle of Wrath)
Cataclysm.note: Aspects of Wrath is a self-contained damage engine that needs no summons, no gear and no concentration — stacks capped at the Wisdom modifier add flat spell damage, and Revelations dump them per Wild Shape charge. That frees the concentration slot entirely for Sleet Storm or Confusion, which is the configuration scored here.
Cataclysm.strength: Holding real area control while still dealing damage is the one thing the pair's two-concentration-slot ceiling makes scarce, and Wrath's level-14 shared elemental immunity plus surface clearing directly fixes a two-body party standing in its own AoE.
Cataclysm.wants: A body with a durability floor above rung 2, because this one is a robe caster and Personal takes the minimum — its 2 is the pair's 2.
uncertain: Circle of Wrath's documentation stops at level 14; 15-20 is flagged (unverified) in the class file, so the Act III rows assume nothing new lands.
Revelation spells assumed to be area effects on 4 targets, twice per fight off Wild Shape charges; if they are single-target the aoe row drops a rung and st rises.

Ruin.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Revenant) / Druid 11 (Circle of Wrath) / Cleric 6 (Tempest Domain)
Ruin.note: The damage-forward Wrath configuration: concentration spent on Call Lightning, retriggered every round, with Tempest's Destructive Wrath maximising two of those bolts per fight and Wrath stacks adding flat damage on top. Revenant's heavy armour and flat DR 2 pay for standing still to do it, and Druid stops at 11 so the top spell tier never arrives.
Ruin.strength: Two short-rest Channel Divinity charges is two maximised Lightning casts every fight rather than two a day, which against +126% enemy HP is the difference between a burst and a clock; the armour and DR keep the caster from being the softer body the AI selects for in a party with no taunt.
Ruin.wants: Anything aimed outward — this body's rescue tops out at 3 and it has no prevention, so the partner has to be the one that does not need picking up.
uncertain: Destructive Wrath assumed to maximise Call Lightning's dice, twice per fight at Cleric 6's two short-rest charges; the domain's exact Listo wording was not in my read range.
Call Lightning scored at 2 targets (see Squall); at 4 the Act III aoe would reach 5.
Path of the Revenant taken from the barbarian dip list; Barbarian rage is unusable on a caster, so only the armour and DR are scored.

AoE re-banded to the rubric's fixed 4-target convention (axis-rubrics.md, Constants). Authored at 2 targets on Call Lightning's 3m radius; the radius point is real but is a rubric-wide change, not a per-batch one.

Wellspring.split: Barbarian 1 (none) / Druid 14 (Circle of the Land) / Warlock 5 (The Fiend)
Wellspring.note: A Land druid built to never long-rest: Natural Recovery refunds slots on a short rest, two 3rd-level pact slots come back on the same clock, and Barbarian 1 buys Str+Con saves, a d12 die and Unarmoured Defence off Constitution. It has essentially no damage of its own.
Wellspring.strength: A long rest costs 120+ supplies and Short Rest Full Heal is off, so a body whose spell budget partly refills between fights raises the pair's Duration block directly — and Endurance is Personal, meaning the pair rests when either half runs dry, so this is the half that stops being the reason.
Wellspring.wants: A damage body on both fight types; this one is 0-1 single-target and 2 on area, and it is spending its concentration on control rather than on either.
uncertain: Natural Recovery charge growth read as 2/3/5/7 from the class file; the exact slot-level cap it refunds at Druid 14 was not stated, and end 4 depends on it covering roughly a fight's worth.
Barbarian 1 grants no Danger Sense (that is Barbarian 2), so no booster is authored here.
Eldritch Blast scored at Cha 12 (see Lullaby).

Coppice.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Revenant) / Druid 14 (Circle of the Land) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend)
Coppice.note: The armoured version of the same idea — Revenant's heavy armour and flat DR 2 in front of Natural Recovery, with the Warlock dip cut to 3 for Pact of the Chain, 2nd-level pact slots and the feat-neutral stopping point. It trades Wellspring's third beam and 3rd-level pact slots for a durability rung.
Coppice.strength: With no taunt in BG3 the AI picks the softer body, and Personal durability takes the minimum, so putting the slot-refunding caster in heavy armour with flat reduction is what stops the pair's floor being set here — flat DR is also worth double behind Lone Wolf's halving against Listo's added small enemies.
Coppice.wants: A partner that answers single targets and holds nothing back for the second fight, since this body's resource clock is what buys those long fights.
uncertain: dur falls 4 to 3 across the acts because Revenant's DR 2 is flat-only mitigation, which the rubric sits a rung below its raw numbers in a boss-weighted Act III.
Natural Recovery scaling (see Wellspring).
Path of the Revenant taken from the barbarian dip list.

Pelt.split: Cleric 6 (War Domain) / Druid 14 (Circle of the Moon)
Pelt.note: A Moon druid that fights in beast form for the whole encounter — Wild Shape Overhaul keeps War Priest's bonus-action attacks and the heavy armour proficiency working inside the form, and Combat Wild Shape is a bonus action twice per short rest. Casting is the price: this body has no area damage and no control worth the name.
Pelt.strength: Wild Shape is a second HP bar refreshed on the short-rest clock rather than the 120-supply one, and in a duo where losing either body usually ends the fight, a spare pool the enemy has to chew through twice is worth more than the numbers it adds.
Pelt.wants: Everything ranged — this body is 1 on area damage and 1 on both control axes, so the partner has to be the entire crowd answer.
uncertain: Beast-form damage taken as roughly par: 2 attacks per Action from Wild Shape Extra Attack at Druid 5, with the level-10 second Extra Attack removed by the overhaul, so the row is frozen and holds rung 2 only because 4 attacks is exactly what par is.
Whether War Priest's bonus-action attack fires inside Wild Shape rests on the overhaul's 'multiclass features keep working' claim in the class file.
Druid 13-20 progression is flagged (unverified) in the class file.

Moon.split: Cleric 6 (Zeal Domain) / Druid 14 (Circle of the Moon)
Moon.note: The same beast-form body with Zeal instead of War: a bonus-action attack Wisdom times per long rest rather than three, and Consuming Fervor at Cleric 6 to maximise a Fire or Thunder blast on the rounds it drops form. It is a hybrid rather than a committed shapeshifter, and pays for that in consistency.
Moon.strength: Consuming Fervor is Channel Divinity twice per short rest, so a maximised Thunderwave upcast onto four bodies is a per-fight burst rather than a per-day one — and it is the only crowd answer this chassis has, since nothing in beast form touches more than one enemy.
Moon.wants: A body that holds the pair's concentration and covers control, because this one deliberately holds none and reads 1 on both control axes in every act.
uncertain: Consuming Fervor is named in axis-rubrics as Cleric 6 Channel Divinity on Fire or Thunder; I have assumed the Zeal domain carries it and that a Druid's upcast Thunderwave is a legal target. If either is wrong the Act III aoe 3 falls to 1.
Cleric 2-6 assumed to land at characters 16-20, so Consuming Fervor exists only in Act III.
Beast-form damage assumptions as for Pelt.

Undertow.split: Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling) / Druid 14 (Circle of the Sea)
Undertow.note: Wrath of the Sea is a 10-turn current that costs a Wild Shape charge rather than concentration, and Crashing Wave pushes a target 5m for Wisdom-many d6 of Cold every turn off a bonus action. That leaves the concentration slot free for Sleet Storm and then Evard's Black Tentacles, which is the configuration scored here.
Undertow.strength: Forced movement every single turn at no concentration cost is the cheapest way in this batch to peel something off the other body, and a two-person party has no third character to do the peeling; Oceanic Gift at Druid 14 then projects the whole current onto the partner for one charge.
Undertow.wants: Sustained single-target pressure on bosses, because this body's damage is a 2 that comes mostly from a bonus action and its area control decays to 2 by Act III.
uncertain: Crashing Wave assumed once per turn despite Lone Wolf's second bonus action; if it can fire twice, st rises a rung in Act II and III.

ctrl_s falls 4 to 3 because a 5m push is act-relative rung-4 material in Act I but sits below Act II's Brand-of-the-Sapping-Scar par; ctrl_a falls to 2 in Act III because Evard's is only 4th tier against a 6th-9th par.
College of Stormcalling's features were not in my read range.

Riptide.split: Rogue 3 (Swashbuckler) / Druid 11 (Circle of the Sea) / Bard 6 (College of Lore)
Riptide.note: The skills body of this batch: Rogue 1 opens with four proficiencies and two Expertises, College of Lore adds three more and two Expertises again, and Swashbuckler lets Sneak Attack land without an adjacent ally. Druid stops at 11, so Oceanic Gift and the top spell tier never arrive.
Riptide.strength: Use Highest Modifier in dialogue hands the party-best total to the host, so one body carrying four Expertises covers the pair's whole untelegraphed check load — and with only two characters there is no third proficiency set to fall back on when a trap or a secret door fires unannounced.
Riptide.wants: A body that can hold a heavy durability floor, because this one is medium armour at best and Personal durability takes the pair's minimum.
uncertain: Rogue 1-3 assumed at characters 1-3 so both Expertises are live from Act I; Bard 2-6 assumed at 15-20, so Jack of All Trades and the Lore Expertises land in Act III.
Investigation Expertise costed at Intelligence 12 (+1); a lower Int drops that row by 1 in every act.
Crashing Wave assumed once per turn (see Undertow).

Totem.split: Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling) / Druid 14 (Circle of the Shepherd)
