Totem.note: Every Shepherd totem is an aura aimed at somebody else — Bear's temp HP equal to 5 plus Druid level, Hawk's reaction advantage, Flumph spreading every heal — layered over Conjure Animals, Flock of Familiars and Mighty Summoner. Its own damage stays at a chip on both axes all run.
Totem.strength: Auras sized for a four-body party land entirely on one partner when the party is two, so the whole totem is spent on the other body rather than diluted, and Mighty Summoner stripping physical resistance off summon attacks keeps a field of conjured bodies relevant against Absolute Wrath.
Totem.wants: A body that converts the totem into damage — this chassis reads 1 on single-target and 2-3 on area, so the buffs need somebody worth buffing.
uncertain: Mighty Summoner's level and Guardian Spirit / Faithful Summons are all flagged (unverified) in the class file; I placed Mighty Summoner at Druid 6 as in 5e.
rsc 4 rests on Bear and Flumph totems reading as a no-action outward temp-HP and healing aura; if the totem is an Action rather than a Wild Shape charge that drops to 3.
Call Lightning scored at 2 targets (see Squall).

AoE re-banded to the rubric's fixed 4-target convention (axis-rubrics.md, Constants). Authored at 2 targets on Call Lightning's 3m radius; the radius point is real but is a rubric-wide change, not a per-batch one.

Menagerie2.split: Warlock 5 (The Fiend) / Druid 14 (Circle of the Shepherd) / Monk 1 (none)
Menagerie2.note: A totem-and-summon board: Conjure Animals held non-concentration until long rest, Flock of Familiars and a Pact of the Chain imp, all standing inside a Spirit Totem aura. It gives up almost all personal damage — the configuration scored is Shillelagh plus Eldritch Blast, with slots going to summons and area control rather than blasting.
Menagerie2.strength: Every totem is an aura aimed at the other character, and in a two-body party the aura covers 100% of the party rather than 50%; the summon set is the only thing in the list that turns a duo into something with a four-body action count against Listo's added enemy bodies.
Menagerie2.wants: A body that actually kills the priority target, because this one is at rung 1 on single-target in every act and never reaches rung 2.
uncertain: Mighty Summoner's level is (unverified) in the class file; scored as landing by Druid 6, which is what holds the Actions rung in Act III.
Level order assumed Warlock 1 at character 1, Druid to 12 by character 15, Warlock 3-5 and Monk 1 in Act III.
Guardian Spirit and Faithful Summons are (unverified) and are not scored at all.

Mycelium.split: Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling) / Druid 14 (Circle of the Spores)
Mycelium.note: A Symbiotic Entity melee druid swinging a Shillelagh quarterstaff with a real Extra Attack from mod 4018, with Spreading Spores running as a standing area. The Bard block is spent entirely on caster levels and skills, not on Magical Secrets, which needs Bard 10.
Mycelium.strength: Bard 6 plus Druid 14 stacks to caster level 20, so a melee body carries 9th-tier slots — and the 4-temp-HP-per-Druid-level buffer refreshes on the Wild Shape charge, which is a short-rest clock in a run where a long rest costs 120+ supplies.
Mycelium.wants: A body that answers single-target burst, since this one is at par on bosses and its whole engine is area chip.
uncertain: That mods 4018 and 1148 resolve to exactly one Extra Attack is (unverified) per the class file; the ST ratios assume four attacks a round.
Spreading Spores is scored at roughly 60% uptime on four targets; the Wild Shape charge it costs is assumed not to displace Symbiotic Entity, which two charges per short rest should cover.
College of Stormcalling's own features are not scored — only Bard chassis levels, Song of Rest and the skill package.

Blightward.note: The same Symbiotic Entity melee druid, opened on War Cleric for heavy armour, martial weapons and Wis+Cha saves, with Spirit Guardians as the standing area engine. It gives up the Bard skill package entirely and reads near-zero on Investigation and Perception-adjacent coverage.
Blightward.strength: Heavy armour and a shield from character 1 puts a full caster at AC 19-20 with 56 temp HP on top, which is the profile that survives Absolute Wrath's layered resistances better than it kills through them; Spirit Guardians upcast off caster-20 slots is at-will area damage that costs no action after the first.
Blightward.wants: Skill coverage — this body rolls nothing on Investigation and is the pair's weakest link on every untelegraphed check.
uncertain: Level order assumed Cleric 1 at character 1, Druid 7 by 8, Cleric 5 and Druid 10 by 15 — Spirit Guardians therefore arrives in Act II, not Act I.
Whether the War domain's heavy armour grant survives being the level-1 class alongside a Druid main is assumed yes; the dip section states it as a level-1 domain grant.

Zodiac.split: Barbarian 3 (Revenant) / Druid 11 (Circle of the Stars) / Cleric 6 (Twilight)
Zodiac.note: A Starry Form Archer support opened on Barbarian for Str+Con saves, a d12 hit die and Revenant's heavy armour plus flat DR 2, finishing on Twilight for Sanctuary on a short-rest Channel Divinity clock. It gives up melee throughput and every Charisma and Intelligence check in the run.
Zodiac.strength: Cosmic Omen recharges on a short rest under Star Druid Tweaks, so it is three to four swings of ±1d6 on a save per rest cycle — in a party of two where one failed save removes half the action economy, that is insurance the pair can actually afford to spend.
Zodiac.wants: Charisma and Intelligence coverage, because this body rolls a flat zero on Persuasion and Investigation in all three acts.
uncertain: Revenant's heavy armour proficiency at Barbarian 3 is taken from the dip section; it and Rage are in tension, and the scored configuration never rages, so Rage contributes nothing.
Twilight Sanctuary arrives at character 17 under the assumed level order, so the Act III rescue rung is only online for the last band.

Auspice.split: Barbarian 3 (Revenant) / Druid 11 (Circle of the Stars) / Monk 6 (Way of the Friar)
Auspice.note: The same Starry Form Archer chassis with Way of the Friar in place of the Cleric block: per-turn temp HP on both bodies, a free teleport to the partner, Friar's Blessing and a 6-ki short-rest pool. It gives up Twilight Sanctuary and every levelled slot above 6th tier.
Auspice.strength: Friar's Blessing and the per-turn temp HP are bonded-pair effects, so a two-body party gets full value from a feature written for four; combined with Cosmic Omen on a short rest this body carries two independent save-insurance layers and never touches a long rest for either.
Auspice.wants: Damage — it is rung 1 on single-target from Act II and rung 2 on area throughout, so the partner has to be the entire tempo half of the pair.
uncertain: Revenant's heavy armour and Monk's Unarmoured Defence are mutually exclusive; the scored configuration wears the armour and uses no Martial Arts, so Monk 6 is bought purely for Friar's aura, ki and the blessing.
Whether Friar's Blessing (+1d4 on both bonded bodies) needs the bond re-established after a death is (unverified).

Lionheart.note: A heavy-armour banner anchor: Extra Attack in half plate and shield, Banner Charges on a short-rest clock from Paragon 6, and Hypnotic Stare as a permanent free save debuff. It gives up area damage completely — rung 0 on AoE in every act — and holds no spell list at all.
Lionheart.strength: Red Banner hands the other character a Reaction attack and Yellow Banner hands them Charisma-mod AC, so every charge is spent on the half of a two-body party that needs it; Vanguard's Charge at Paragon 9 gives blanket Disadvantage on attacks against the anchor, which is scale-invariant against Listo's inflated damage.
Lionheart.wants: An area answer — this body is a flat 0 on AoE and near-0 on area control, so the partner must own the crowd half of the enemy-AP square outright.
uncertain: Paragon 7's Those Who Help Others is named but not described in the class file; the Rescue rung 2 from Act II rests on it being an improved Help, and would drop to 1 if it is not.
The Act III configuration is melee; Warlock 5 with Agonizing Blast at Charisma 20 would read rung 2 on single-target instead of rung 1, but only by abandoning Strength as the attack stat.
Feat budget is 6, not 7 — no class in this split reaches 13.

Ensign.note: The deep Lionheart: Paragon 13 for Vanguard's Glory, which turns every enemy that walks into melee range into an opportunity attack, with a Blood Hunter level for four short-rest Blood Curses and a Warlock block for pact slots. It has no spell list, no area damage and no way to move the fight.
Ensign.strength: Lone Wolf hands this body two Reactions, so Vanguard's Glory collects two free attacks per enemy turn rather than one, and Banner Charges sit on a short-rest clock — the whole chassis runs without ever paying the 120-supply long rest.
Ensign.wants: A body that owns the crowd column entirely, since this one is 0 on AoE and 0-1 on area control across the run.
uncertain: Blood Hunter 1 is below subclass level, so it is written (none); it buys Hunter's Bane, shields and two short-rest Blood Curses only.
Vanguard's Glory is scored at roughly one extra attack a round rather than two, on the assumption that not every enemy turn puts something into range.

Nighthawk.split: Paragon 11 (Nighthawk) / Blood Hunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer) / Druid 6 (Circle of the Spores)
Nighthawk.note: A resistance-stripping front-liner: Searing Blade removes all resistances on a failed Constitution save, Supernatural Dampening then stops the target healing, and Crimson Rite plus Symbiotic Entity stack two permanent weapon riders on top. It pays for it in three-way stat spread across Strength, Charisma and Wisdom.
Nighthawk.strength: Absolute Wrath is on and ordinary enemies carry layered resistances, so a body that strips them outright makes the partner's damage type stop mattering — that is worth more in a two-character party than in one that can carry four damage types between its members.
Nighthawk.wants: Area damage and area control, because Searing Blade is one target at a time and this body has almost nothing for the crowd column.
uncertain: Vigilant Aegis grants Protection from Evil and Good through Help; it is scored at rung 3 rather than the rung-4 prevention clause because the protection is creature-type gated.
Iron Filings' stacking 1d4 is scored at an average of two stacks a round.
Druid 6 arrives only in Act III under the assumed level order, which is why AoE and area control move off zero only in the last band.

Pyrelight.note: The same Nighthawk debuff front line with an arcane tail instead of a blood one — Pact of the Chain for a permanent third body, and Wizard 6 for Sculpted Fireballs that finally give the chassis a crowd answer. Strength, Charisma and Intelligence all want investment and only one of them can be 22.
Pyrelight.strength: Searing Blade strips the resistances that Absolute Wrath layers on ordinary enemies, and Evocation's Sculpt Spells means the Fireball can land on a pack the partner is standing in — a duo has no spare body to pull out of the blast.
Pyrelight.wants: Save-or-lose control on a concentration slot, which this body will never hold and never contest.
uncertain: Three-stat spread — Strength for attacks, Charisma for Nighthawk's DCs, Intelligence for the Wizard block; the scored Intelligence is 14 by Act III, which makes Fireball's save DC roughly two below par.
Wizard 6 lands entirely in Act III under the assumed level order, so the AoE and area-control rises are act-III-only and real, not a re-baselining artefact.

Prodigy.note: A Reckless Attack platform in Revenant heavy armour: flat DR 2 from the Barbarian order, Prodigy's Sheer Will taking another 2 off every source, and Rage's physical resistance under both. Opening Barbarian rather than Paragon costs the Constitution and Charisma save pair and every Paragon skill.
Prodigy.strength: Reckless Attack's permanent Advantage costs a body that already halves all incoming damage under Lone Wolf and then subtracts a flat 4 on top of the halving, so the usual price of the toggle is close to nothing here; Prodigy's Competitive Streak also refunds Willpower Dice off the partner's natural 20s.
Prodigy.wants: Concentration control and a save-or-lose answer, since this body's only control is a taunt and it holds no slot worth interrupting.
uncertain: Reckless Attack is scored as a x1.35 multiplier on weapon damage (hit chance 0.65 to 0.88); the rubric's h-cancels convention does not cover Advantage, so this is a judgement.
Rage and the Wizard block are mutually exclusive in a round; the scored configuration rages and casts only out of Rage, which is why AoE stays at rung 2 rather than higher.
Revenant's heavy armour at Barbarian 3 is the only heavy-armour source in this split — Paragon taken at level 4+ does not grant it.

Redoubt.note: The deepest Prodigy on the list: Paragon 13's Training From Hell adds resistance to non-magical bludgeoning, piercing and slashing on top of heavy armour, a shield and Sheer Will's flat reduction. The Wizard tail is bought for slots and a familiar; Bladesong itself never fires because the body never takes the armour off.
Redoubt.strength: Flat damage reduction is worth double under Lone Wolf's halving, and a proportional physical resistance stacked under it makes this the hardest body in the batch to remove — which matters most in a party of two, where the enemy AI has only one other target to pick and losing either half ends the fight.
Redoubt.wants: A crowd engine and a concentration controller, because this body clears one enemy at a time and has no answer to the extra bodies Listo's encounter mods add.
uncertain: Bladesong requires no medium or heavy armour and no shield, so the named subclass is inert in the scored configuration; Wizard 2 contributes light armour, the weapon list and caster levels only.
Sheer Will's damage reduction reaches 3 only at Paragon 17, which this split does not reach — scored at 2 from Paragon 9.

Titania.note: A crit-fishing lockdown body: Oberon's Favor puts a Willpower Die of Psychic on every weapon attack, Strike Of The Butterflies drops the crit threshold by 2, and Fairy's Curse turns each of those crits into a Charisma save against losing bonus actions and reactions. It has no area damage whatsoever and no spell list to fall back on.
Titania.strength: Fairy's Curse removes enemy bonus actions and reactions for free, with no concentration and no slot, which is exactly the currency this run trades in; Shifting Court's position swap also pulls the other character out of a pack and drops the armoured one in on a bonus action.
Titania.wants: An area engine — this body reads 0 on AoE in every act and 0-1 on area control, so the partner has to answer crowds alone.
uncertain: Fairy's Curse is crit-gated; scored as reliably repeatable on the strength of a -2 crit threshold across sixteen empowered attacks a fight, which is a judgement rather than a computed rate.
Shifting Court's extraction is scored at the Rescue rung-4 prevention clause even though it heals nothing; if the renderer's reader disagrees this should drop to 3.
Whether Regent's crit threshold stacks with the Critfisher Ring is flagged (unverified) in the class file and is not scored.

Revel.note: The deep Regent: Eternal Bloom at Paragon 13 adds a stack every turn so Oberon's Favor never runs dry, and five d8 Willpower Dice fund both the Psychic rider and the Shifting Court swaps. It buys that with a single Blood Hunter level and a Warlock tail, and holds no area capability at all.
Revel.strength: Everything the chassis does runs on short-rest dice, so it fights at full strength three times per long rest in a run where a long rest costs 120+ supplies; Fairy's Curse stripping reactions and bonus actions is action-economy denial in a fight where the enemy has more bodies than you do.
Revel.wants: A body that clears packs, because this one removes exactly one enemy's turn at a time and nothing else.
uncertain: Blood Hunter 1 is below subclass level and written (none); it contributes two short-rest Blood Curses and nothing else.
Same crit-gating judgement on Fairy's Curse as Titania, with one more Willpower Die and Eternal Bloom's guaranteed stack behind it.

Grimoire2.note: The single-stat Paragon: Scholar's Armament puts the main-hand weapon on Charisma for attack and damage, four Focuses cover four damage types, and Warlock 3's Agonizing Blast runs off the same stat. The Wizard block is off-stat — Intelligence never gets past 14, so Fireball's save DC sits roughly two below par.
Grimoire2.strength: Four Focuses by Paragon 11 means four damage types on one body, which is the cheapest answer in the list to Absolute Wrath's layered resistances in a party too small to cover them with gear; Magic Resistance at Paragon 9 gives advantage on the spell saves that otherwise remove half the party in one roll.
Grimoire2.wants: Hard single-target control — this body debuffs saves but never actually takes a turn away, and Will Over Weave sits two levels past the split.
uncertain: The AoE rung is the least certain number in this batch. Force and Thunder Focus Spell Sword attacks 'hit enemies around the target' at will, four attacks a round; read literally that is rung 5, but the splash size is undocumented, so it is scored at rung 3 throughout.
Spell Sword attacks are treated as at-will cantrips; Arcane Surge (a Willpower Die) only raises their level, so the engine is scored as unbounded on Endurance.
Charisma is save-proficient from Paragon 1, so Lone Wolf's +4 goes to Wisdom and Dexterity and Charisma 22 costs two ASI feats plus a gate.

Spellblade.note: Spellblade and Lore on one Charisma stat: Scholar's Armament makes the sword a Charisma weapon and the Bard block spends the same score on slots, Cutting Words and a genuine skill package. Barbarian 3 arrives last and is bought for Reckless Attack and flat DR 2, with Rage unused because it would shut off the Spell Sword attacks.
Spellblade.strength: Two characters have to clear every check in the campaign, and Lore's three bonus proficiencies plus two Expertise on a stat this body already needed makes it the only chassis in the batch that reads above rung 2 on Skills; Bardic Inspiration on a short-rest clock is a resource the partner can spend on damage or healing under Magical Inspiration.
Spellblade.wants: Durability, or a body that can take the front rank, because Reckless Attack hands the enemy advantage on the softer half of a two-body party.
uncertain: Same undocumented Spell Sword splash as Grimoire; AoE scored at rung 3 throughout on the same judgement.
Rage is scored as never used — it would block the Spell Sword attacks, which are treated as cantrips — so Barbarian 3 contributes Reckless Attack, Danger Sense, the d12 and Revenant's DR 2 only.
Expertise is placed on Perception and Persuasion; moving it to Investigation would trade about a rung of Act III Skills between the two checks.

Kensho.note: A throughput chassis built on Falling Rain, a free-action weapon attack that rides every Willpower Die spent, with Fanning the Flames adding a stacking Fire rider inside each turn. The Warlock and Wizard tails buy a familiar and a late crowd answer at the cost of a third stat.
Kensho.strength: Lone Wolf's second Action means twice as many Blade Skills per round and therefore twice as many free Falling Rain attacks, so this is the chassis whose engine is doubled rather than merely duplicated by the run's baseline economy.
Kensho.wants: Control of any kind — this body removes enemy turns permanently or not at all, and holds nothing that buys the pair a round.
uncertain: Falling Rain is scored at one free attack per Willpower Die spent, i.e. the whole short-rest pool per fight; the class file does not cap it per turn.
Fanning the Flames is scored at an average of +6 damage a round from within-turn stacking; the stacks clear at the start of your turn, so two Actions build them twice.

Satori.split: Paragon 11 (Sword Saint) / Blood Hunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer) / Druid 6 (Circle of the Spores)
Satori.note: The same Falling Rain engine with two permanent weapon riders bolted on — Crimson Rite from Ghostslayer and Symbiotic Entity from Spores — plus 24 temp HP and a Conjure Animals set that costs one slot and lasts until long rest. Three stats want investment and the Wisdom-gated Halo DC never gets there.
Satori.strength: Crimson Rite and Symbiotic Entity are both permanent-until-long-rest, so the whole rider package is paid once and then runs at-will across all three fights of a cycle rather than out of a per-fight pool; Rite of the Dawn also gives a Radiant damage type, which Absolute Wrath resists least in Act II.
Satori.wants: Area control, since this body has persistent riders but no way to stop several enemies at once and reads 1 on area control even in Act III.
uncertain: Symbiotic Entity's +1d6 is scored as applying to the Paragon weapon attacks; the class file describes it as weapon or unarmed attacks and does not restrict it to Druid levels.
Druid 6 lands entirely in Act III under the assumed level order, which is why the rider stack, temp HP and summon set all arrive at once.

Tonic.split: Paladin 3 (Oath of the Ancients) / Artificer 11 (Alchemist) / Bard 6 (College of Lore)
Tonic.note: A heavy-armoured apothecary: Paladin 1 buys the plate and the Wis/Cha saves, Artificer 11 buys elixirs, Restorative Reagents and Spell-Storing Item, and Bard 6 arrives only in Act III to patch the skill floor. It gives up all damage identity — four mundane swings and a smite are the whole offence.
Tonic.strength: Six elixirs and free Lesser Restoration per rest attack the one resource a two-body run actually runs out of, camp supplies at 120+ a long rest, and Spell-Storing Item hands the other character Int-mod scrolls it could never cast itself.
Tonic.wants: A body that removes enemies quickly, because this one is at par on single-target and near zero on area damage in both early acts.
uncertain: Level order assumed Paladin 3 → Artificer 11 → Bard 6, so College of Lore's three proficiencies and Expertise land only in Act III; a front-loaded Bard block would trade Act III skills for Act I ones.
Alchemist's Chemical Mastery (free Heal / Greater Restoration) is Artificer 15 and is not reached at 11, so the camp-supply argument is weaker than the class file's headline.

Draught.split: Paladin 3 (Oath of the Ancients) / Artificer 11 (Alchemist) / Cleric 6 (Peace Domain)
Draught.note: The same plated apothecary, with the last six levels spent on Peace instead of Lore — Emboldening Bond and Warding Bond for the pair rather than skills for itself. Its skill sheet never improves, and Perception stays near unrollable all run.
Draught.strength: Emboldening Bond puts a permanent d4 on every save both characters make, which in a party of exactly two is total coverage, and it stacks with Flash of Genius spending Lone Wolf's spare reaction on the partner's save.
Draught.wants: A body with real Perception and area damage; this one cannot find a trap and cannot clear a room.
uncertain: Peace Domain lands at character 15–20 under a primary-first level order, so Emboldening Bond and Warding Bond exist only in Act III; taking Cleric earlier would move both forward at the cost of the Artificer 11 breakpoint.
Spirit Guardians needs Cleric 5, i.e. character 19, so the Act III aoe of 2 credits barely two fights of it.

Carapace.note: Arcane Armor in Guardian configuration: heavy plate from Artificer 3, Extra Attack at 5, Thunder Gauntlets, and a reaction that yanks an attacker off the partner. The Sorcerer levels are bolted on at the very end for Twinned and Quickened, so for fifteen characters this is a pure armoured brawler.
Carapace.strength: Perfected Armor's pull is a taunt in a game with no taunt, and Lone Wolf's second reaction means using it does not cost the ordinary one — in a duo that is the difference between the softer body being focused and not.
Carapace.wants: Damage. This body is at par on single-target in every act and never exceeds it, so the partner has to be the one that ends fights.
uncertain: Guardian rather than Infiltrator is chosen per rubric rule 3; the Infiltrator line would trade the pull for a ranged Int attack and about a rung of Act II single-target.
Thunder Gauntlets are 1d8 against par's 2d6, which is why Armorer never clears par on st despite Extra Attack at 5.

Stormshell.split: Sorcerer 6 (Draconic Bloodline) / Artificer 11 (Armorer) / Warlock 3 (The Great Old One)
Stormshell.note: Armorer run in Infiltrator configuration — heavy armour with a Lightning Launcher that fires off Intelligence, so one stat drives attack, damage, AC spells and spell DC. The Warlock 3 tail arrives at character 18 and buys a familiar and short-rest slots rather than damage, because Charisma is a dump stat here.
Stormshell.strength: Hypnotic Pattern always-prepared at Artificer 9 plus Perfected Armor's glimmer means this body can lock a crowd and still shoot, which matters when Listo's added encounters outnumber a two-person party every fight.
Stormshell.wants: A partner who can hold the concentration on something else, since this body's crowd answer occupies the pair's one slot the moment it is cast.
uncertain: Lightning is a locked damage type on the Launcher line, so rubric rule 4's 0.5 multiplier on half of Act II+ encounters is applied to the rider; a resistance strip would return most of a rung.
Warlock 3 at character 18 contributes almost nothing offensively on an Int body — Eldritch Blast off Charisma 14 is below the weapon line.

Fusillade.split: Paladin 3 (Oath of Vengeance) / Artificer 11 (Artillerist) / Bard 6 (College of Lore)
Fusillade.note: A plated gun platform: Eldritch Cannon from Artificer 3, Arcane Firearm adding 1d8 to every spell from 5, Fireball always-prepared at 9, and a Lore Bard tail that finally gives the body a skill sheet in Act III. Its own weapon line never rises above par.
Fusillade.strength: The cannon resummons off the Ranger's-Companion template rather than a daily charge, so a duo gets a permanent third initiative slot for free — and the Homunculus infusion makes it four bodies out of two characters.
Fusillade.wants: Single-target closing power against bosses; the cannon and Fireball are crowd tools and this body's own swings sit exactly at par.
uncertain: Cannon damage is excluded from st and aoe under rubric rule 2 (summons are §4) and scored as Actions instead; if a future pass counts it as damage the aoe row rises about a rung in Acts II–III.
Fortified Position's two cannons is Artificer 15 and is out of reach at 11.

Mortar.split: Paladin 3 (Oath of Vengeance) / Artificer 11 (Artillerist) / Cleric 6 (Light Domain)
Mortar.note: The same gun platform with Light Domain instead of Lore — Radiance of the Dawn and Warding Flare rather than Expertise. It keeps a Perception of 1 for the entire run, which is a real hole in a modlist whose traps sit at DC 15–25.
Mortar.strength: Two Channel Divinity charges on a short-rest clock is exactly the cadence this run rewards, and Warding Flare imposing disadvantage on an attack aimed at the partner is a second body-saving reaction Lone Wolf already paid for.
Mortar.wants: A body that can actually roll Perception and Investigation, because this one is blind to everything the run does not announce.
uncertain: Light Domain lands at character 15–20, so Radiance of the Dawn contributes to Act III only.
Cannon damage excluded from the damage axes per rubric rule 2, as above.

Cogsmith.note: The one-stat body: Battle Ready puts Intelligence on attack and damage, Enhanced Weapon self-supplies the magical prerequisite, and everything else — spell DC, Arcane Jolt uses, Flash of Genius, saves — keys off the same number. It gives up any damage ceiling; it is at par on single-target in all three acts.
Cogsmith.strength: Warding Bond at Artificer 5, a Steel Defender whose Deflect Attack imposes disadvantage on attacks aimed at the *other* character, and Arcane Jolt healing that rides the attack routine — three separate ways to keep a two-body party from losing half of itself.
Cogsmith.wants: A body that clears crowds; this one has almost no area damage and no area control worth the name until very late.
uncertain: College of Stormcalling is taken as given by the search; its features were not in the read set, so the Bard 6 block is scored only for Jack of All Trades, Song of Rest, Expertise and full-caster slots.
Improved Defender (Arcane Jolt 4d6) is Artificer 15 and is one level out of reach at 14.

Ironwright.split: Sorcerer 6 (Draconic Bloodline) / Artificer 11 (Battle Smith) / Paladin 3 (Oath of the Ancients)
Ironwright.note: Battle Smith cut short at 11 to make room for Sorcerer metamagic and a late Paladin block. It keeps the Steel Defender and Warding Bond but loses Death Ward, Magic Item Savant and Improved Defender, and it spends its Charisma on nothing.
Ironwright.strength: Twinned Haste covers the whole party when the party is two, and Quickened is the only reliable route to three casts in a turn alongside Lone Wolf's second Action — that is the Act III turn this chassis exists for.
Ironwright.wants: Crowd removal and a Perception body; this one is zero on Perception all run and thin on area damage until Sorcerer 5 lands.
uncertain: Sorcery points scale on Sorcerer class level only, so a 6-level dip Twins or Quickens about twice per long rest — the Act III act rung of 4 assumes that budget, not sustained use.
Paladin 3 arrives at character 18 and buys heavy-armour-free Divine Smite and Lay on Hands only; no Aura of Protection at 3.

Pounce.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Zealot) / Ranger 11 (Beast Master) / Wizard 6 (School of Evocation)
Pounce.note: A bow Ranger with a Panther that scales off its proficiency bonus, saves like a PC and Helps as a bonus action, plus a late Wizard block that is cast off Intelligence 14. The Barbarian opener buys Str/Con saves and a d12 first level, but Rage is unusable on a body that holds Hunter's Mark.
Pounce.strength: The Panther is a third initiative slot that can Help a downed partner up as a bonus action, which in a party of two is the whole difference between a wipe and a recovery; Conjure Animals at Ranger 9 turns it into a set.
Pounce.wants: A body with a real casting stat, because this one's Wizard slots come off Intelligence 14 and its own spell DC is Wisdom.
uncertain: Zealot's Fanatical Focus is not claimed as a booster: Rage blocks spellcasting, and this body's damage rides Hunter's Mark, so it will not be raging.
Share Spells is Beast Master 15 and is not reached at Ranger 11 — the one-buff-covers-two-actors argument does not apply to this split.
Wizard 6 gives 3rd-level spells known against a multiclass slot table reaching 6th; the Act III aoe of 2 assumes upcast Fireball off half the levelled slots.

Menagerie.split: Sorcerer 6 (Draconic Bloodline) / Ranger 11 (Beast Master) / Paladin 3 (Oath of the Ancients)
Menagerie.note: The same Panther chassis opened with Sorcerer for Con/Cha saves and closed with a three-level Paladin block at character 18. Draconic Resilience's hit points are the only durability it buys; the Paladin levels arrive too late to be anything but Divine Smite fuel.
Menagerie.strength: Twinned Haste is a party-wide Haste when the party is two, and dropping it on the Panther or the partner converts Lone Wolf's economy into a genuine four-actor turn.
Menagerie.wants: Area damage and a Perception body; the companion set covers action economy but nothing here clears a room.
uncertain: Sorcerer levels 2–6 land at characters 13–17 under a primary-first order, so metamagic exists only in the back half of Act II and Act III.
Paladin 3 at character 18 grants no aura; Aura of Protection needs Paladin 6.

Sunlance.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Zealot) / Ranger 11 (Conclave of the Dawnstriders) / Wizard 6 (School of Evocation)
Sunlance.note: The highest raw damage ceiling in the conclave list — Valkyrie leaps with a free Extra Attack on landing, Zeal stacking to another, and Divine Flurry buying five extra attacks at a reduced critical threshold for an Action, a bonus action and a 3rd-level slot. The price is the Faded window afterwards and a body that must be in melee.
Sunlance.strength: It is the one Ranger whose single-target row does not fall across the run, because Divine Flurry scales with the slot table rather than a fixed die — and Herald of the Sun's Radiant/Fire toggle sidesteps Absolute Wrath's physical resistances that par eats.
Sunlance.wants: Someone to cover the turn after Divine Flurry, because Faded is a real dead round and there is no third body to hide behind.
uncertain: Divine Flurry throughput is scored at two casts per fight in Act II and three in Act III off half the levelled slots; a different slot split moves the st row by a rung either way.
Pursuit of Valor is Dawnstriders 15 and is not reached at Ranger 11, so the kill-into-free-Valkyrie loop the class file describes is absent from this split.

Daybreak.split: Artificer 3 (Artillerist) / Ranger 11 (Conclave of the Dawnstriders) / Wizard 6 (School of Evocation)
Daybreak.note: The same leaping Dawnstrider opened with three Artificer levels instead of Barbarian — Int and Con saves, medium armour and shields without spending Lightly and Moderately Armoured, and an Eldritch Cannon from character 3. Intelligence has to be real for the Artificer and Wizard halves, which starves Wisdom.
Daybreak.strength: Artificer 1 returns two armour feats and hands over the best save pair in the game, and the cannon is a permanent third body that resummons without a daily charge — two characters fielding three actors from character 3.
Daybreak.wants: A Charisma face; between Ranger, Artificer and Wizard this body has nothing to say in town and no route to Hag's Hair.
uncertain: The Eldritch Cannon at Artificer 3 is a flat 2d8 with 20 HP; per the rubric's own worked case it is close to irrelevant by Act II, so it is scored as Actions rather than damage and does not carry a rising row.
Three casting stats — Wis for the conclave, Int for Artificer and Wizard — is a genuine spread; the Wizard block's DC is scored as unreliable.

Wyrmling.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Zealot) / Ranger 11 (Drakewarden) / Wizard 6 (School of Evocation)
Wyrmling.note: A drake handler: a permanent flying companion from Ranger 3, Infused Strikes adding the drake's essence damage to weapon hits, resistance to that type at 7, and an 8d6 cone at 11 off a long-rest charge or a 3rd-level slot. The essence is a single element, which Absolute Wrath punishes from Act II.
Wyrmling.strength: Infused Strikes buffs the *partner's* attacks as well as its own within 30 ft, which is the only rider in the Ranger list that pays a two-body party twice, and Drake's Breath is the conclave's own area answer without a caster level.
Wyrmling.wants: A resistance strip or a second damage type, because the drake's essence rider is one element and it is the part of this body's damage that is not weapon-based.
uncertain: Infused Strikes is scored as a once-per-turn rider. If the installed implementation fires on every qualifying hit, the Act I single-target row rises to 4 and Act II to 3.
Reflexive Resistance and Perfected Bond are Drakewarden 15 and are not reached at Ranger 11.

Scalebond.split: Sorcerer 6 (Draconic Bloodline) / Ranger 11 (Drakewarden) / Paladin 3 (Oath of the Ancients)
Scalebond.note: The drake chassis opened on Sorcerer for Con and Cha saves, with the metamagic block landing mid-Act-II and a Paladin tail at character 18. Draconic Resilience adds a hit point a level; nothing else here is defensive.
Scalebond.strength: Twinned Haste on the drake and the partner turns one 3rd-level slot into two hasted actors, which is the cheapest action-economy purchase this pair will find, and Draconic hit points offset the Ranger's d6 chassis.
Scalebond.wants: Crowd control; Drake's Breath is once a fight and this body has no way to stop a room of enemies from acting.
uncertain: Infused Strikes scored once per turn, as above.
The mod author warns a new playthrough may be needed for Drakewarden animation; scored as if it works.

Courtier.note: The party face that never spent a point on Charisma: Otherworldly Glamour adds the full Wisdom modifier to every Charisma check, and Ranger 14 buys Vanish and Fey Reinforcements on top. The Sorcerer block is the last five levels and contributes metamagic, not fuel.
Courtier.strength: In a two-Tav run one body has to carry town dialogue, and this is the only chassis in the batch that does it off the same Wisdom it already needed for its spell DC — the other character is freed to be anything at all.
Courtier.wants: A crowd-clearing engine; Dreadful Strikes is a 1d6 rider and Summon Fey is one body, so nothing here answers being outnumbered.
uncertain: Persuasion credits Otherworldly Glamour's full Wisdom modifier on top of proficiency and a Charisma of 14 taken from the Sorcerer opener.
Misty Wanderer is Fey Wanderer 15 and is one level out of reach at Ranger 14, so the passenger-teleport argument does not apply.

Glamour.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Zealot) / Ranger 11 (Fey Wanderer) / Wizard 6 (School of Evocation)
Glamour.note: Fey Wanderer opened on Barbarian for Str and Con saves and closed with a Wizard block. Otherworldly Glamour still makes it the face, but the Charisma it adds Wisdom to is an 8, so the ceiling is lower than the Sorcerer-opened version.
Glamour.strength: Beguiling Twist gives advantage on charm and fear saves and turns a *partner's* successful save into a free control effect — a reaction that only pays out when there is another body to watch, which is exactly this run.
Glamour.wants: Area damage and a second concentration slot; this body holds Hunter's Mark and has nothing left for a control spell.
uncertain: Persuasion assumes the Otherworldly Glamour proficiency pick plus Wisdom modifier on a Charisma of 8.
Fey Reinforcements at Ranger 11 gives one free Summon Fey per long rest; counted in act, not in the damage rows, per rubric rule 2.

Umbra.split: Sorcerer 6 (Draconic Bloodline) / Ranger 11 (Gloom Stalker) / Paladin 3 (Oath of Vengeance)
Umbra.note: A front-loaded ambusher: +3 initiative and a first-round extra attack with 1d8 from Ranger 3, Iron Mind patching the Ranger's missing Wisdom save at 7, and Stalker's Flurry re-attacking on a miss at 11. Everything it has is online by character 12 and then only gets bigger numbers.
Umbra.strength: Winning initiative matters more with two bodies than with four, and Dread Ambusher plus Umbral Shroud is a genuine delete-one-enemy-before-it-acts opener against Listo's inflated enemy counts.
Umbra.wants: Sustained crowd damage; this body spends its edge in round one and is a plain bow Ranger for the other three.
uncertain: Iron Mind's Wisdom and Intelligence save proficiencies are not added to prof: the schema's grant list is level-1 class, Lone Wolf, Resilient, Slippery Mind and Diamond Soul only. This body genuinely holds five to six proficient saves and is scored as four — flag for a booster id or a grant-list extension.
Shadowy Dodge is Gloom Stalker 15 and is not reached at Ranger 11.

SoulSorcerer.note: The deeper Gloom Stalker — Ranger 14 adds Vanish, hiding as a bonus action, on top of Stalker's Flurry, and the Sorcerer tail is the last five levels. Two classes rather than three means seven feats instead of six.
SoulSorcerer.strength: Vanish plus Umbral Shroud makes this the one body in the batch that can break contact entirely when a duo's initiative goes wrong, and Favored Soul's Warding Bond arrives with the metamagic to Twin the rest of the buff list.
SoulSorcerer.wants: A body that can stand in the open and hold a line, because this one's answer to being focused is to leave.
uncertain: Iron Mind's two save proficiencies are unrepresentable in the prof grant list, as above.
Sorcerer 2–6 lands at characters 16–20, so all metamagic and every Sorcerer slot is an Act III capability.

Riftstep.split: Sorcerer 6 (Draconic Bloodline) / Ranger 11 (Horizon Walker) / Paladin 3 (Oath of Vengeance)
Riftstep.note: Planar Warrior converts an entire attack's damage to Force and adds 1d8, rising to 2d8 at 11; Distant Strike teleports before each attack and grants a third attack when three enemies are on the board. It is a melee body with almost no defensive kit beyond Ethereal Step once a rest.
Riftstep.strength: Lone Wolf's second bonus action means Planar Warrior can be applied twice a turn, and Force is the least resisted type in the game — this body sidesteps Absolute Wrath's layered physical resistances that the reference weapon eats head-on.
Riftstep.wants: Crowd control or area damage; Distant Strike only pays when there are three enemies, and this body has nothing that stops them acting.
uncertain: The Act III single-target ratio lands at 1.12, just under the rung-3 band; the Force-conversion advantage over a resisted mundane weapon would push it over, but that credit is not in the par model, so 2 is written.
Two Planar Warrior marks a turn assumes both Lone Wolf bonus actions are free, which competes with Hunter's Mark re-targeting.

Planeshear.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Zealot) / Ranger 11 (Horizon Walker) / Wizard 6 (School of Evocation)
Planeshear.note: The Force-conversion Ranger opened on Barbarian for Str and Con saves and Danger Sense, with a Wizard block cast off Intelligence 14. The Barbarian levels buy survivability the conclave lacks and a Rage this body will rarely use.
Planeshear.strength: Everything this body throws becomes Force, which is the one damage type Listo's resistance layering does not touch, and Evocation's Sculpt Spells means the Fireballs it learns at character 15 do not also hit the only other party member.
Planeshear.wants: A partner with a real casting stat and a Charisma face; this body dumps both.
uncertain: Act III st is 1.12 of par and rounds down to 2, as with the Sorcerer-opened version.
Zealot's Fanatical Focus not claimed — Rage blocks the Hunter's Mark this body's damage assumes.

Volley.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Zealot) / Ranger 11 (Hunter) / Wizard 6 (School of Evocation)
Volley.note: Colossus Slayer for one target, Volley for a room, and Multiattack Defence at 7 as the only mitigation. The Wizard tail adds a second area answer in Act III off an Intelligence of 14, which is thin, and the Barbarian opener is really just the save pair.
Volley.strength: Volley fired from both Lone Wolf Actions is the strongest at-will area engine any half-caster reaches, and it is at-will — no slot, no clock — against a run where three hard fights have to come out of one 120-supply long rest.
Volley.wants: A body that can lock down a boss, because this one's boss answer is a 1d8 rider and nothing else.
uncertain: Endurance is scored 5 on the at-will clause: bow attacks, Colossus Slayer and Volley all cost nothing per fight, and only Hunter's Mark touches the slot table.
Multiattack Defence is flat, attack-facing mitigation, so the durability row drops a rung as the acts become boss-weighted.

Hordebreak.note: The same Volley engine with a seven-level Mesmerist tail instead of a caster block: Hypnotic Stare's permanent free −1 to one enemy's saves, Towering Ego, and Gift of Will at exactly Mesmerist 7. Stopping Barbarian at 2 costs a feat outright — five instead of six.
Hordebreak.strength: Gift of Will puts Charisma plus half level onto the *partner's* Wisdom saves, and in a party of two that is the whole party covered against the Hold and Dominate effects that end a duo fight; Hypnotic Stare costs no resource and improves every save the pair forces.
Hordebreak.wants: A Charisma-heavy or Investigation-heavy partner — this body rolls a flat zero on Investigation for the whole run.
uncertain: Towering Ego scales with Charisma and this body's Charisma is 12, so the booster is worth about +1 rather than the +5 the class file quotes for a Charisma primary. It is authored because it is real, not because it is large.
The Mesmerist multiclass node is undocumented — whether a Mesmerist taken at character 14 still grants its skill picks is unverified, and the Persuasion figures assume it does.
Barbarian 2 is deliberately below subclass level, hence (none) in the split.

Quarry.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Zealot) / Ranger 11 (Monster Slayer) / Wizard 6 (School of Evocation)
Quarry.note: The boss-killer conclave: Slayer's Prey is a 1d6 rider that costs no concentration and therefore stacks with Hunter's Mark, Hunter's Sense makes a hit bypass all resistances and immunities, and Magic-User's Nemesis at 11 is a counterspell that works on anything.
Quarry.strength: Supernatural Defense's +1d6 on every save the prey forces and a free negation of the boss's one big spell are precisely the two effects that stop a two-body party losing half its action economy in a single round.
Quarry.wants: Crowd clear. Everything this body owns is aimed at one creature and the run keeps sending more than one.
uncertain: supernatural-defense is authored from Act II because Monster Slayer 7 lands at character 10 under this level order.
Hunter's Sense is scored as insurance against Absolute Wrath rather than as a damage rung; it is Wisdom-modifier uses per long rest, which is a per-fight burst, not a routine.

Bloodhound.split: Sorcerer 6 (Draconic Bloodline) / Ranger 11 (Monster Slayer) / Barbarian 3 (Path of the Zealot)
Bloodhound.note: Monster Slayer opened on Sorcerer for Con and Cha saves and closed with three Barbarian levels at character 18, which is late enough that Danger Sense and Rage are Act III only. Its identity is a no-concentration damage rider plus a free counterspell.
Bloodhound.strength: Slayer's Prey does not hold concentration, so this body can carry Hunter's Mark *and* a Twinned control spell — one of the few chassis here that can occupy the pair's second concentration slot without giving up its damage rider.
Bloodhound.wants: An area answer; the Sorcerer block reaches only 3rd-level spells known and the conclave is entirely single-target.
uncertain: Barbarian 3 at characters 18–20 means the d12 hit die, the level-1 armour proficiencies and the save pair are all forfeited — this dip buys only Danger Sense, a subclass and three Rages.
Zealot's Fanatical Focus not claimed: Rage blocks the spellcasting this body relies on.

Heartwood.split: Sorcerer 6 (Draconic Bloodline) / Ranger 11 (Primeval Guardian) / Paladin 3 (Oath of the Ancients)
Heartwood.note: The only Ranger that is a tank: guardian form gives Large size, temp HP equal to half Ranger level every turn and +2 maximum HP per Ranger level from 7, at the price of a 5-foot movement speed. It pairs with a bow and nothing else.
Heartwood.strength: Temp HP every single turn costs no action and no camp supplies, which is the one resource a duo genuinely runs out of, and Rooted Defense turns the ground around it into difficult terrain permanently with no concentration and no slot.
Heartwood.wants: Mobility and crowd damage — this body cannot chase anything, so the partner has to bring whatever reaches the back line.
uncertain: Guardian Aura, the outward healing half of the conclave, is Primeval Guardian 15 and is not reached at Ranger 11 — the rescue row is therefore ordinary Ranger Revivify, not the passive partner healing the class file advertises.
Rooted Defense is scored as rung-3 area control: it is permanent and slot-free but only difficult terrain, which the rubric's rung 1 names as an incidental.
Piercing Thorns is turn-based-mode only per the class file; scored as if the run is played in turn-based combat, which it is.

Great.split: Sorcerer 6 (Draconic Bloodline) / Ranger 11 (Primeval Guardian) / Warlock 3 (The Great Old One)
Great.note: The tree-form Ranger with a Warlock tail at character 18 rather than a Paladin one — a Pact of the Chain familiar and two short-rest 2nd-level slots instead of Divine Smite. Charisma is 14 at best, so the Warlock block is a body and a clock, not damage.
Great.strength: Short-rest pact slots on top of at-will temp HP means this chassis asks for a long rest less often than anything else in the batch, which against a 120-supply camp cost is worth more than a damage rung.
Great.wants: Reach and pace; at 5 feet of movement it contributes nothing to a fight it cannot see the start of.
uncertain: Guardian Aura is Primeval Guardian 15, not reached, as above.
Warlock 3 at character 18 breaks nothing in the feat cadence but delivers Eldritch Blast off a Charisma of 14, which is below this body's bow line and is not counted in st.

Whiteout.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Zealot) / Ranger 11 (Snowlight Conclave) / Wizard 6 (School of Evocation)
Whiteout.note: The hardest control conclave in the Ranger list: any Cold or Radiant damage forces a Constitution save or Blinds for two turns, with no concentration and no resource, and from 11 a Blinded creature takes 1d6 Radiant for every action it tries to take. It needs a Cold or Radiant damage source to work at all.
Whiteout.strength: Blind is a full attack shutdown, it costs this body nothing, and it never competes with the pair's two concentration slots — against Listo's added enemy counts, blinding a room is worth more than any damage rider in the class.
Whiteout.wants: A reliable Cold or Radiant damage source, and a body that can hold a concentration control spell, because this one already carries Hunter's Mark.
uncertain: Act I control is scored 3 rather than 4 because Glaring Frost needs a Cold or Radiant source and neither Blinding Smite (Ranger 9) nor a reliable elemental weapon can be assumed at character 6–8; Ray of Frost from the Wizard block does not arrive until character 15.
Snowborn Anthelion, which makes Glaring Frost an area effect, is Snowlight 15 and is not reached — hence area control stays at 2–3.
Snow Blindness damage is scored inside aoe at a 0.55 save-fail rate against two blinded enemies.

Rime.split: Sorcerer 6 (Draconic Bloodline) / Ranger 11 (Snowlight Conclave) / Paladin 3 (Oath of Devotion)
Rime.note: The blinding conclave with Devotion's Sacred Weapon as its Radiant source, which is the cleanest fix in the batch for Snowlight's one dependency. The Paladin block lands at character 18, so for two acts the trigger is Armour of Agathys and Blinding Smite.
Rime.strength: A permanent Radiant weapon means Glaring Frost fires on every hit, and Lone Wolf's four attacks a round means four Constitution saves a round with no resource spent — a lockdown engine that never touches the pair's concentration slots.
Rime.wants: A body that can hold a concentration spell and one that can find traps; this chassis carries Hunter's Mark and rolls Investigation off Intelligence 10.
uncertain: Sacred Weapon is Oath of Devotion's Channel Oath and this body reaches Paladin 3 only at character 18, so the reliable Radiant source is an Act III capability; Acts I–II are scored on Blinding Smite and the conclave's own cold spells.
Snowborn Anthelion not reached at Ranger 11, as above.

Moths.split: Sorcerer 6 (Draconic Bloodline) / Ranger 11 (Swarmkeeper) / Paladin 3 (Oath of the Ancients)
Moths.note: Gathered Swarm run as Flurry of Moths: once per round after an attack the swarm deals psychic damage, Blinds, or teleports the Ranger — free, every round, no concentration. Mighty Swarm at 11 raises the die and adds a rider; Writhing Tide gives flight charges at 7.
Moths.strength: A free reposition every round is the answer to being focused when there is no third body to peel, and a no-resource Blind on a boss is the cheapest way a two-person party avoids eating a boss turn.
Moths.wants: Area damage. The swarm hits one target and the Sorcerer block reaches only 3rd-level spells; nothing here clears adds.
uncertain: Only one Gathered Swarm option is scored, per rubric rule 3 — Moths for the Blind. Jellyfish or Bees would move control down and single-target damage marginally up.
Swarming Dispersal is Swarmkeeper 15 and is not reached at Ranger 11.

Chitin.note: The deeper Swarmkeeper — Ranger 14 buys Vanish on top of Mighty Swarm, and the two-class shape returns a seventh feat. The Sorcerer block is the last five levels and is metamagic without much fuel.
Chitin.strength: A free Blind every round that spends no concentration, no slot and no bonus action, stacked on Favored Soul's Twinned buffs — the pair keeps both concentration slots for something else while still removing a boss turn.
Chitin.wants: A crowd engine and an Investigation body; this chassis is single-target control and reads secret doors off Intelligence 10.
uncertain: Moths chosen as the single Gathered Swarm configuration, as above.
Swarming Dispersal is Swarmkeeper 15; Ranger 14 misses it by one level, which is the main thing this split gives up relative to a Ranger 15 build.

Cinder.split: Paladin 3 (Oath of Devotion) / Monk 11 (Warrior of the Elements) / Cleric 6 (Tempest)
Cinder.note: An elemental Monk that retunes its damage type at will and pays for it by stopping at Monk 11, six levels short of the 1d12 Martial Arts die. The Paladin opener buys Wis+Cha saves and a Divine Smite it can never spend on unarmed strikes; the Cleric block only lands in Act III.
Cinder.strength: Damage-type selection is the cheapest answer in the roster to Absolute Wrath's layered resistances — no gear swap, no second damage source — and the push/pull rider on opportunity attacks is control taken on the enemy's turn, which costs a two-body party nothing.
Cinder.wants: A partner who owns the pair's concentration slot and brings area damage, because this body is 0 on AoE until character 15.
uncertain: Elemental Burst (6) and Elemental Epitome (17) carry no numbers in the class file; Elemental Burst is scored as no AoE rung rather than guessed.
Dexterity is modelled as a lagging secondary at +3/+4/+5 across the acts; the whole Monk damage row moves a rung if a build funds Dex to parity with Wis.

Emberwrath.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Zealot) / Monk 11 (Warrior of the Elements) / Cleric 6 (Twilight)
Emberwrath.note: The same elemental Monk opened on Barbarian for Str+Con saves, a d12 hit die and Rage's physical resistance. It gives up Divine Smite and any Act I or Act II outward healing, and Rage's +2 damage does nothing on Dex-scaled strikes.
Emberwrath.strength: Four disjoint saves covering Wis, Con and Dex from level 1, under proportional physical resistance that stacks with Lone Wolf's halving — with no taunt in BG3 the enemy AI picks the softer body, and this one is very hard to make soft.
Emberwrath.wants: A body that carries the pair's control spell and its out-of-combat healing; this chassis has neither until character 15.
uncertain: Rage is 3 charges per long rest at Barbarian 3 — one per hard fight — so its resistance is scored as covering the fight it is spent in, not the whole cycle.
danger-sense and fanatical-focus are both partial tier; whether they jointly satisfy the two-of-Wis/Con/Dex clause is the renderer's call.

Physic.note: A Mercy Monk opened on two Bladesinger levels for Int+Wis saves and Bladesong's +2 AC, finishing Wizard 6 only in Act III. The Intelligence the school wants is the one stat this body cannot fund, so the dip is bought for the save pair, not the school.
Physic.strength: Flurry of Healing and Harm at Monk 11 turns Lone Wolf's second bonus action into two Flurries a round that damage and heal in the same swing — in a party of two, every free Hands of Healing lands on the only other body there is, and Lone Wolf's halved damage doubles each point.
Physic.wants: Area damage and area control; this body removes one enemy at a time and has nothing at all for a crowd.
uncertain: Hands of Harm is necrotic and taxed 0.5 on half of encounters from Act II per rule 4; the single-target row reads 3/2/2 if Absolute Wrath resists it more widely than assumed.
Implements of Mercy grants two skills from a list the class file does not enumerate — no Perception or Persuasion credited from it.

Mercywork.note: The same pairing run Monk-first: it trades Int+Wis saves for Str+Dex but puts Monk 8's ki, Evasion and Hands of Harm inside Act I and Diamond Soul inside Act II. Wizard 6 arrives at character 15 and is close to inert by then.
Mercywork.strength: Diamond Soul at character 14 makes all six saving throws proficient for the whole back half of the run — the largest single answer in the class to boss DCs climbing +2, bought with no feat, no gear and no concentration.
Mercywork.wants: A partner who can hold a crowd and who can talk; this body rolls a negative Persuasion in all three acts.
uncertain: Bladesong only lands at character 16 in this order, so the booster is authored from Act III.
Hand of Ultimate Mercy needs Monk 17 and is not reached; no in-combat rez is scored.

VengeancePaladin.split: Paladin 3 (Oath of Vengeance) / Monk 11 (Way of Shadow) / Cleric 6 (Twilight)
VengeancePaladin.note: A scout Monk: Shadow Arts buys Hide, Pass Without Trace and Darkness off the ki pool, and the Paladin opener buys Wis+Cha saves. It spends its concentration on Darkness and it cannot see through its own, because nothing in this split grants Devil's Sight.
VengeancePaladin.strength: A two-body party has no dedicated scout and no spare turn to make one; Shadow Arts covers stealth, repositioning and party-wide Pass Without Trace out of a pool that refills on every short rest, which is the clock this run can actually afford.
VengeancePaladin.wants: A body that can see in magical darkness, or one that will take the concentration slot so this one can stop paying for Darkness.
uncertain: Darkness is scored as area denial discounted for self-blinding; with a partner carrying Devil's Sight the area-control row is 3/3/2 instead.
Ki spent on Shadow Arts is the same ki Flurry wants; the damage row assumes utility casts come out of the spare points, not the Flurry budget.

Nightwake.split: Monk 11 (Way of Shadow) / Cleric 6 (Twilight) / Barbarian 3 (Path of the Zealot)
Nightwake.note: The same shadow scout opened on Monk, so Evasion and eight strikes a round arrive inside Act I and Twilight Sanctuary inside Act II. Barbarian's three levels come last and buy Rage without the level-1 saves, armour or Unarmoured Defence.
Nightwake.strength: Twilight Sanctuary from character 13 is a no-action aura that temp-HPs the partner every round, and in a party of two that aura covers everyone there is — it is the cheapest rung-4 Rescue in this batch and it runs on a short-rest Channel Divinity.
Nightwake.wants: Area damage and a second concentration slot; this body's is spent on Darkness and its AoE is a 0 until Act III.
uncertain: Barbarian taken at character 18 grants no saves and no Unarmoured Defence; only Rage and Zealot's reroll are scored, both from Act III.
Monk skill picks exclude Perception, Investigation and Persuasion, so all three are rolled unproficient off Wisdom, Intelligence and a dumped Charisma.

Wyrmbreath.split: Paladin 3 (Oath of the Ancients) / Monk 11 (Way of the Ascendant Dragon) / Cleric 6 (Light)
Wyrmbreath.note: The one Monk in the list with real area damage: Breath of the Dragon replaces an attack with a two-dice cone, three dice from Monk 11. It is scored in the mixed configuration — one breath a round plus what ki is left for Flurry — because a breath-every-action build empties the pool by round two.
Wyrmbreath.strength: Aspect of the Wyrm's resistance aura is the only Monk feature that hands the *other* character a defensive buff, and at a party of two the 10-ft aura covers the whole party; Draconic Strike also retunes the breath's damage type, which is how it stays relevant through Absolute Wrath.
Wyrmbreath.wants: Sustained single-target damage against bosses, and a body that will spend the concentration slot this one never uses.
uncertain: Act I is ki-starved: proficiency-bonus free breaths amortise to one per fight and Monk 5 holds six ki, so three breaths and two Flurries is the whole round budget — the damage rows would both rise a rung if the free uses were per fight rather than per long rest.
Augment Breath needs Monk 17 and is not reached, so the breath stays at three dice through Act III.

Skyfang.split: Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling) / Monk 14 (Way of the Ascendant Dragon)
Skyfang.note: The dragon Monk on a Bard opener, which buys Dex+Cha saves, Jack of All Trades and two Expertise picks — the skill coverage the class otherwise has none of. Bard 6 lands at character 18, so its college tier-2 feature is an Act III arrival.
Skyfang.strength: It is the rare body that answers a crowd and still talks its way through town: the breath cone twice a round covers Listo's added-enemy encounters, and Expertise on a Charisma skill means the duo does not need its other half to be the face.
Skyfang.wants: Single-target burst for bosses and a concentration-holding controller; this body's boss row never gets above par.
uncertain: College of Stormcalling's features are not in the read set; the college is scored as a Bard 3 skill package plus Countercharm only.
Diamond Soul lands at character 17, so all-six save proficiency is authored from Act III.

Ghostarm.split: Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Monk 11 (Way of the Astral Self) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend)
Ghostarm.note: The single-stat Monk: the astral arms attack and damage off Wisdom, so the class's usual Dex problem disappears and every point goes to Wisdom, Constitution and skills. It gives up Dex-scaled initiative and Dexterity saves without Lone Wolf's help.
Ghostarm.strength: Its strikes are force damage, which is the least resisted type in the list — nothing in Absolute Wrath's layered resistances touches this body's damage row, so its ratio holds across all three acts where every elemental chassis slides.
Ghostarm.wants: Area damage, which sits at 0 in two acts, and a body willing to hold the pair's one concentration spell.
uncertain: Perception carries Lore proficiency plus Expertise on a Wisdom primary, which is the best trap-detection total this batch produces; it still peaks near 0.75 against the 15–25 band.
Agonizing Blast from the Warlock dip is scored as a fallback only — Charisma is tertiary here, so Eldritch Blast lands well under the astral arms.

Stormform.split: Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling) / Monk 14 (Way of the Astral Self)
Stormform.note: The Wisdom-only Monk taken to 14 for Diamond Soul, with a Bard opener for Dex+Cha saves and Expertise. Two classes instead of three costs it a third body and a short-rest slot pool, and Bard 6 arrives only at character 18.
Stormform.strength: Body of the Astral Self's Deflect Energy is a reaction that eats 1d10+Wis of six damage types, and Lone Wolf grants a second reaction — this is the best user of that extra reaction in the class, twice a round, for free.
Stormform.wants: A crowd answer and a controller; its area damage and area control are both 0 or 1 in every act.
uncertain: College of Stormcalling's features are not in the read set; only the Bard 3 skill package and Countercharm are scored.
Deflect Energy is flat mitigation and is held at rung 4 rather than lifted, on the boss-weighted-act clause.

Kinlight.split: Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Monk 11 (Way of the Friar) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend)
Kinlight.note: A Friar Monk carrying **Friar's Blessing** — one blessing, chosen, not the union of four — so both bodies roll +1d4 on attacks and saves while the Bond holds. The Bond costs a ki, a bonus action and this body's only concentration slot, which is the whole price of the chassis.
Kinlight.strength: Friar's Bond covers the entire party at a party size of two, from character 6: per-turn temp HP on both bodies, a free teleport to the partner, and a shield this Monk is allowed to wear without losing Unarmoured Defence — AC 20 in Act I with no armour proficiency and no gold.
Kinlight.wants: A partner who does not need the concentration slot, since the Bond permanently occupies this one, and who brings the area damage this body has none of.
uncertain: Scored on Friar's Blessing alone. Valor, Retribution and Faith are mutually exclusive with it and none of their effects are counted anywhere in this record.
Guardian of Light grants advantage on Concentration checks with a shield equipped, authored under the war-caster id per the schema's note that the id is keyed to the effect.

Chapel.split: Paladin 3 (Oath of Devotion) / Monk 11 (Way of the Friar) / Cleric 6 (Life)
Chapel.note: The Friar Monk on a Paladin opener for Wis+Cha saves, again carrying **Friar's Blessing** only. Cleric 6 Life arrives at character 15 and adds Revivify and Disciple of Life on top of the Bond's per-turn temp HP; the Bond still eats the concentration slot, so Spirit Guardians is off the table.
Chapel.strength: Two stacked party-wide effects at a party size of two — the Bond's temp HP every turn on both bodies and a +1d4 on every save either of them rolls — against a run where a single failed save removes half the action economy.
Chapel.wants: A concentration-free crowd answer; the Bond owns this body's slot and its area damage never rises above 1.
uncertain: Scored on Friar's Blessing alone; the other three blessings are not counted.
Cleric 6 gives Revivify but not Death Ward (Cleric 7), so Rescue holds at rung 4 rather than reaching 5 in Act III.

Whetstone.split: Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling) / Monk 14 (Way of the Kensei)
Whetstone.note: A weapon Monk: kensei weapons count as monk weapons, Agile Parry buys +2 AC on nearly every turn for free, and Sharpen the Blade at Monk 11 spends three ki for +3 attack and damage for a whole minute. It reaches Monk 14 and no further, so the 1d12 Martial Arts die never arrives.
Whetstone.strength: Sharpen the Blade is a flat +3 on eight attacks a round under Lone Wolf's two Actions and two bonus actions — that is +24 raw damage per round for three ki off a short-rest pool, which is the resource clock this run can pay and long rests are not.
Whetstone.wants: Anything that touches a crowd — this body has no AoE and no area control worth a rung in any act.
uncertain: Sharpen the Blade has no effect on a weapon that already carries an enchantment bonus; the damage row assumes the mundane-weapon rule of §1, and a magic weapon deletes the Act II rung-4.
Act II spends 12 of 13 ki per fight on Sharpen, Deft Strike and two Flurries a round — the Endurance rung already prices the three refills, but nothing is left over for utility.

Keenedge.split: Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Monk 11 (Way of the Kensei) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend)
Keenedge.note: The same weapon Monk stopped at 11 to buy a Lore Bard's skills and a Warlock 3 familiar. Sharpen the Blade still lands, but Diamond Soul does not, and the extra classes cost it the last three Monk levels.
Keenedge.strength: Three short-rest pools on one body — ki, pact slots and Bardic Inspiration from Bard 5 — against a run where a long rest costs 120+ supplies; the pair can take the fights back to back that a long-rest chassis cannot.
Keenedge.wants: A crowd answer and a body to hold the concentration slot this one leaves free.
uncertain: Same mundane-weapon assumption as Whetstone: Sharpen the Blade is void on an enchanted weapon.
Bard 6 lands at character 18, so Font of Inspiration's short-rest clock only covers Act III.

Deathgrip.split: Cleric 6 (Grave) / Monk 11 (Way of the Long Death) / Paladin 3 (Oath of Vengeance)
Deathgrip.note: A Monk built around Mastery of Death — at Monk 11, dropping to 0 HP costs one ki instead of the fight. The Cleric opener buys Wis+Cha saves and Wisdom casting that shares the Monk's primary; Paladin 3 arrives at character 18 and is nearly decorative.
Deathgrip.strength: Losing either body usually ends a two-character fight, and this converts that loss into a single ki off a pool that refills on every short rest — repeatably, with no action, no slot and no concentration. Touch of Death stacks Wis+level temp HP on top of every kill.
Deathgrip.wants: A crowd answer and a face; this body has no AoE until Act III and rolls Persuasion off a dumped Charisma.
uncertain: Mastery of Death has no rung on the Durability ladder — it is repeatable death denial rather than mitigation — and is scored at 4 as rung-3-grade mitigation without the armour.
Concentration is flagged true only for the Act III Spirit Guardians line off Cleric 6; Acts I and II hold no concentration.

Gravebound.split: Cleric 6 (Grave) / Monk 11 (Way of the Long Death) / Blood Hunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer)
Gravebound.note: The same death-denial Monk with Blood Hunter instead of Paladin in the last three levels, bought for Blood Maledict rather than Crimson Rite — an unarmed Monk cannot put a rite on a weapon it is not holding.
Gravebound.strength: Blood Curses cost no slot, mostly allow no saving throw and refresh on a short rest, so they layer under Stunning Strike without touching the pair's two concentration slots — the cheapest boss debuff in this batch.
Gravebound.wants: Area damage in Acts I and II, where this body is a flat 0, and a partner who can talk.
uncertain: Blood Hunter at character 18 grants no saving throws and Crimson Rite is unusable on an unarmed routine, so only Blood Maledict and Ghostslayer's fourth curse are scored.
Intelligence drives Blood Maledict's amplified DCs and is dumped on this chassis; the curses are scored on their no-save variants only.

Topplewright.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Zealot) / Monk 11 (Way of the Open Hand) / Cleric 6 (War)
Topplewright.note: Open Hand's Topple, Push and Stagger ride the Ki Save DC in Listo, so they scale off Wisdom — the stat this body already maxes — and land on every Flurry strike for no extra action. Barbarian opens for Str+Con saves and Rage; the Cleric block is Act III only.
Topplewright.strength: The split First/Second Strike techniques let one round of Flurries put four different enemies on the floor with no concentration spent, which is the one kind of control a duo can afford: Listo adds bodies to every fight and the pair only owns two concentration slots between them.
Topplewright.wants: A body that deals real area damage; this one removes enemy turns but barely removes enemy hit points on a crowd.
uncertain: Topple and Push are Ki-Save-DC effects landing only on a hit; the area-control rung assumes the mod's split First/Second Strike variants let one Flurry pair spread across two targets.
War Priest's bonus-action attack arrives at character 15 and competes with Flurry for the same bonus actions; it is scored as Actions surplus, not as extra damage.

Fistlaw.split: Paladin 3 (Oath of Vengeance) / Monk 11 (Way of the Open Hand) / Cleric 6 (Order)
Fistlaw.note: The Open Hand control Monk on a Paladin opener for Wis+Cha saves, finishing with Order domain. It has no Rage, so it is the softer of the two Open Hand bodies, and Evasion only arrives at character 10.
Fistlaw.strength: Order's Voice of Authority turns every buff or heal aimed at the partner into a free weapon attack for them — in a two-body party that is a genuine action handed across, and it stacks on top of a Flurry routine that already prones the enemy for nothing.
Fistlaw.wants: Area damage and durability cover; this body's mitigation is Unarmoured Defence and Evasion and nothing else.
uncertain: Voice of Authority is scored as Actions rung 4 in Act III on the strength of the ladder's 'an Action handed to the other body' clause; it grants an attack rather than a full Action, so 3 is defensible.

Soul.split: Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Monk 11 (Way of the Sun Soul) / Paladin 3 (Oath of Devotion)
Soul.note: The only Way that makes a Monk a ranged character: Radiant Sun Bolt is a 30-ft spell attack on the Martial Arts die, and the bonus-action follow-up doubles under Lone Wolf. The cost is Stunning Strike — a ranged spell attack cannot carry it — so this body throws away the class's best control.
Soul.strength: A duo has no way to hold a line, and this is the one Monk that contributes full damage without walking into it: eight Sun Bolts a round at range means the single-target term takes no reach discount at all, and radiant is the second-least resisted type in the list.
Soul.wants: Hard single-target control, which this body traded away, and someone to hold the concentration slot.
uncertain: Sun Soul scales on Dexterity, not Wisdom, and does not benefit from the Ki Save DC change — so this chassis carries Monk's secondary-stat penalty without any of its Wisdom payoff.
Searing Sunburst costs 3 ki against a Flurry budget of 8; the configuration scored is one Sunburst per fight, which is why AoE peaks at 2 and then falls.

Sun.split: Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Monk 11 (Way of the Sun Soul) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend)
Sun.note: The ranged Monk with a Warlock 3 tail instead of Paladin: a Pact of the Chain familiar, two invocations and a short-rest slot pool, at the price of Wis+Cha saves the Bard opener already replaced with Dex+Cha.
Sun.strength: Two at-will ranged engines on one body — Sun Bolts off ki and Eldritch Blast off nothing — plus a familiar, means it never runs out of a turn to take, which is what a two-body party with 120-supply long rests actually needs.
Sun.wants: Hard control of any kind; single-target control sits at 1 in every act and this body has no answer to a boss's turn.
uncertain: Agonizing Blast rides Charisma, which is tertiary here, so Eldritch Blast is scored as a fallback rather than a damage engine.
Repelling Blast is the second invocation and carries the Act III area-control rung; it now allows a Strength save, so it is priced as an incidental rather than reliable displacement.

Psionaut.note: A control Sorcerer whose Psionic list — Dissonant Whispers up to Dominate Person and Evard's Black Tentacles — does not count against spells known and can be cast off sorcery points with no verbal or somatic component. Bard 6 arrives at character 15 and is what finally gives it anything to aim at its partner.
Psionaut.strength: Psionic Sorcery pays for one full control spell per fight out of a second pool, so the pair's two concentration slots stop competing with its slot budget; Summon Beholderkin from Sorcerer 7 is a third body on the initiative order in a party that only has two.
Psionaut.wants: Damage — this body is a 1 on single-target in every act and its whole plan is removing turns rather than hit points.
uncertain: Psionic Defenses (Psychic resistance, advantage on Charmed and Frightened saves) has no id in the closed booster registry and is therefore scored as nothing on the saves axis.
Sorcery points are long-rest only until Sorcerer 20, so the one-free-Evard's-per-fight figure is 14 points divided by three fights, not per short rest.

Farseer.split: Sorcerer 11 (Aberrant Mind) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend)
Farseer.note: The same psionic controller cut to Sorcerer 11 so a Lore Bard and a Warlock 3 fit underneath. It keeps Revelation in Flesh and loses Warping Implosion; the Bard block lands inside Act II, which is where its Rescue and its skills both switch on.
Farseer.strength: Three casting pools on one body — slots, sorcery points and short-rest pact slots — against a run where a long rest costs 120+ supplies, plus Psychic resistance and advantage on Charm and Frighten saves, which are the two effects most likely to take half a two-person party out of a fight.
Farseer.wants: A body that removes hit points; single-target damage sits at 1 in all three acts and the pair cannot win on control alone.
uncertain: Same registry gap as Psionaut: Psionic Defenses scores nothing on saves.
Eleven Sorcerer levels give eleven sorcery points, so Psionic Sorcery funds roughly three spell levels per fight rather than four.

Dartfall.split: Sorcerer 14 (Draconic Bloodline (vanilla) + Draconic Bloodline Expanded) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Dartfall.note: An Amethyst dragon Sorcerer: Elemental Affinity adds Charisma to every point of Force damage, which means every Magic Missile dart. Draconic Resilience patches the d6 hit die and the missing armour; what it gives up is any control feature at all.
Dartfall.strength: Magic Missile never rolls to hit, so where par is paying a 0.65 hit chance this body is not — and Force is the least resisted type in the list, so nothing Absolute Wrath layers on touches it. That combination is why its damage ratio rises across acts instead of sliding.
Dartfall.wants: Hard control and a crowd answer; this chassis is par on both control axes and never better.
uncertain: The auto-hit credit is the 0.65-to-1.0 conversion §1 allows where a chassis resolves differently from par; without it the damage row is 1/2/2.
College of Stormcalling's features are not in the read set and are scored as a Bard 3 package plus Countercharm only.

Scaleblade.split: Sorcerer 14 (Draconic Bloodline (vanilla) + Draconic Bloodline Expanded) / Bard 6 (College of Swords)
Scaleblade.note: The same Amethyst force-caster with a Swords college on the tail for medium armour, scimitars and a Fighting Style. The armour is real AC on a d6 chassis; the weapon half is not, because nothing here makes a weapon swing off Charisma.
Scaleblade.strength: A caster that never misses and never gets resisted, wearing medium armour by Act III — in a duo with no taunt the enemy AI hunts the softer body, and this is the rare full caster that is not obviously it.
Scaleblade.wants: Concentration-free control, and someone to answer crowds; both control axes sit at par all run.
uncertain: Bard 6 lands at characters 15–20, so the Swords medium armour is an Act III arrival and Durability is not lifted before then.
Same auto-hit convention as Dartfall.

Anointed.note: Favored Soul with the **Life** domain: Cure Wounds, Revivify, Death Ward, Mass Cure Wounds and Raise Dead all arrive as Sorcerer spells off Charisma, so Metamagic applies to them. It buys light and medium armour and shields at level 1 and an Extra Attack at 6 it has no attack stat for.
Anointed.strength: Twinned Death Ward and Twinned Greater Restoration cover a two-person party completely for one Metamagic pick — a party of two is the only size at which Twinned is a full-party buff — and Raise Dead on the caster chassis removes the failure mode where one body down leaves the other alone.
Anointed.wants: Damage of any kind; this body is a 1 on single-target in every act and its slots go to keeping the partner upright.
uncertain: Rescue falls from 5 to 4 in Act III because Life's list tops out at Raise Dead — nothing 9th-tier, no Mass Heal — while the act's rung 5 asks for exactly that.
Extra Attack at Favored Soul 6 is scored as nothing: no feature in this split moves weapon attacks onto Charisma.

Favored.note: Favored Soul with the **Peace** domain, which is the class's only route to Warding Bond — the pak gates it on Sorcerer 3 and no other bloodline reaches it. Sanctuary, Aura of Purity, Greater Restoration and Mass Cure Wounds come with it; damage does not.
Favored.strength: Twinned Sanctuary and Twinned Greater Restoration blanket a party of two, and Aura of Purity covers both bodies against the condition load Listo's encounters throw — prevention that costs one Metamagic point rather than a second body's turn.
Favored.wants: A damage engine; this chassis removes almost no enemy action points of its own and exists to keep the other body's supply intact.
uncertain: Warding Bond is authored in redirect, not in Rescue, per the rubric's cap; on a d6 chassis it will usually be the softer body and the renderer should transfer nothing.
