Twinned does not double Warding Bond — the pak refuses a second cast while the caster holds the status — so only Sanctuary, Greater Restoration and Mass Cure Wounds are scored as Twinned.

Illomen.split: Sorcerer 14 (Shadow Magic (vanilla) + Shadow Magic Expanded - Umbral Form) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Illomen.note: A Shadow Sorcerer built on Hound of Ill Omen — a short-rest, slot-free body that hunts one target and gives it disadvantage on saves. The split stops at Sorcerer 14, so **Umbral Form never arrives**: the subclass's Act III payoff is four levels out of reach.
Illomen.strength: The Hound is single-target lockdown that costs no slot, no concentration and no action of the partner's, on the short-rest clock this run can pay — and Strength of the Grave at level 1 keeps a d6 caster from going down in a party where one body down is half the action economy.
Illomen.wants: Area damage and a body that can absorb a hit; this chassis has neither and no Umbral Form to fall back on.
uncertain: The subclass key names Umbral Form but Sorcerer 14 cannot reach the level-18 feature; nothing from it is scored, and the split would need Sorcerer 18 to earn it.
True Darkness is not installed, so the published Shadow Sorcerer darkness builds do not apply here and no darkness cheese is credited.

Duskhound.split: Sorcerer 14 (Shadow Magic (vanilla) + Shadow Magic Expanded - Umbral Form) / Bard 6 (College of Swords)
Duskhound.note: The same Hound-centred Shadow Sorcerer with a Swords college for medium armour and a Fighting Style, arriving in Act III. Umbral Form is again out of reach at Sorcerer 14, so the chassis is its level-1 and level-6 features plus a spell list.
Duskhound.strength: Two death-denials on a caster body — Strength of the Grave regaining 1 HP at 0, and the Hound running interference on whatever is trying to kill it — in a run where losing either half of a two-person party usually ends the fight.
Duskhound.wants: Sustained damage; this body's single-target term never rises above 1 and its area term never above par.
uncertain: Umbral Form is unreachable at Sorcerer 14; see Illomen.
Swords' medium armour lands only at character 17, so Durability is authored flat rather than rising in Act III.

Galeflow.note: A lightning and thunder blaster with a bonus-action fly after every levelled cast. It is locked to two damage types that Absolute Wrath resists on roughly half of encounters from Act II, and it has no control feature of its own.
Galeflow.strength: A two-person party has no front line to hide behind, and Tempestuous Magic is a free disengage-and-fly every single turn — the caster simply is not where the melee is, which is worth more here than the Heart of the Storm chip damage it gives up by leaving.
Galeflow.wants: Hard control and a durable body to stand in front; this chassis is a 1 on both durability and single-target through Act II.
uncertain: The AoE row already carries rule 4's 0.5 multiplier on half of encounters from Act II for a lightning/thunder lock; without the tax it reads 3/4/4.
Heart of the Storm's 6 m radius contradicts Tempestuous Magic's fly-away plan; the configuration scored is fly-away, so its chip damage is not counted.

Squall2.split: Sorcerer 11 (Storm Sorcery (vanilla)) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend)
Squall2.note: The storm caster cut to 11 for a Lore Bard and a Warlock tail. Storm's Fury lands at Sorcerer 11 and the Warlock block arrives at character 18, bringing Eldritch Blast and Agonizing Blast onto a Charisma 22 body just in time for the fourth beam.
Squall2.strength: Four full Eldritch Blast beams across two Lone Wolf Actions is an at-will single-target engine that costs no slot at all, which is exactly what a long-rest caster runs out of by the third fight of a 120-supply rest cycle.
Squall2.wants: Durability cover and hard control; this body is a 1 on durability in every act and its control is plain long-rest slots.
uncertain: Eldritch Blast is 1d8 per beam in this list, not 1d10; four beams over two Actions at Charisma 22 is about 84 raw, or 1.10× par, which is what carries the Act III damage rung.
Same lightning/thunder resistance tax on the AoE row as Galeflow.

Tidebend.split: Sorcerer 14 (Wild Magic (vanilla) + Wild Magic Subclass - Additional Spells) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Tidebend.note: Wild Magic played as Bend Luck first and chaos second: a reaction that swings any visible creature's attack, check or save by ±1d4 for two sorcery points. The added subclass list — Hypnotic Pattern, Confusion, Dominate Person, Telekinesis — is castable off points via Arcane Chaos, at the cost of a guaranteed surge.
Tidebend.strength: Lone Wolf grants a second reaction and Bend Luck is the best thing in the class to spend it on: a ±1d4 on the enemy's save against the partner's control, or on a boss's attack roll against a d6 caster, is exactly the single-roll intervention a two-person party lives or dies on.
Tidebend.wants: A durable body to stand in front and a damage engine; a surge that Banishes or Confuses this chassis removes half the party outright.
uncertain: Wild Magic has no level 13–20 subclass feature — Expansion does not cover it — so nothing is scored past Controlled Chaos at 11.
Arcane Chaos casts always trigger a surge; the area-control rung assumes the pair only starts that loop in fights it can afford to lose, per the class file's own advice.

Chaosblade.split: Sorcerer 14 (Wild Magic (vanilla) + Wild Magic Subclass - Additional Spells) / Bard 6 (College of Swords)
Chaosblade.note: The same Bend Luck controller with a Swords college on the tail for medium armour and a Fighting Style, which arrives at character 17. It is the more survivable of the two Wild Magic bodies and the slower to come online.
Chaosblade.strength: Two reactions a round, both spendable on Bend Luck, on a body wearing medium armour by Act III — the pair gets a save-swinging interrupt without having to feed it the concentration slot or the softest body in the party.
Chaosblade.wants: Sustained damage and a crowd answer that does not need a surge roll to be safe.
uncertain: No Wild Magic feature exists past level 11; the Act III column is spell-list and Bard progression only.
College of Swords' medium armour is an Act III arrival at character 17.

Bloodcant.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Revenant) / Rogue 11 (Arcane Trickster) / Wizard 6 (Bladesinging)
Bloodcant.note: A Revenant opener buys Str+Con saves, a d12 hit die and flat DR 2, then eleven Rogue levels and a Bladesinger tail turn it into a Booming-Blade gish. It gives up the Rogue's own skill package — Barbarian first means one Rogue skill and no level-1 Expertise.
Bloodcant.strength: Booming Blade scales on character level, not class level, so the Rogue-11 freeze that costs every other split its Act III damage does not bite here; two Lone Wolf Actions fire two full-strength cantrip strikes plus a Sneak Attack every round with no clock at all.
Bloodcant.wants: A body that answers crowds — its area damage never gets past one 3rd-tier spell a fight and it has no outward healing whatsoever.
uncertain: Rage suppresses spellcasting, so the Barbarian block is scored as saves, hit die and Revenant's DR only — none of its Rage riders are counted on a body that must cast.
Bladesong is 2/long rest and requires light armour and a free hand; scored as one partial booster, which is what pushes Act III to rung 5 alongside Danger Sense.

Cogtrick.note: Artificer 1 opens with Int+Con saves, medium armour and shields, then a Steel Defender and infusions carry a Rogue/Bladesinger body that would otherwise be a robe. The price is the same one Bloodcant pays — Rogue as a later class means one skill and no level-1 Expertise.
Cogtrick.strength: Enhanced Weapon and Enhanced Defense are permanent stat on a duo that cannot rely on four characters' worth of loot drops, and the Steel Defender is a third initiative slot in a two-body party.
Cogtrick.wants: A body with real area damage and outward healing; this one has neither and its Steel Defender is soak, not rescue.
uncertain: Battle Smith's Steel Defender is priced as one permanent extra body (Actions rung 2); Extra Attack needs Artificer 5 and is not bought.
Artificer's half-caster rounding passive is documented as core-spellcaster-only, so the slot total under a modded Bladesinger tail is unverified.

Nightfall.split: Rogue 11 (Assassin) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend)
Nightfall.note: The alpha-strike Rogue: Alacrity restores an Action and Bonus Action at the top of the fight, and everything that has not acted is hit at advantage. Stopping at Rogue 11 freezes Sneak Attack at 6d6 and forfeits Imposter and Death Strike entirely.
Nightfall.strength: Listo's d10+Dex initiative variant means this body reliably takes the first round outright, and in a duo the first round is half the party's whole opening — but its whole plan is online by character 8 and the ratio to par falls from 1.25 to 1.05 by Act III.
Nightfall.wants: A body that still contributes on round four, and something that removes several enemies' turns at once — area control here is a single 3rd-tier spell.
uncertain: Sneak Attack is counted twice a round — own turn plus one reaction — matching the rubric's worked anchor. Lone Wolf's second reaction can make it three when opportunity attacks are actually offered; that upside is not scored.

Requiem.split: Rogue 11 (Assassin) / Cleric 6 (Trickery Domain) / Barbarian 3 (Path of the Revenant)
Requiem.note: An Assassin that buys a Cleric's 3rd-tier slots and a Revenant's flat damage reduction instead of Rogue 12–20. Invoke Duplicity gives it a decoy, Spirit Guardians gives it the crowd answer no Rogue subclass has.
Requiem.strength: Spirit Guardians is at-will while concentration holds, which in Listo's oversized encounters converts the Rogue's single-target habit into per-round area damage without spending another slot; Revenant's flat DR 2 stacks under Lone Wolf's halving.
Requiem.wants: A body that will hold the pair's other concentration slot for hard control, since this one is spending its own on Spirit Guardians.
uncertain: Barbarian 3 lands last, so its Rage is unusable alongside Cleric concentration; only Danger Sense, the hit die and Revenant's DR are scored.

Consuming Fervor (maximised Fire/Thunder Channel Divinity, twice per short rest at Cleric 6) would move AoE two rungs, but the rubric does not name its domain and Trickery is not an obvious carrier — not claimed.

Inquisitive.split: Rogue 11 (Inquisitive) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Archfey)
Inquisitive.note: The detection body. Insightful Fighting turns Sneak Attack on without an ally, Steady Eye puts advantage on Perception and Investigation permanently, and Reliable Talent floors every proficient roll at 10. It gives up Eye for Weakness at 17 and any real area damage.
Inquisitive.strength: A two-character party cannot cover this run's trap and secret-door load — the best pair in the field averages 0.60 on Perception — and this is the only chassis in the batch that fixes both checks with one feature that costs no resource and no action.
Inquisitive.wants: A body that removes several enemies' turns at once; this one is a single-target engine with one 3rd-tier area spell a fight.
uncertain: Steady Eye's advantage is folded in as a flat +4 from Act II; the schema takes finished modifiers and has no way to express advantage.
Unerring Eye's uses key off Wisdom modifier, which a Dex/Con Rogue does not have — not scored.

Augury.note: Inquisitive's detection package on a Sorcerer chassis — Con+Cha saves at level 1, medium armour and shields from Favored Soul, and Metamagic at the tail. Rogue arrives as a later class, so it loses the level-1 Expertise pair and three of its four skills.
Augury.strength: Quickened Spell against Lone Wolf's second Action is the only reliable route to three casts in a turn, and Twinned covers the entire party when the party is two people — Twinned Haste, Twinned Blur, Twinned Death Ward all cost one point per slot level.
Augury.wants: Concentration-free hard control and a second damage type; the Fireball tail is one commonly-resisted element on a body with three sorcery points to spend.
uncertain: Sorcery points equal Sorcerer class level, so a 6-level tail funds roughly two Twins or two Quickens per long rest — the tools without the fuel.

Gambit.split: Rogue 11 (Mastermind) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Great Old One)
Gambit.note: Master of Tactics makes Help a bonus action, so this body picks its partner up off the floor without spending an Action, and hands out advantage on the same clock. It gives up Soul of Deceit and Rogue's late Sneak Attack dice to buy a Bard's slots.
Gambit.strength: In a duo a downed partner is 50% of the action economy, and this is the only body in the batch that reverses that at-will, with no resource and no rest clock — Lone Wolf's second bonus action means it rarely has to choose between Help and its own off-hand attack.
Gambit.wants: A partner that converts granted advantage into a big single hit — smites, crit-fishing — and a body that answers crowds, because area damage here is one 3rd-tier spell.
uncertain: Misdirection (13) redirects an attack to a creature within 2 m — in a duo that is always the partner, so it is scored as nothing rather than as durability.
Insightful Manipulator's penalty scales with Wisdom, which a Dex Rogue does not carry.

Coilstorm.note: Three more Rogue levels than the rest of the batch buys 7d6 Sneak Attack, Blindsense and an eighth feat, at the cost of the third class entirely. Bardic Stormcalling supplies the only area damage it will ever have.
Coilstorm.strength: The extra Sneak Attack die is exactly what the other Rogue splits pay for stopping at 11 — this body holds 1.33× par into Act II where they have already fallen to 1.21× — and bonus-action Help still stands the partner back up for free.
Coilstorm.wants: A body that holds a concentration control spell and covers crowds; this one is two turns of single-target work a round and nothing else.
uncertain: Act III lands at 1.14× par — one hundredth under the rung-3 band. Scored 2; a slightly better mundane weapon assumption flips it.

Phantom.split: Rogue 11 (Phantom) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend)
Phantom.note: The only Rogue here that splits Sneak Attack across two bodies — Wails from the Grave throws half the dice at a second enemy — plus Whispers of the Dead, an on-demand short-rest grant of every skill of one ability. Ghost Walk and Death's Friend sit past Rogue 11 and are forfeited.
Phantom.strength: Whispers of the Dead is close to a cheat code when two characters have to cover every check in the campaign, and Soul Trinkets feed off kills rather than rests, which is the right currency in a run where a long rest costs 120+ supplies.
Phantom.wants: A real crowd answer — Wails is two targets, not four, and works out to under a fifth of AoE par.
uncertain: Tokens of the Departed grants advantage on Constitution and Death saves off a kill-fed economy; there is no booster id for it, so the saves rung understates this body.
Wails from the Grave computes to 0.16–0.22× AoE par — below the rung-1 floor — but is scored 1 because the Soul Trinket economy adds uses the per-long-rest count does not capture.

Pall.note: Phantom's kill-fed trinket economy under a Grave Cleric's slots: Path to the Grave opens a vulnerability window for the Sneak Attack, Spirit Guardians finally gives the Rogue a crowd answer, and Revivify arrives at Cleric 5.
Pall.strength: Path to the Grave doubles one damage instance on a short-rest clock, which is exactly the shape a burst body wants against +170% boss HP; and Grave's max-healing-at-0-HP turns the partner's cheapest heal into a full pickup.
Pall.wants: A body that holds hard single-target control, because this one's concentration is already committed to Spirit Guardians.
uncertain: Cleric levels land in Acts II–III under the assumed order, so Spirit Guardians is an Act III capability here rather than an Act II one.

Outrider.split: Rogue 11 (Scout) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Archfey)
Outrider.note: Skirmisher turns an enemy ending its turn beside you into free repositioning, and Survivalist hands over two Expertises for nothing so the Rogue's own four land where the run actually checks. Ambush Master and Sudden Strike sit past Rogue 11 and are lost.
Outrider.strength: Skirmisher is a reaction, and Lone Wolf grants two of them, so this body disengages twice a round without spending an action in encounters Listo has deliberately overpopulated.
Outrider.wants: Area damage and an area control spell — this chassis has no answer to being outnumbered beyond walking away from it.
uncertain: Ambush Master's +5 initiative and party-wide advantage mark arrive at Rogue 13; at Rogue 11 the subclass is Skirmisher and Superior Mobility only, which is why this reads as a mobility chassis rather than a tempo one.

Trailfire.note: Scout's mobility bolted to a Sorcerer opener for Con+Cha saves, medium armour and Metamagic. Rogue as a later class costs the level-1 Expertise pair, and Scout's own payoff levels at 13 and 17 are unreachable.
Trailfire.strength: Twinned Haste is the whole argument: in a two-person party one Twin covers everyone, and it hands the partner a third Action on top of Lone Wolf's second — the rung-5 clause on Actions, bought with a 6-level tail.
Trailfire.wants: A concentration-free control layer, since Haste and Fireball both want this body's own slot and its one concentration.
uncertain: Three sorcery points at Sorcerer 6 fund one Twinned Haste per long rest, so the Actions rung 3 in Act III is a per-day capability, not a per-fight one.

Unweave.split: Rogue 11 (Seeker) / Cleric 6 (Knowledge Domain) / Blood Hunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer)
Unweave.note: The counterspell-shaped Rogue: Auspicious Parry converts an incoming hit into 1 damage for a reaction, Spell Siphon interrupts an enemy cast once per short rest, and Arcane Strike is a Force Sneak Attack that ignores the usual requirements. It costs Intelligence on top of Dexterity and forbids a shield or a second weapon.
Unweave.strength: Losing either character usually ends the fight, so a 1-damage no button that Lone Wolf lets you press twice a round is worth more here than its cost implies — and Force plus Radiant from the Dawn rite sidesteps most of Absolute Wrath's layered resistances.
Unweave.wants: A crowd engine and a second concentration slot; this body spends its own on Spirit Guardians and has no area control at all before Act III.
uncertain: Conduit of the Weave's Sorcery Point income depends on enemies casting levelled spells within 18 m; against non-casters the whole Seeker kit is unfunded and Auspicious Parry stops being repeatable.
Brilliant Edge (Int as Force damage, piercing resistance) is Rogue 13 and not reached — the Force upside here is Arcane Strike only.

Nullbrand.split: Rogue 11 (Seeker) / Cleric 6 (Knowledge Domain) / Barbarian 3 (Path of the Revenant)
Nullbrand.note: Seeker's parry-and-siphon package with Revenant DR 2 and a d12 tail instead of Blood Hunter's rite. Knowledge domain feeds the Intelligence the subclass already demands.
Nullbrand.strength: Two reactions a round means Auspicious Parry and Uncanny Dodge in the same enemy turn, which is the cheapest way in the batch to make a light-armour body survive Listo's boss damage without spending a feat on armour.
Nullbrand.wants: Area damage — Spirit Guardians arrives only in Act III and this body has nothing else that touches more than one enemy.
uncertain: Barbarian 3 arrives last and cannot Rage while the Cleric block concentrates, so only Danger Sense, the hit die and Revenant's flat DR are scored.

Mindshard.split: Rogue 11 (Soulknife) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Great Old One)
Mindshard.note: The most self-sufficient Rogue in the list — weapon, accuracy fix, mobility and invisibility all come out of one Psionic Energy pool, so it needs no gear. It pays for that in damage type: Psychic Blades deal Psychic, which is among the most commonly resisted types late.
Mindshard.strength: Homing Strikes is miss-insurance, and when one character's turn is a quarter of the party's entire round a whiffed Sneak Attack costs far more than it would in a four-body party.
Mindshard.wants: A second damage type and a crowd answer; the resistance tax alone drops this body from 1.21× par to 0.91× from Act II.
uncertain: Absolute Wrath's resistance multiplier is applied at half strength: the body can fall back on a mundane finesse weapon, which is a real second damage type, but doing so forfeits Homing Strikes and the mobility. A full 0.5 on half of encounters would read 3/2/1.
The number and size of Psionic Energy Dice and their recovery rate are not stated by the mod; the Endurance rung leans on Sneak Attack being at-will rather than on the die pool.

Psiflare.split: Sorcerer 6 (Favored Soul) / Rogue 11 (Soulknife) / Warlock 3 (The Great Old One)
Psiflare.note: Soulknife on a Sorcerer opener — Con+Cha saves, medium armour and shields, Metamagic — but Rogue as a later class strips the level-1 Expertise pair, which is most of what makes a Rogue worth opening with.
Psiflare.strength: Fireball off a Twinned or Quickened cast finally gives the psychic blades a second damage type, which is the exact hole Absolute Wrath opens in a Psychic-locked body from Act II.
Psiflare.wants: Concentration-free crowd control; both this body's area options cost a slot it only has three of.
uncertain: Same half-strength Psychic resistance assumption as Mindshard.

Panache.split: Rogue 11 (Swashbuckler) / Bard 6 (College of Swords) / Warlock 3 (The Hexblade)
Panache.note: The Rogue that needs no setup body: Rakish Audacity turns Sneak Attack on whenever nothing else is crowding the target, and Dirty Tricks give it a Charisma-based disarm, blind and mockery every turn. Swashbuckler has nothing at all from 13 to 20, which stopping at 11 makes free.
Panache.strength: In a two-character party there is usually no second melee to flank with — this is the hole Rakish Audacity fills, and it is the reason this chassis keeps its damage without needing the partner to stand anywhere in particular.
Panache.wants: An area engine; Dirty Tricks are one target at a time and the Bard tail is one 3rd-tier spell a fight.
uncertain: Hex Warrior lands only in Act III under the assumed order, so the Charisma-weapon plan is not scored — Dexterity remains the attack stat throughout and Charisma funds Dirty Tricks and Panache only.
Goon's Rogue Overhaul patches Swashbuckler only at 1.2.2.0; the Rakish Sneak Attack RAW rework is absent, so the level-3 wording used here is the shipped one.

Swashbuckler.note: Swashbuckler with a Draconic tail for hit points, an unarmoured AC floor and Metamagic. It keeps the Rogue level-1 package — four skills and two Expertises — that the Sorcerer-first variants give away.
Swashbuckler.strength: Quickened Spell plus Lone Wolf's second Action lets this body throw a Fireball and still run its full attack routine in one turn, which is the only way a Rogue chassis ever touches four enemies at once.
Swashbuckler.wants: A body that holds hard control on a short-rest clock; this one's control is a per-turn Dirty Trick and nothing above 3rd tier.
uncertain: Draconic Resilience's 13 + Dex only beats light armour by a point and is scored as a hit-point rung rather than an AC one.

Cutpurse.split: Rogue 11 (Thief) / Blood Hunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer) / Bard 6 (College of Swords)
Cutpurse.note: Fast Hands on top of Lone Wolf's second bonus action is three bonus actions a round, which is a fifth attack every turn; Crimson Rite puts a permanent 1d4 on all of them and Swords adds Two-Weapon Fighting. It gives up Use Magic Device and Thief's Reflexes at 13 and 17.
Cutpurse.strength: Five attacks a round against a par of four is the largest raw action-economy purchase three levels can buy, and the Rite is a one-time bonus action that lasts until long rest — it costs nothing per fight in a run where rests cost 120+ supplies.
Cutpurse.wants: Area damage and outward healing; this chassis is the batch's cleanest single-target engine and does literally nothing else.
uncertain: Fast Hands is assumed to stack with Lone Wolf's second bonus action for three total; the class file asserts the stack but does not name the cap.
Crimson Rite's 1d4 is a flat rider, so its 1.55× par in Act II decays to 1.34× in Act III on the ratio alone — no extra decay applied on top.

Pilfer.split: Rogue 11 (Thief) / Bard 6 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend)
Pilfer.note: Thief's third bonus action carrying a fifth attack every round, with a Lore Bard's slots and Expertises behind it and a feat-neutral Warlock 3 for a familiar and two short-rest slots. Rogue 13 and 17 are given away.
Pilfer.strength: Eldritch Blast keys beams off character level, so three Warlock levels on a character-20 body still fire four full beams — a real ranged option on a melee chassis for levels that also pay their own feat.
Pilfer.wants: A crowd engine; five single-target attacks a round do nothing about being outnumbered, which is what Listo's added encounters are for.
uncertain: Charisma sits around 12–14 on this body, so the four Eldritch Blast beams are worth roughly 26 raw per Action — a fallback, not a competitor to the attack routine.

FavoredSorcerer.note: A Sorcerer opener for Con+Cha saves, medium armour and shields, then fourteen Archfey levels: Fey Presence as short-rest area charm-or-fear, Chains of Carceri at 12, and Eldritch Cone as the actual damage engine. It never reaches Mystic Arcanum above 7th.
FavoredSorcerer.strength: Pact slots refill on a short rest, so this body opens every fight with its full casting pool where a full caster is dividing a long-rest table by three — and Eldritch Cone is at-will four-target save-for-half damage twice a round, which no slot-based engine can repeat.
FavoredSorcerer.wants: Outward healing and revival; this chassis prevents damage to enemies well and does nothing at all to keep its partner standing.
uncertain: Eldritch Cone freezes at 3d10 from character 10 and never checks Agonizing Blast; the ratio still reads 3.6× par in Act II and 3.2× in Act III, so the decay is recorded in the note rather than as a rung drop.
Archfey gets no 14th-level feature from Expansion and no other mod was found filling the gap, so Warlock 14 here buys Arcanum 7th and nothing subclass-side.

Thistle.note: The same Archfey blaster with a Draconic tail for hit points and an unarmoured AC floor, plus a single Monk level. It is a feat down on every other Warlock 14 split and has no healing at all.
Thistle.strength: Fey Presence is an area charm-or-fear on a short-rest clock from level 1, which is how a two-body party survives being outnumbered — and it costs no concentration, so the pair's two slots stay free.
Thistle.wants: Any rescue at all — prevention, revival or outward healing — and a body that can absorb a hit, because this one is a d8 caster in cloth.
uncertain: Monk 1 contributes almost nothing to a Charisma caster — Unarmoured Defence keys off Dexterity and Wisdom — and it breaks the three-level feat block, costing a feat outright. Scored as hit points and a filler level.

Radiance.note: One of only three Charisma casters in the list with real healing. Healing Light is a bonus-action heal that spends no slot, Revivify arrives at Warlock 5 on a short-rest slot, and Eldritch Cone supplies the damage. The cost is that Healing Light's pool is on the long-rest clock.
Radiance.strength: A bonus-action heal stacks with an Action and Lone Wolf's second Action in the same turn, and in a duo where losing either character ends the fight that is the single most valuable thing on the list — with Revivify sitting on a slot that comes back every short rest.
Radiance.wants: A body that can hold a concentration control spell and stand in front; this one is a light-armour caster whose own concentration is usually committed.
uncertain: Celestial Resistance's temp HP for the partner is out-of-combat only, so it is scored as a between-fights rescue rung rather than an in-combat aura.
Persuasion assumes the Beguiling Influence invocation, which Warlock's own skill list does not otherwise offer.

Beacon.note: Celestial's healing package with a Bladesinger tail bought for +2 AC, +2 Constitution saves and a transcribable scroll library rather than for its casting. Intelligence competes with Charisma the whole way and the Wizard slots stay at 3rd tier.
Beacon.strength: Bladesong is the cheapest concentration insurance in the list for a body in cloth, and Listo's scroll drops turn two Wizard levels into a permanent, slot-castable library that a Warlock's tiny spells-known list otherwise cannot hold.
Beacon.wants: A crowd-control layer and a front-line body; this chassis is damage and healing with almost no way to remove an enemy's turn outside its pact slots.
uncertain: Bladesong requires light armour and a free hand and runs 2/long rest, so it is authored as a partial booster; it does not reach rung 5 alone.
Warlock pact slots do not combine with the Wizard table in BG3, so the Wizard block is scored as its own level-6 progression.

Brimstone.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Revenant) / Warlock 11 (The Fiend) / Cleric 6 (Light Domain)
Brimstone.note: A Revenant opener buys Str+Con saves, heavy armour proficiency, a d12 hit die and flat DR 2 for a Fiend blaster; Light domain adds Warding Flare and a second Fireball route. Warlock stops at 11, so Chains of Carceri and Hurl Through Hell are both forfeited.
Brimstone.strength: Fiend's expanded list puts Fireball on short-rest pact slots — two upcast casts every single fight from Act I, which is 2.2× area par when a long-rest caster is rationing one — and Dark One's Blessing turns each kill into temp HP on the squishier half of a two-body party.
Brimstone.wants: Hard single-target control on a short-rest clock; without Warlock 12 this body's boss answer is Command and a 6th-level Arcanum once a day.
uncertain: Rage is unusable on a body whose whole plan is casting, so Barbarian 3 is scored as saves, hit die, Danger Sense and Revenant's DR only.
Six feats against a seven-to-eight-feat Act III budget: the split's three-class shape costs one.

Bargain.note: The durable blaster: Dark One's Blessing, Dark One's Own Luck at 6 and Fiendish Resilience at 10, with Favored Soul's medium armour and shields under it and Chains of Carceri at Warlock 12. It gives up any Arcanum above 7th.
Bargain.strength: Losing a character usually ends the fight, so survivability on the Charisma caster is worth more here than on a four-person team — and Fiend's Fireball on short-rest pact slots means the area damage arrives every fight rather than three times a day.
Bargain.wants: Outward healing or revival, and a body willing to be hit first; this one is tough for a caster and still the softer half of most pairs.
uncertain: Hurl Through Hell (Fiend 14, from Expansion) would lift Act III single-target to 1.62× par and rung 4 if it recharges on a short rest; its Listo cadence is unverified, so it is not scored.

Whisper.split: Sorcerer 6 (Favored Soul) / Warlock 14 (The Great Old One)
Whisper.note: Mortal Reminder frightens on a crit, and a blaster throwing six to eight Eldritch Blast beams a round crits far more often than the feature's wording suggests. Entropic Ward, Thought Shield and Create Thrall fill the back half; Arcanum stops at 7th.
Whisper.strength: Fear that fires off the attack routine costs no concentration and no slot, which matters exactly because the pair holds only two concentration slots between them — and Chains of Carceri adds Hold Monster on a short-rest clock without spending one.
Whisper.wants: Outward healing and a body that can hold the line; this chassis has no rescue before its Sorcerer tail and never carries armour worth the name.
uncertain: Mortal Reminder's crit-triggered fear is scored as an area-control layer on the strength of beam count; the actual crit rate depends on gear this scoring rule excludes.
Create Thrall (14) is priced as one controlled body, one rung of Actions surplus, not as a full extra character.

Fathom.split: Sorcerer 5 (Draconic Bloodline) / Warlock 14 (The Great Old One) / Monk 1 (none)
Fathom.note: The Great Old One blaster with a Draconic tail for hit points instead of Favored Soul's armour and healing, plus a single Monk level. One feat down on the two-class variants, and with no rescue at all.
Fathom.strength: Every beam is a chance at Mortal Reminder's fear, which is free area control on a body already spending both Actions on Eldritch Cone — in a duo, an enemy that runs is an enemy that spends its turn not attacking either of you.
Fathom.wants: Any outward healing, and a durability floor; this is the softest body in the batch and the pair's Durability is its weaker half.
uncertain: Monk 1 is scored as a filler level; it buys no saves (Sorcerer is the level-1 class) and its Unarmoured Defence keys off two stats this body dumps.

Hexbind.note: Hexblade's Curse adds proficiency bonus to every damage roll against the cursed target, and a character-20 body fires eight Eldritch Blast beams a round — so the curse is worth +48 raw damage per round, not +6. Master of Hexes at 14 spreads it on a kill.
Hexbind.strength: The curse recharges on a short rest, which is once per fight in this run's three-fights-per-cycle arithmetic, so it runs at full uptime — and it is the only thing in the batch that makes a chassis rise from 1.04× par in Act I to 1.74× in Act III instead of being outrun.
Hexbind.wants: A body that keeps it alive; it is a light-armour caster in melee range whenever it binds a weapon, with no self-healing above Armour of Hexes.
uncertain: Hexblade's Curse is scored as adding proficiency bonus per damage roll, i.e. per beam. If Listo applies it once per turn instead, Act III falls from rung 4 to rung 3.
Configuration fixed as blast-plus-curse rather than Pact of the Blade melee; the blade line computes to 3/3/2 and is strictly worse from Act II.

Grudge.split: Warlock 11 (The Hexblade) / Cleric 6 (War Domain) / Barbarian 3 (Path of the Revenant)
Grudge.note: The melee Hexblade: Hex Warrior puts Charisma on the weapon at level 1, Deepened Pact adds Extra Attack at 5, and War Priest adds bonus-action swings on a short-rest clock. Warlock stops at 11, so there is no Chains of Carceri and no Master of Hexes.
Grudge.strength: One stat runs the whole body — attacks, damage, save DC and the party's dialogue — which is the only way a two-character party affords a front-line fighter and a face, and War Priest's bonus attacks double under Lone Wolf's second bonus action.
Grudge.wants: Hard control the pair can rely on; this body's boss answer is a Command off a pact slot and nothing above 5th tier.
uncertain: Barbarian 3 arrives last and cannot Rage on a body that casts and concentrates; scored for Revenant's heavy armour and flat DR, the d12 and Danger Sense.

Eldritch Cone is kept on a melee Hexblade — the invocation does not require a free hand, but it does compete with the attack routine for the two Actions. AoE is scored at one Action's worth of Cone plus one round of attacks.

Warpsong.note: Every Eldritch Blast applies Warp, and Warp detonates for 1d10 Force in a 3 m radius, scaling to 4d10 by character 17. Perils of the Warp pays for it out of the caster's own maximum hit points, every turn, and the mitigation is a level-10 feature.
Warpsong.strength: Force is the least-resisted damage type in the run, and this is the only chassis in the batch that turns a single-target cantrip into repeating area damage with no slot, no concentration and no rest clock — Eldritch Cone rides on top of it.
Warpsong.wants: Sustained outward healing and a body that can carry the pair's durability floor; this one is deliberately bleeding maximum hit points and there is no third character to cover it.
uncertain: Whether Warp detonations count as Eldritch Blast for Agonizing Blast or Mizora's rider system is unverified; detonation damage is scored without the Charisma modifier.
The patron is flagged 'for testing' in Listo's own changelog, so every number here is less settled than the rest of the batch.
Endurance is scored low because the max-HP drain forces long rests rather than because the damage has a clock — the damage itself is at-will.

Riftblade.note: The same Warp engine with a Swords Bard tail for medium armour, scimitars and a fighting style instead of Stormcalling's lightning. It buys back a little of the durability Perils of the Warp keeps taking away, and gives up the Bard's own area damage.
Riftblade.strength: Chaos Rift at 14 Warps every foe in a 6 m radius and can land Paralyzed, Frozen or Confusion on all of them at once, which is a whole encounter's worth of removed action points from one Action in a party that only has four.
Riftblade.wants: Healing that arrives every round, not every fight — the max-HP drain is continuous and nothing on this body reverses it.
uncertain: Same unverified Warp/Agonizing-Blast interaction and same 'for testing' caveat as Warpsong.
Medium armour from College of Swords conflicts with nothing here, but it arrives only in Act III under the assumed level order.

Pirouette.split: Sorcerer 6 (Favored Soul) / Bard 11 (College of Dance) / Druid 3 (Circle of the Moon)
Pirouette.note: A Dexterity unarmed dancer bolted onto a caster-20 slot table: Favored Soul buys medium armour and shields, Druid 2 buys a permanent familiar, and Bard 11 supplies Expertise ×4 and Magical Secrets. It gives up Extra Attack entirely, so its melee never reaches par and its real output is spells.
Pirouette.strength: Twinned Death Ward covers the whole party because the party is two, and Agile Strikes turns every Bardic Inspiration handed to the partner into a free kick — an inspiration economy that pays twice in a duo.
Pirouette.wants: A body that actually removes a boss's action points per round, because this one's single-target line never clears par.
uncertain: Druid dip subclass is my choice, not the search's; Circle of the Moon picked for Wild Shape as an emergency HP bar. Wild Companion (Druid 2) is what the actions rung is actually paying for.
College of Dance's Tandem Footwork and Leading Evasion are unverified in the class file; nothing above is scored off them.

Tarantella.note: The pure dancer — unarmed damage rides the Inspiration die (1d10 at Bard 14, one short of the d12) with no Extra Attack, so it swings twice a round where par swings four times. Everything it gives up in weapon slots it gets back as a full 20-caster-level slot table.
Tarantella.strength: Dance needs no weapon proficiency and no second attack stat, so the whole feat budget goes into Charisma and defence; and Lone Wolf's second bonus action lets Inspiring Movement and the Agile Strikes kick both land every round.
Tarantella.wants: A partner that carries the single-target kill, and one that will spend the Inspiration dice this body cannot stop generating.
uncertain: Act III st = 0 is the computed melee configuration (3 strikes × 1d10+Dex = 34 raw vs par 76). The same body can cast instead; rule 3 forced one configuration and I scored the dancer.
Act III dur 3 credits Leading Evasion (Bard 14 with the Level 20 patch) as Evasion-grade; the class file marks it unverified.

Silvertongue.split: Fighter 1 (none) / Bard 14 (College of Eloquence) / Warlock 5 (The Great Old One)
Silvertongue.note: A heavy-armoured control Bard whose damage is entirely Agonizing Eldritch Blast — four Force beams twice a round by character 20 — with Unsettling Words as a bonus-action save debuff that costs no concentration. It gives up any weapon routine and every Act I damage rung to get there.
Silvertongue.strength: Unsettling Words rolls the die before you commit, so the pair's one concentration slot is only ever spent on a control spell you already know will land; and Unfailing Inspiration means a die handed to the other body is never wasted.
Silvertongue.wants: Crowd clearance and a body that can hold a second concentration effect, since this one's slot is permanently booked on hard control.
uncertain: Silver Tongue (Eloquence 3) is on the mod's own Known Issues list as possibly broken; the Persuasion modifiers above do not credit it.
Level order assumed Fighter 1 → Bard 10 by character 15 → Warlock 5 in Act III's back half; a Warlock-early order would raise Act I st to 1 and lower Act II aoe.

Demagogue.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Revenant) / Bard 11 (College of Eloquence) / Cleric 6 (Peace)
Demagogue.note: A Barbarian-opened save chassis — Str and Con from level 1, Revenant heavy armour and flat DR 2, Danger Sense — running an Eloquence control list and Peace's Emboldening Bond. Rage itself is nearly dead weight here, because raging blocks the spellcasting that is the whole point.
Demagogue.strength: Emboldening Bond puts a permanent d4 on both characters' attacks, checks and saves, and with only two bodies the Peace bonds cover the entire party rather than half of it.
Demagogue.wants: Damage — both damage axes sit at 0–2 and this body will never close a fight on its own.
uncertain: Barbarian Rage blocks spellcasting, so a Barbarian-first caster gets level-1 value (saves, d12, armour) and Danger Sense and essentially nothing else from the class. I picked Revenant precisely because heavy armour and DR 2 are not rage-gated.
Act III dur drops to 3 because Revenant's DR 2 is flat-only, which the rubric prices a rung below its raw numbers in a boss-weighted act.

Mantle.split: Fighter 1 (none) / Bard 14 (College of Glamour) / Warlock 5 (The Fiend)
Mantle.note: Heavy armour from Fighter 1, Eldritch Blast for at-will Force damage, and Glamour's Mantle of Inspiration as a bonus-action temp-HP pump on a short-rest clock. It buys durability and outward support at the cost of every Act I damage rung.
Mantle.strength: Unbreakable Majesty makes the first attack on this body each turn cost the attacker a Charisma save — in a two-character party where losing one member ends the fight, an aggro shed is worth more than a damage rung.
Mantle.wants: Area damage; the pair will still be standing at round six with the crowd intact unless the other body clears it.
uncertain: Unbreakable Majesty arrives at Bard 14, i.e. deep in Act III; the Act III dur 4 rests on it and on nothing else.

Pageant.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Revenant) / Bard 11 (College of Glamour) / Cleric 6 (Life)
Pageant.note: The healer half of Glamour: Mantle of Inspiration's temp HP stacked on Life's Disciple of Life, behind Revenant heavy armour and a Barbarian save base. It has no damage engine at all and does not pretend to.
Pageant.strength: Every point healed is doubled by Lone Wolf's halved incoming damage, and out-of-combat healing directly buys long rests back in a run where one costs 120+ supplies.
Pageant.wants: Both damage axes — this body is 0–2 on single-target and area in every act.
uncertain: Act III rsc held at 4 rather than 5: caster level 17 does reach a 9th slot and Mass Heal, but the rubric's Act III rung 5 also asks for Legendary rescue gear, which rule 1 excludes.

Almanac.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Revenant) / Bard 11 (College of Lore) / Cleric 6 (Knowledge)
Almanac.note: The skill chassis of the batch: Lore's three bonus proficiencies, Bard Expertise ×4, Jack of All Trades and Knowledge's two Expertise picks, wrapped in Revenant heavy armour so it is not a liability in a fight. It has no damage engine.
Almanac.strength: Two characters must clear every check in the campaign and `Use Highest Modifier in dialogue` hands the party-best total to the host — so one body carrying Perception, Investigation and Persuasion this far above the DC bands genuinely covers the run's untelegraphed half.
Almanac.wants: A body that removes enemy action points, permanently or temporarily; this one contributes almost none of the pair's tempo.
uncertain: Act III skills credit Peerless Skill (Lore 14) — but the split is Bard 11, so it is NOT included; the numbers are Expertise ×4 plus Knowledge Expertise plus a Wis 16 from Lone Wolf.
Knowledge domain is my pick for the Cleric 6; the class file's dip table does not list it among the heavy-armour domains, so the heavy armour above comes from Revenant, not the domain.

Peerless.note: A full caster at the level-20 slot table with Lore's Cutting Words reaction, Expertise ×4 and Magical Secrets ×4, plus Metamagic. Favored Soul's medium armour and shields are the only concession to being hit at all.
Peerless.strength: Twinned Death Ward, Twinned Greater Restoration and Twinned Haste each cover the entire party because the party is two — a Sorcerer dip buys a rescue rung here that costs other chassis six levels.
Peerless.wants: A front body that can hold a line, because this one is medium armour at rung 2 durability and the enemy AI picks by softness.
uncertain: Act III skills credit Peerless Skill (Lore 14, dialogue-usable) as roughly +2 on the Persuasion line; the class file describes it as a self-buff applied pre-emptively, so the exact dialogue interaction is a judgement.
aoe scored at the control-leaning quarter-of-slots split, not the half default — a Lore Bard's Magical Secrets go to control and rescue. A blaster configuration of the same split would read 2/3/4.

Squall.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Revenant) / Bard 11 (College of Stormcalling) / Cleric 6 (Tempest)
Squall.note: A thunder-and-lightning blaster: Stormcalling's Conductor and Staccato Lightning under Tempest's Destructive Wrath, which maximises every lightning or thunder die twice per short rest. It stops one College level short of Electrifying Aria, which is where the subclass actually pays.
Squall.strength: Two maximised area casts every fight on a short-rest clock is exactly the resource shape a 120-supply long rest rewards, and Chorus of Thunder's Concussion denies an enemy its reaction — worth more when there are only two of you to be reacted at.
Squall.wants: Single-target kill pressure, and a body that does not care about layered lightning resistance.
uncertain: Absolute Wrath: the whole engine is Lightning and Thunder, so I applied a ×0.85 resistance multiplier rather than the ×0.75 a single-type body would take. A strip or Elemental Adept would remove it.
ctrl_s 4 rests on Chorus of Thunder's Concussion being repeatable and costing no concentration — it costs one Bardic Inspiration, a short-rest resource at Bard 5+.

Aria.note: The full Stormcalling package: Electrifying Aria at Bard 14 is one Action buying a 12m field that repeats for ten turns, degrades every caught enemy's Constitution save each turn, and then converts into Finale!'s mass stun. Fighter 1 pays for the heavy armour it stands in.
Aria.strength: One Action buying an entire fight of area damage and save degradation is the trade a two-character party wants most, and the Aria simultaneously drops the partner's crit threshold — a buff that covers 50% of the party rather than 25%.
Aria.wants: A boss answer; the single-target row never leaves rung 1 and the Aria is indifferent to which enemy matters.
uncertain: Electrifying Aria and Finale! land at Bard 14, i.e. character 15+ on this level order — the whole Act III lift is one level deep and Act II sees none of it.
Stormcalling entered Listo on a playtesting footing per the class file; treat every number keyed to it as less battle-tested than the vanilla Colleges.

Favoredsoul.note: The martial Bard: Extra Attack at College 6, six Flourishes, and Master's Flourish at 14 letting you roll a d6 instead of spending Inspiration. The arithmetic is unkind — four rapier attacks and an at-will d6 is 0.75× par by Act III, so this is a caster that also swings.
Favoredsoul.strength: Goon's Flourish interrupts convert Lone Wolf's spare second Reaction into damage, and Favored Soul's shields plus Defensive Flourish keep a Charisma caster standing in melee without a Fighter dip.
Favoredsoul.wants: A body that actually kills things; this one's single-target line is being outrun in every act after the first.
uncertain: Sorcerer-first level order costs this chassis its Act I: at character 8 it is Sorcerer 6 / Bard 2, with no Extra Attack and no Flourishes. A Bard-first order would read st 2/1/1 instead.
The class file warns explicitly not to plan a Swords Bard around Arcane Acuity; nothing above does.

Riposte.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of Ginnungagap) / Bard 11 (College of Swords) / Cleric 6 (Zeal)
Riposte.note: The one Barbarian-first Bard where Rage is not wasted: a Swords Bard's damage is weapon-based, so Reckless Attack's near-permanent Advantage applies and Ginnungagap's spell-save Advantage is live while it rages. Zeal buys heavy armour and a bonus-action attack.
Riposte.strength: Reckless Attack is far cheaper here than in a four-party — Lone Wolf already halves everything coming back — and Ginnungagap's Advantage on spell saves is a blanket answer to the caster-heavy encounters the list adds.
Riposte.wants: Area damage and a concentration holder, since raging shuts this body's own spell list off.
uncertain: I applied Advantage as a ×1.25 uplift on attack damage rather than the ×1.35 the h convention implies, because enemy AC is not recoverable from the manifest and Advantage's value shrinks as hit chance rises.
rage-of-ginnungagap is authored on all three acts, but its value is gated on actually raging — which costs this body its spell list for the duration.

Dirge.split: Fighter 1 (none) / Bard 14 (College of Tragedy) / Warlock 5 (The Great Old One)
Dirge.note: A reaction chassis: Poetry in Misery refunds an Inspiration every time anyone nearby rolls a natural 1, Tale of Hubris drops a crit threshold, and Sorrowful Fate rewrites a target's save into a Charisma save. Damage is Eldritch Blast and nothing else.
Dirge.strength: Lone Wolf grants a second Reaction, so Poetry in Misery and Tale of Hubris are both live in the same round — this is the subclass that most directly converts Lone Wolf's spare economy into resource.
Dirge.wants: A crowd answer, and a body sturdy enough that Nimbus of Pathos is never the least-bad option.
uncertain: Nimbus of Pathos drops the target to 0 HP when it ends, which in a duo is 50% of the action economy — I scored it as worth nothing and treated it as a liability, not a rescue rung.
Tragedy's feature names are unverified in the class file (the mod page renders them as images); the effects are verified.

Threnody.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of the Revenant) / Bard 11 (College of Tragedy) / Cleric 6 (Twilight)
Threnody.note: Tragedy's reaction economy behind Revenant heavy armour, with Twilight bought for Twilight Sanctuary — a no-action temp-HP aura on a Channel Divinity clock. No damage engine of any kind.
Threnody.strength: Twilight Sanctuary costs no action and refreshes temp HP on the partner every round, and with Short Rest Full Heal off and Camp Cost 3 that directly buys long rests back.
Threnody.wants: Both damage axes; this body removes almost no enemy action points permanently.
uncertain: Twilight Sanctuary needs Cleric 2, which on a Barbarian-3-then-Bard-11 order does not land until Act III; Acts I and II are scored without it.

Fanfare.split: Sorcerer 6 (Favored Soul) / Bard 11 (College of Valour) / Paladin 3 (Oath of Devotion)
Fanfare.note: Valour buys shields and martial weapons and Extra Attack at 6; Paladin 3 buys Divine Smite, which converts any slot from any of the three classes into weapon damage. Caster level 18 means about twenty slots to spend, and half of them go to smites.
Fanfare.strength: The smite pool here is fed by a near-full-caster slot table rather than a half-caster's, which is the one configuration where a long-rest smite budget survives being amortised over three fights and four rounds.
Fanfare.wants: A concentration holder and a crowd answer; this body's slots are booked on smites and its area line only reaches rung 3 in Act III.
uncertain: Paladin 3 is below Aura of Protection, so no aura-of-protection booster; the saves rung is the four-disjoint set alone.
Smite arithmetic: ~20 slots, half to damage = 3.3 per fight at ~5d8, which is ~19 raw per round against par 76 — real, but still less than one at-will Improved Divine Smite would give.

Clarion.split: Sorcerer 6 (Favored Soul) / Bard 11 (College of Valour) / Warlock 3 (The Hexblade)
Clarion.note: A one-stat martial: Hexblade puts Charisma on the weapon, Valour supplies Extra Attack and shields, and Agonizing Eldritch Blast is the ranged fallback. Everything runs off Charisma, so the whole feat budget goes to Charisma and defence.
Clarion.strength: Because there is only one attack stat to fund, this body can afford both an at-will Force option that nothing in Absolute Wrath resists and a melee routine — and Warlock's pact slots come back on the short rest a 120-supply long rest makes precious.
Clarion.wants: Crowd clearance and a concentration holder; this chassis is rung 2 on both damage axes and never spikes.
uncertain: The Hexblade is my pick for the Warlock 3 boon; the class file's dip section covers Warlock levels but not the patron list, so Hex Warrior's exact Listo implementation is unverified.
Eldritch Blast is 1d8 per beam here, four beams at character 20 — 84 raw per round, 1.10× par III. That is the ceiling of this chassis's single-target line.

Conqueror.split: Paladin 14 (Oath of Conquest) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Conqueror.note: Conquering Presence is an Action that frightens everything in 30 ft on a Channel Oath charge and costs no concentration, and Aura of Conquest then bills every frightened enemy half the paladin level in psychic each turn. The Bard 6 dip is there for the slot table and Expertise, not for a second engine.
Conqueror.strength: A short-rest area control that never touches the pair's two concentration slots is strictly additional rather than substitutional, and Guided Strike's +10 chosen after seeing the roll guarantees the one attack a duo cannot afford to miss.
Conqueror.wants: Area damage — the frighten aura removes turns but leaves the crowd alive, and this body's own aoe never clears rung 1.
uncertain: Lone Wolf's +4 is on Strength and Constitution, so Dexterity is unproficient and the four-disjoint set misses one key save; the rung comes from Aura of Protection as a blanket booster, not from coverage.
Aura of Conquest's damage was discounted by the 0.55 save-fail chance and by requiring the enemy to start its turn in the aura, which is why aoe reads 1 rather than 2.

Tyrant.split: Paladin 14 (Oath of Conquest) / Bard 6 (College of Swords)
Tyrant.note: The same Conquest control package with Swords instead of Stormcalling — the Bard 6 Extra Attack is redundant against the Paladin's, so what it actually buys is Flourishes, a Fighting Style and Expertise ×2. It gives up any area damage at all.
Tyrant.strength: Conquering Presence plus Aura of Conquest means one Channel Oath charge per fight strips turns off the whole crowd without spending a concentration slot, which is the resource a two-body party has exactly two of.
Tyrant.wants: Crowd clearance; this chassis is 0 on the area damage axis in all three acts and control alone does not end fights.
uncertain: Conquest tags the character as Oath of Vengeance for all oathbreaking rules per the mod's own warning — a roleplay constraint, not a scoring one, but it is real.
Invincible Conqueror is the level-20 capstone and this split stops at Paladin 14, so none of the capstone's value is scored.

Sanctify.split: Paladin 14 (Oath of Devotion) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Sanctify.note: Sacred Weapon adds Charisma to attack rolls on a short-rest charge, which is the one thing that moves a Paladin's hit chance above par; Aura of Devotion hands the partner charm immunity from level 7. The Bard 6 dip supplies slots, Expertise and a Staccato Lightning bonus action.
Sanctify.strength: Charm immunity covering both characters at 9m answers the list's revamped enemy casters directly, and in a duo an aura that reaches the partner covers 50% of the party rather than 25%.
Sanctify.wants: Area damage and area control — this body clears rung 1 on neither and Listo's encounters add bodies specifically to punish that.
uncertain: st 3 in every act credits Sacred Weapon as roughly a ×1.25 uplift on attack damage for the fight it covers (one Channel Oath charge, refreshed on each short rest, three per long-rest cycle).

Smite budget: Paladin 14 / Bard 6 is caster level 13, ~17 slots, and the 5th–7th slots have nothing to cast but upcast smites — which is the only reason this chassis's long-rest pool reaches ~18 raw per round.

Devout.split: Paladin 14 (Oath of Devotion) / Bard 6 (College of Swords)
Devout.note: The plainest body in the batch: heavy armour, shield, Improved Divine Smite, Sacred Weapon, Aura of Protection and Aura of Devotion. Swords adds a Fighting Style, Flourishes and Expertise ×2 and nothing else the Paladin does not already have.
Devout.strength: Two blanket save auras stacked on one body cover both characters at 9m, and with Listo's boss spell save DCs climbing +1/+2/+2 that is the axis where standing still costs the most.
Devout.wants: Everything the crowd side of the square needs — this chassis is 0 on area damage and 1 on area control in every act.
uncertain: Bard 6's Extra Attack is redundant against the Paladin's and is scored as worth nothing; the six levels buy slots, Expertise ×2 and Song of Rest.

Enmity.split: Paladin 14 (Oath of Vengeance) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Enmity.note: The damage oath: Vow of Enmity is Advantage on one target for a Channel Oath charge, which with four attacks a round is worth more here than to any normal party member. Abjure Enemy frightens without concentration. It has no crowd answer at all.
Enmity.strength: Lone Wolf's second Action doubles the number of attacks that ride each Vow of Enmity charge, so a short-rest resource that a four-party would spread thin covers a whole boss fight here.
Enmity.wants: Area damage and area control — the aoe row peaks at 1 and this body's whole plan is one target at a time.
uncertain: The st row falls from 4 to 3 between Acts II and III because Vow of Enmity's Advantage multiplier is scale-invariant while par carries the ×2.26 enemy HP — the body has not got worse, the world moved past it.
Advantage priced at ×1.25 rather than the ×1.35 the h=0.65 convention implies; see the batch caveat.

Reprisal.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of Ginnungagap) / Paladin 11 (Oath of Vengeance) / Cleric 6 (Zeal)
Reprisal.note: Barbarian first for Strength and Constitution saves and Reckless Attack, Paladin 11 for Improved Divine Smite and Aura of Protection, Zeal for heavy armour and a bonus-action attack. It forfeits the Paladin's own Wisdom and Charisma save proficiencies to get them.
Reprisal.strength: Reckless Attack's permanent Advantage is much cheaper in a duo where Lone Wolf already halves everything coming back, and it stacks under Improved Divine Smite's at-will 1d8 on all four attacks a round.
Reprisal.wants: A crowd answer and a concentration holder; raging shuts this body's Cleric and Paladin spell lists off entirely.
uncertain: Divine Smite is a weapon action rather than a spell in BG3 and is assumed usable while raging; the Cleric and Paladin spell lists are not, which is why aoe stays 0 until Spirit Guardians arrives in Act III.
Strength reaches 20 only around character 12 on this build, because Lone Wolf's +4 went to Wisdom and Dexterity for save coverage — Act I damage per hit is scored at +3, not +5.

Warding.note: Two defensive auras on one body — Aura of Protection at 6 and Aura of Warding at 7, the latter giving both characters resistance to spell damage — with War Priest supplying a bonus-action attack and Cleric 5 supplying Spirit Guardians. It has no skills to speak of, because Cleric grants none.
Warding.strength: Aura of Warding is proportional rather than flat, so it does not decay against the run's inflated damage, and it reaches the partner — a resistance covering half the party from one body is the best defensive six levels a Charisma character can buy.
Warding.wants: Skill coverage; Perception and Investigation here are effectively unrolled, and the partner has to carry the run's untelegraphed checks alone.
uncertain: Act III aoe 3 is Spirit Guardians as at-will area damage while concentration holds, per the rubric's own anchor — but it books this body's one concentration slot, so the pair's ctrl_a cannot also claim it.
Cleric 6 lands at characters 15–20 on a Paladin-first order, so Acts I and II see neither Spirit Guardians nor the second Channel Divinity charge.

Evergreen.note: The same double-aura Ancients anchor with Zeal instead of War — heavy armour, martial weapons and a bonus-action attack whose uses scale on Wisdom, which on a Charisma paladin means about three per long rest. Spirit Guardians arrives with Cleric 5 in Act III.
Evergreen.strength: Aura of Warding's spell-damage resistance plus Aura of Protection's Charisma to every save is two blanket effects reaching both bodies from one chassis, against a run whose boss save DCs climb every act.
Evergreen.wants: Skills and a boss-side control answer; this body rolls Perception and Investigation at effectively nothing.
uncertain: Zeal's bonus-action attack allowance is Wisdom-scaled and this body dumps Wisdom, so it is worth roughly one extra attack per fight — scored inside the actions rung, not as damage.

Bleak.split: Paladin 14 (Oath of the Bleak Walkers) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Bleak.note: Black Flames is a bonus-action Channel Oath adding 1d10 Fire and 1d10 Necrotic and applying Sickened, No Quarter is an area knockback-and-prone on the same clock, and Death's Maw grants flat damage reduction equal to proficiency bonus while standing near a corpse. It stops one level short of the level-15 Black Flames upgrade.
Bleak.strength: The level 7 aura's stacking crit-range reduction applies to both characters, and it compounds with a partner making many attacks under Lone Wolf's second Action — a party-wide multiplier from one body.
Bleak.wants: Area damage; No Quarter removes turns but the aoe row peaks at 1 and Listo's encounters add bodies.
uncertain: dur falls 4 → 3 in Act III because Death's Maw's reduction is flat proficiency bonus, which the rubric prices a rung below its raw numbers in a boss-weighted act.
Bleak Walkers removed its Oath Framework files in v1.2, so its oathbreaking behaviour is unverified; irrelevant to the axes but relevant to a run.

Blackflame.split: Paladin 14 (Oath of the Bleak Walkers) / Wizard 6 (Hierophant)
Blackflame.note: The same Bleak Walkers anchor with six Wizard levels bolted on for slots, scroll transcription and a Fireball. The Wizard half runs on Intelligence, which this body dumps, so every save-or-lose spell in that list is close to dead and only the save-for-half damage spells survive.
Blackflame.strength: Wizard scroll transcription turns Listo's abundant scroll drops into a permanent library on a body that already has the slots to cast them, and Black Flames plus No Quarter both run off Channel Oath's short-rest charge rather than the long-rest pool.
Blackflame.wants: A real caster; this body's Intelligence DC is far below par, so the partner has to own every save-or-lose effect the pair casts.
uncertain: The Hierophant subclass was outside my read set; I scored Wizard 6 as slots, scroll access and Fireball only, and credited nothing to the subclass. If Hierophant carries a real payload this chassis is undervalued.
Fireball off an Intelligence DC on a Charisma body: I used an effective save-fail of ~0.25 rather than 0.55, giving a 0.625 rather than 0.775 multiplier. Damage survives; control does not.

Regnant.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of Ginnungagap) / Paladin 11 (Oath of the Crown) / Cleric 6 (Order)
Regnant.note: A taunt anchor: Crown's Channel Oath forces attacks onto the body wearing Order's heavy armour, a Barbarian rage's physical resistance and Aura of Protection, while Voice of Authority hands the partner a free weapon attack every time this body buffs or heals them.
Regnant.strength: BG3 has no taunt, so the pair value on durability is its weaker body — Crown's Channel Oath is one of the few effects that actually redirects enemy attention, and Voice of Authority converts every outward heal into an extra attack from the other half of a two-body party.
Regnant.wants: Area damage and skills; the aoe row does not clear 2 and Perception and Investigation are unrolled.
uncertain: Voice of Authority gives the partner a free weapon attack, not an Action, so I scored the Act III actions rung at 4 rather than the rung-5 'an Action handed to the other body'.
Unyielding Saint is Oath of the Crown 15 and this split stops at Paladin 11; none of it is scored.

Coronet.split: Paladin 14 (Oath of the Crown) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Coronet.note: Crown's taunt-and-tank Channel Oath on a full Paladin 14 chassis — heavy armour, shield, Improved Divine Smite, Aura of Protection — with Bard 6 supplying the slot table, Expertise ×2 and Song of Rest. No area damage worth the name.
Coronet.strength: Forcing attacks onto the body carrying Aura of Protection and heavy armour is exactly the shape a Lone Wolf duo wants, because the model prices the pair's durability at its softer half and there is no other way to move that.
Coronet.wants: Crowd clearance; this chassis removes one enemy's attention at a time and never removes a crowd.
uncertain: Listo adds a Royal Decree cantrip to this oath whose mechanics the class file marks unverified; nothing above is scored off it.

Moonlight.split: Barbarian 3 (Path of Ginnungagap) / Paladin 11 (Oath of the Moon) / Monk 6 (Way of the Friar)
Moonlight.note: Three layers of damage reduction stacked on one body — rage's physical resistance, Aura of Moonlight's flat Charisma modifier off every hit, and Divine Guardian's halving — with Friar temp HP and Martial Arts feeding a bonus-action strike engine under Improved Divine Smite. It gives up heavy armour and every Paladin save proficiency.
Moonlight.strength: Divine Guardian is a short-rest Channel Oath that halves all damage on the *other* character for ten turns, and Friar's Blessing puts a d4 on both bonded bodies' saves — in a duo, losing either half ends the fight, so a targeted keep-my-partner-alive button is worth more than any damage rung.
Moonlight.wants: Any area answer at all — this body is 0 on area damage in every act and its area control is a single Channel Oath charge per fight.
uncertain: Divine Smite on Monk unarmed strikes is not assumed; the smite arithmetic rides the weapon attacks only, and the Flurry strikes are scored as plain Martial Arts damage.
Barbarian and Monk Unarmoured Defence do not stack — I took 10 + Dex + Con and scored the durability rung off the three reduction layers, not off AC.
Warding Bond is authored as redirect from Paladin 5 (Moon's own spell list is the only Paladin route to it), but the rubric caps redirection at rung 1 on rescue and nothing above scores it there.

Silver.split: Paladin 14 (Oath of the Moon) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Silver.note: The most duo-tuned oath on a full Paladin chassis: Aura of Moonlight reduces all incoming damage to both characters by the Charisma modifier and stacks with resistance, Divine Guardian halves it outright on the partner, and Fount of Moonlight at 13 puts +2d6 Radiant on every melee hit. That last one books the concentration slot.
Silver.strength: One body holding Aura of Protection, Aura of Moonlight and Warding Bond covers the entire party because the party is two, and Full Moon is a bonus-action 9m blind-and-slow on a short-rest charge that never touches either concentration slot.
Silver.wants: Area damage and a second concentration slot, because Fount of Moonlight occupies this one for the whole fight.
uncertain: st rises to 4 in Act III on Fount of Moonlight's +2d6 Radiant across four attacks a round (28 raw), which is the largest at-will rider in the Paladin half of this batch — but it is a concentration spell and the chassis is flagged accordingly.
Aura of Moonlight's radius under Listo's global aura patch is unverified for a v10.0-era subclass; scored at the mod's own 3m → 9m.

Radiance.verdict: Two pact-slot Charisma blasters whose core loops both run without concentration, so the pair's two slots stay free for whatever the fight actually asks for. Radiance owns rescue: Healing Light is a bonus-action heal that spends no slot, and with Lone Wolf's second bonus action it can fire twice in a turn that still contains two Actions, with Revivify sitting on a short-rest pact slot. Whisper owns removal: Mortal Reminder frightens off the crits of a six-to-eight beam Eldritch Blast routine, and Chains of Carceri adds Hold Monster on the same short-rest clock, so the control layer costs nothing either body was already spending.
Radiance.cost: Nobody stands in front. Both are light-armour ranged casters, and Whisper reads 0 on sustain until its Sorcerer tail arrives, which means every rescue in the first two acts is Radiance's alone and Radiance is the body being shot at. Force is the through-line of both damage packages against enemies carrying layered resistances, and Healing Light's pool refills only on a 120-supply long rest.

vars.note: trades the free fear for Voice of Authority handing Radiance a reaction attack every time Precept casts, plus a body that actually occupies melee range.
the only partner here that will be hit on purpose, with Divine Guardian halving damage on Radiance for ten turns off a short rest; the pair drops to zero area damage on Moonlight's half.
a second Celestial pool and Bladesong instead of the fear layer, which doubles the healing and leaves the duo with almost nothing that removes an enemy's turn.

Bargain.verdict: Bargain is the blaster built to survive being the target: Dark One's Blessing on every kill, Dark One's Own Luck at 6, Fiendish Resilience at 10, and Favored Soul's medium armour and shields under all of it. Its area answer is Fireball on a pact slot, which means the burst arrives in every fight instead of three times a day, and Chains of Carceri at Warlock 12 supplies a Hold Monster that touches neither concentration slot. Radiance covers the one axis Bargain reads 0 on for two full acts: outward healing, on a bonus action, with a short-rest Revivify behind it.
Bargain.cost: Two ranged Charisma casters is a duplicated face and a duplicated damage type; force is most of what both of them throw, and fire is the second type most likely to be resisted by the time Act III's layered defences show up. Neither body takes the front rank, so the pair's answer to a melee threat is that both of them are hard to kill rather than that either of them is a wall. Radiance's Healing Light pool is long-rest.

vars.note: swaps the second Charisma caster for lightning that ignores resistance outright, which is the cleanest answer to layered defences in the batch; the pair loses the bonus-action heal and the short-rest Revivify with it.
gives Bargain the front-rank body it wants and Divine Guardian's halving, but Moonlight is 0 on area damage in every act, so the pact Fireball becomes the pair's only crowd tool.

vars.text: Slot discipline: the pact Fireball and Chains of Carceri draw on the same two short-rest slots. Against +126% HP trash the Fireball is the clear; against a boss at +170% the same slot is the Hold Monster, and spending it on the approach fight is the usual way this pairing loses.

Beacon.verdict: Two Celestial warlocks, which buys two independent bonus-action heal pools and two Revivifies on short-rest slots — the deepest rescue layer any pairing in this batch reaches, on a run where losing either body ends the fight. Bladesong is the specific reason Beacon is the one holding concentration: +2 AC and +2 Constitution saves on a body in cloth is the cheapest concentration insurance available, and the two Wizard levels turn Listo's scroll drops into a permanent slot-castable library that a Warlock's spells-known list cannot hold.
Beacon.cost: This is the pairing that stacks a strength instead of covering a hole. Neither body removes an enemy's turn outside its pact slots, both are cloth, both spend radiant and force, and with only two bodies there is no third damage type to switch to when a resistance layer eats the first two. It is also the pairing where both halves want the same concentration spell and only one of them can hold it.

vars.note: trades the mirrored healing for lightning that ignores resistance and treats immunity as resistance, which is the exact gap this pairing leaves open in Act III.
a weapon, a real skill block and Cutting Words as concentration-free control opposite the healing; the pair gives up its second Revivify.
a front rank that halves damage on Beacon for ten turns off a short-rest Channel Oath, at the cost of every point of area damage on that half.

Spellblade.verdict: Spellblade runs the sword, the slots, Cutting Words and the pair's entire out-of-combat block off one Charisma score, because Scholar's Armament makes the blade a Charisma weapon and Lore spends the same stat on proficiencies and Expertise. It holds no concentration at all, and Whisper's fear comes off crits in the blast routine rather than off a spell, so both of the pair's two concentration slots are free for the whole campaign. Bardic Inspiration refills on a short rest and Whisper can spend it under Magical Inspiration, which turns a support die into damage.
Spellblade.cost: Sustain is the hole and it is a real one: Whisper reads 0 until its Sorcerer tail and Spellblade 1 in Act I, and neither body carries a revival before then. Reckless Attack hands enemies advantage against the melee half of a two-body party with nothing but flat DR 2 and Lone Wolf's halving behind it, and Barbarian 3 arrives last, so the mitigation shows up after the acts that need it. Both bodies are Charisma, so the face role is paid for twice.

vars.note: healing and a scroll library behind the sword, which fixes the sustain hole and the missing arcane utility in one body; the tradeoff is losing the concentration-free fear layer.
heavy armour, Hill Rune resistance and Cloud Rune's redirect on a short-rest clock instead of the blast routine, which also means the pair's ranged damage leaves with it.

vars.text: Cutting Words against inflated HP: subtracting a die from an enemy's attack is worth more here than the damage it displaces, because +126% HP means fights are long and Spellblade's own body is the soft one; the inspiration die spent defensively is a die not spent on Magical Inspiration.

Precept.tag: order-domain flurry monk + hexblade curse blaster
Precept.verdict: The attacks and the damage rider live on different bodies. Every time Precept casts, Voice of Authority hands Hexbind a reaction attack, and Lone Wolf's second bonus action doubles Flurry of Blows, so a single round puts four Precept strikes and a free Hexbind attack on the board without either character spending an Action on damage. Hexbind is the body that makes those extra swings expensive: Hexblade's Curse adds proficiency bonus to every damage roll against the cursed target, which on an eight-beam routine is worth tens of points a round rather than six, and it recharges on a short rest, so at three fights per long-rest cycle it runs at full uptime.
Precept.cost: Neither half can absorb a focused turn. Precept gives up the heavy armour Order grants because Martial Arts and Flurry require going without it, and has no redirection to move damage anywhere; Hexbind is a light-armour caster standing in melee range whenever it binds a weapon, reading 0 on sustain in Act I and 2 thereafter. All of the pair's healing is Precept's, and the pair's area damage is thin in every act.

vars.note: swaps the curse for a bonus-action heal pool and a short-rest Revivify, so Precept is no longer the only rescue; the free reaction attacks then land as cantrip damage instead of as a proficiency-bonus rider.

vars.text: Where the curse goes: the curse is the pair's largest single damage decision, so it belongs on the +170%-HP body rather than on whatever is nearest. Master of Hexes at 14 spreads it on a kill, which makes opening it on a trash target and walking it onto the boss a real line rather than a waste.

Two concentration slots, both spare: nothing in this pairing's damage loop holds concentration, so both slots can go to buffs or a lock. That is the actual argument for it over the Charisma-caster duos, which spend at least one slot to reach the same output.

Stormcalling.verdict: Stormcalling exists to solve the problem that a two-body party cannot carry a spare damage type: at Circle level 10 its lightning ignores Resistance and treats Immunity as Resistance, which is the only clean answer in the batch to Absolute Wrath's layered defences. Storm Shift adds Wisdom to every lightning roll and returns 3x Druid level in temp HP for one Wild Shape charge, and Call Lightning is retriggered every round off a single slot. Beacon takes the other concentration slot and everything Stormcalling is not: the bonus-action heal pool, Revivify on a short-rest slot, and Bladesong keeping that concentration up in cloth.
Stormcalling.cost: A boss with +170% HP takes all of its turns against this pair. Stormcalling's single-target control sits at 1 in all three acts and Beacon has almost nothing that removes a turn outside its pact slots, so the duo's plan against a hard target is to out-damage it. Both are ranged with no front rank, and Chain Lightning at 14 is a per-long-rest button against 120-supply rests.

vars.note: identical score, opposite tradeoff: Mortal Reminder's fear supplies the single-target answer the pairing lacks, but the pair's rescue drops to druid slots on a long-rest clock until Whisper's Sorcerer tail.
medium armour, shields and Fiendish Resilience on the other half plus a pact Fireball, which adds a second area engine to a pair that was already short a control layer rather than short a clear.

vars.text: Count one free slot, not two: Call Lightning owns Stormcalling's concentration from the moment it comes online, so the partner's spell is the pair's only remaining concentration decision. Pick it as the answer to the boss, not as a second buff.

Moonlight.verdict: Moonlight is the front rank, and unusually it is a front rank that protects the other body: Divine Guardian is a short-rest Channel Oath that halves all damage on Beacon for ten turns, and Friar's Blessing puts a d4 on every save either character rolls. Its own stack is rage's physical resistance, Aura of Moonlight subtracting Charisma from every hit, and Divine Guardian's halving, all sitting on top of Lone Wolf's own halved damage. Beacon does the entire ranged job behind it: the area damage Moonlight reads 0 on in all three acts, the healing, and the pair's concentration behind Bladesong.
Moonlight.cost: The whole crowd answer sits on one cloth body. Moonlight is 0 on area damage in every act and its area control is a single Channel Oath charge per fight, so if Beacon is the one that gets focused down the pair has no clear at all. Neither half has a real single-target lock, and Moonlight gives up heavy armour and every Paladin save proficiency to run the Friar frame.

vars.note: same score, storm-bard tail instead of the Bladesinger: lightning arrives as a third damage type, and Bladesong's concentration insurance leaves.
